0.content:
Aether and Lumine's Spaceship (also: the twins' spaceship, the Traveler's spaceship, Traveler's spaceship): The twins' spaceship is the vessel in which the Traveler and their sibling crossed the sea of stars before ever reaching Teyvat. It is a star-shaped craft of white and gold with a blue cockpit dome, made of a material nothing in Teyvat could scratch. It once lay overgrown at Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai; after the Cataclysm the Heavenly Principles removed it and hid it on the Frost Moon, where Columbina brought the Traveler to find it (Welkin Moon's Homecoming, 6.3).

The ship holds the Traveler's flight logs, a cabinet of old outfits, and a hibernation chamber that opens only with each twin's own key. It sits at the heart of Traveler's Crater and has been freely visitable since the Moon Gazing quests (6.7).

Appearance: Shaped like a four-pointed star, with the front and rear points each split into two sharp prongs. The hull is mostly white with gold lines and a blue cockpit dome in the middle. Its look echoes Celestial architecture, in particular the Nails and Teleport Waypoints. The hull is described as impervious: when the ship lay in Nod-Krai, generations of locals tried to strip it for parts and could not dent it.

While it lay at Starsand Shoal it became overgrown with plants. In the Frost Moon's low gravity it rests inside a vast crater, with Teyvat shining overhead.

Function: Built for interstellar travel, it carries a genetic vault and a hibernation chamber reachable only with the two special keys, one belonging to each twin. A navigational AI-like guide handled maintenance, course and destinations while the twins slept. As a pioneer vessel it could terraform a planet: reshape its lithosphere, atmosphere and biosphere so a civilisation could take root. It also made protective outfits for the sleeping twins; the Traveler's As Heaven and Earth Are Made Anew outfit is one of them, found in a cabinet aboard.

By the time the twins reached Teyvat they no longer had a clear memory of the guiding presence aboard. Item text (Wings of Descension) and the outfit description both mention a long journey, protective clothing and a speaker warning of danger, and the wiki reads them as the same entity; the games do not confirm this.

History: After the twins' home world was destroyed, they set out in the ship to look for a world with the potential to survive and rebuild civilisation, surveying countless planets across thousands of years. Along the way they received a goodwill signal sent from Teyvat by the dragons' Project Moongazer and replied that they would visit once their present affairs were settled. The flight log shows the ship passed Teyvat once, long before, without landing; the Traveler guesses the sibling may have left then. Aeons later Teyvat's gravity captured it, and it fell to Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai.

The fall was observed in Khaenri'ah by the Universitas Magistrorum, who reported predicted orbit and re-entry to King Irmin (per the Orbits namecard). The Traveler remembers feeling kuuvahki for the first time as they entered Teyvat. During the Cataclysm, five hundred years ago, the sibling appeared outside the ship and woke the Traveler; they tried to flee together but were beaten and separated by Asmoday. The Heavenly Principles then took the ship from Nod-Krai and hid it on the Frost Moon, then outside the false sky.

Places: The ship stands in Traveler's Crater on the Frost Moon, in the Lunar Highlands. The High-Speed Transit Lane at the Nuur Stone Circle leads there, and the viewpoint at the crater is named The Next Journey.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ship is on the Frost Moon and the Traveler knows where it is. In Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3) Columbina took the Traveler there; they read the flight logs, took a spare outfit from the cabinet, and left the ship in place. Since the Moon Gazing quests (6.7) it is permanently accessible. Why the Heavenly Principles hid it remains unexplained.

1.comment: Aether and Lumine's Spaceship: The Traveler's Hibernation Keys
1.content: The ship's hibernation chamber opens only with two special keys, one for each twin. The keys later matter in Natlan, where the sibling's choice of whether to seek the Traveler is tied to a key given to Direidyth; see the main entry for the wiki's reading and its player-choice variant.

2.comment: Aether and Lumine's Spaceship: Starsand Shoal Landing
2.content: The ship fell to Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai long before the Cataclysm and stayed there long enough to be overgrown and to be seen by several generations of locals, none of whom could damage it. The Traveler first sensed kuuvahki as they entered Teyvat and, during Song of the Welkin Moon, glimpsed the landing again through the Eternal Moon's Marrow.

3.content:
Afterglow Cavern: Afterglow Cavern is a mountain cave in Wavechaser Plain, Nod-Krai, southeast of Favonius Keep. It was once a tunnel leading north, but it collapsed after a kuuvahki-related anomaly. Travellers know it mostly as the den of a large moonlight-loving gecko.

At first the cave was split in two separate parts: a southern cave reached near a waterfall north of Dreadshade Mire, and a northern cave reached near the Teleport Waypoint just east of Favonius Keep.

Geography: A rocky cave in the hills of Wavechaser Plain. The southern entrance lies by a waterfall north of Dreadshade Mire; the northern one is by the waypoint directly east of Favonius Keep. The collapse cut the old northward tunnel, which is why the cave was at first two separate halves.

Intricate Bloom plants grow in the cave and can be used to reconnect the blocked path deeper in; slothsheep, creatures that live only where kuuvahki is present, wander in the area.

People: No residents. A guide named Vacarao is met at the northern entrance, near a locked chest, and later by the nearby waypoint; he is a local who cannot use Frostmoon Scion magic and lacks kuuvahki devices strong enough to clear the blockage.

An overseas traveling merchant had befriended a slothsheep that wandered into the cave and became trapped by the collapse, and insisted on rescuing it. Vacarao later reported that when the merchant tried to take the slothsheep out of Nod-Krai it turned into a lifeless seed, since slothsheep cannot live outside kuuvahki regions.

Dangers: The collapsed tunnel and unstable kuuvahki around it. Vacarao warns that kuuvahki anomalies have been frequent in the area and urges care.

The cave is the arena of the Radiant Moongecko, an ancient territorial gecko drawn to moonlight. In-game texts say it lives deep in the rock, that kuuvahki has crystallised its body into segments as precise as machine parts, and that on full-moon nights it gnaws on lunar-suffused rock and soil to preserve its bloodline. Some scholars think its ancestors once lived on the surface and were driven underground by sweeping changes in the world.

Quests: Slothsheep in Need (hidden exploration objective, 6.3): talk to Vacarao, solve two Intricate Bloom puzzles, and guide the trapped slothsheep across a bridge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the northern tunnel remains collapsed and the cave is the Radiant Moongecko's lair.

4.content: The Radiant Moongecko is a normal boss that dwells in Afterglow Cavern. Official descriptions call it an ancient monster drawn to moonlight that lives deep in the rock; the Archive says kuuvahki has crystallised its body into mechanical-looking segments that harden into stone spikes against intruders. Its fiercely territorial nature is explained in-game by the scarcity of moonlight that reaches the rock walls.

5.content:
Aino's House (also: Ainos House, Aino and Ineffa's home): Aino's House is the home of the child inventor Aino and her robot Ineffa, set inside the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. It is an eclectic, colorful building made of scrap metal and creativity.

The in-game map describes it as the place where parts, gears and half-finished contraptions fill the space and the "Whiz-Kid Mechanic's wild ideas take root". Each odd invention sparkles with inspiration, so that an ordinary dwelling becomes a private gallery of marvels and mess.

Places: The house is an instance entered from the craftshop. The wiki shows Aino's bedroom as one interior location; her bedroom holds a cabinet, and her character story says she keeps the first robot she ever built there.

That robot has no intelligence module, only jingles when shaken, and was meant purely as company for a girl who had said too many goodbyes. It is now rusted and falling apart, but Aino keeps it as family, and Ineffa learned its history while helping to tidy the workshop.

People: Aino, a young orphan prodigy, treats her creations and screws as family, and Ineffa is her robot helper. Visitors are not guaranteed a welcome: the craftshop's door is said to slam in the face of people who do not appreciate Aino's inventions.

Atmosphere: Messy, warm and busy, with the scent of machine oil, metal and krumkakes drifting through the craftshop. Half-built gadgets sit on every surface and nothing is quite finished, which suits the place.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is simply Aino and Ineffa's home; the wiki records no change.

6.content: In Aino's character story, Ineffa helps Aino carry her very first self-assembled robot to a cabinet in her bedroom. The old machine has rusted, lost its last screw and cannot be repaired, but it is kept for companionship. This is a lore detail from the character story, not a quest.

7.content:
Amsvartnir (also: Lake Amsvartnir): Amsvartnir is a lake in Wavechaser Plain, in northern Nod-Krai, lying north of the city of Piramida. A sacred forest grows beside it, beyond the ruins of an ancient palace and on the edge of the wasteland. Above the water, hidden from mortal eyes by day, stands the Royal Court of the Seelie, where Koitar, the first of the Seelie, was once confined.

Visitors uncover the court by melting a Lunar Conflux Barrier and playing a silent lyre, which begins the World Quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song. The name is borrowed from Norse mythology, where Ámsvartnir ("pitch black") is the lake holding the island on which the wolf Fenrir was bound.

Geography: A lake with a central island and floating islands overhead, surrounded by a sacred forest. Lakeside Prisms and Lunar Conflux Barriers are part of the exploration puzzles. Local life includes Pale-Furred Wolves and Radiant Glacial Wolf elites, and Winter Icelea grows here.

The lake lies in Wavechaser Plain, itself part of Pohjola. The restored court has aqua-green crystals at its base and on the islands above, and aqua-blue beams that form geometric patterns around the structure, connecting the central island to those overhead.

Places: The Royal Court of the Seelie lies above the lake: a sacred secluded domain that cannot be perceived by ordinary people. It holds a giant lyre. A viewpoint here is called Palaces of Times Bygone.

Ancient Handwriting notes are found in chests after the quest. Moonlanes carry the Traveler up through the floating islands, and the lake's central island and the airborne islands are linked once the prisms are reconnected.

History: The Etherlight Spindlelute's legend says the lake lies beyond the ruins of an ancient palace and that whoever breaks the golden branch in the sacred forest will find the Royal Court, hidden from mortal sight by day. It calls the court a kingdom of the past, forgotten by time and space, where no heavenly light reaches, whose owner has long gone. A young woman's silent lament still echoes in its hall.

The quest's mural and the legend speak of a woman who dreamed of a different future than the one the Heavenly Principles had woven: a tower raised to heaven by men, mountain-sized beasts breaking from the earth, three moons, and an ancient dragon. Tradition names her as Koitar, the first Seelie and wife of Anacharsis, confined in the court after losing her memories.

Atmosphere: Hushed, silvery and mournful: a lake with Seelie circling above, a silent instrument whose music only the player hears, and a song of exiles in a hall stripped bare. The Traveler hears the lament in a language they have never studied yet understand.

Dangers: Wolves, including the Radiant Glacial Wolf, roam the shore. The court itself is not hostile; its challenges are puzzles of light and prisms.

Travel: Lies in Wavechaser Plain, north of Piramida. The court appears after the Lunar Conflux Barrier is melted and the lyre played, and completing the quest unlocks a Teleport Waypoint at the court.

Quests: World Quest: Echoes of a Forsaken Song (6.3). Follow the Seelie up the Moonlanes, break seals on the floating islands and reconnect Lakeside Prisms to hear fragments of a lament, then examine the mural. The quest unlocks the Palaces of Times Bygone viewpoint.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Royal Court stands restored and open to visitors, and the Seelie gather there.

Koitar herself does not appear in the court in this quest, only her recorded words and song.

8.comment: Amsvartnir: Royal Court of the Seelie
8.content: A sacred, secluded domain above Amsvartnir, hidden from mortals by day. It was built of mighty stone pillars with golden beams and no windows for outside light. Koitar wept there day and night amid Seelie who no longer knew her. Boreas and his kin dwelt in the area before leaving for Mondstadt. The Traveler broke the barrier, revealed a giant lyre and helped the Seelie rebuild the temple.

9.content: Three notes recovered from chests by the court, written in the first person by a woman confined in a lonely temple. They tell of a beast named Boreas ("North Wind") who served as her emissary and then left to bring prosperity to the south, and end as she starts to remember. They tie the lake's legend to Mondstadt's wind god tradition.

10.content:
Archaeolune Storm Research Center (also: Land of Raging Storms): The Archaeolune Storm Research Center is an ancient dragon facility on the Frost Moon whose job was to watch Archaeolune storms, surges of moon energy that sweep the surface. Today it lies in an Archaeolune Energy disturbance zone, and a terminal there holds a researcher's anxious notes about where the storms came from.

Its map viewpoint is called Land of Raging Storms. It has an upper and a lower level.

Geography: A multi-level dragon complex set among Archaeolune Energy barriers and Storm Occlusion Fields, patches of shelter where a traveller can rest from the storm. It uses Ancient Moon Pearls, Edict Modules, terminals and a High-Speed Transit Lane.

The disturbance zone around it fills a gauge on anyone caught outside shelter; once full, the traveller is carried back to the last safe place without harm. Elsewhere on the moon, storms and the lunar sea work the same way.

Dangers: Archaeolune storms and disturbance zones; Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network guardians; and puzzle barriers that must be broken with the traveller's own absorbed Archaeolune Energy.

History: The record on its terminal shows dragon researchers troubled by a disturbance in Archaeolune Energy that grew faster over time and could become a storm, a phenomenon not seen when they first arrived on the moon. Someone named Kalag insisted the cause was blackbody contamination from Ungien's Circle, brought by the mysterious visitor Ungien had returned with from space. The author dismissed this as political: it would let Kalag remove Maagees's people from the biosphere, and Kalag could not be acting without backing, since King Xiuhcoatl favoured Ungien and Maagees.

The author's priority was finishing an inhibitory field device quickly so it would not delay every other project. As a half-doubted guess, they wondered whether the disturbance could come from the Moon Maiden at the Lunar Palace, since the palace sits above the Moonheart like a spring above its source, and noted that one of Maagees's students had been visiting the palace often. They could not imagine why anyone would do that, or how the Moon Maiden could agree.

People: Named in the record: Kalag, who wants Maagees's people out of the biosphere according to the author; Maagees, a life scientist and Ungien's partner; Ungien, who had returned with a mysterious visitor; King Xiuhcoatl; the Moon Maiden at the Lunar Palace; and one of Maagees's students, taken to be Lusalim. The author is not identified.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the center is derelict, still dangerous, and open to exploration.

11.comment: Archaeolune Storm Research Center: Archaeolune Storm
11.content: A storm of Archaeolune Energy, the moon energy that is very similar to kuuvahki. Gravity, safety and travel on the Frost Moon are shaped by it. Dragon researchers recorded a rising disturbance that could produce such storms and built field devices to calm it; their record says the cause was never settled.

12.content:
Ashveil Peak: Ashveil Peak is the northernmost area of Pohjola, the large island of northern Nod-Krai, added in 6.3. It is a harsh, cold highland of cliffs under dark clouds. Its two subareas are Kipumaki Cliff, a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity where an undying Abyssal fiend was sealed long ago, and Cliffwatch Camp, the Lightkeepers' outpost that stands guard over it.

It is a place of vigilance and grief rather than settlement: the Lightkeepers keep a small camp with a graveyard of their own dead, and the Traveler's world quests here centre on repairing the ancient seal and fighting the Abyssal threat beneath it.

Geography: Ashveil Peak is part of Pohjola and lies at its far north, beyond Wavechaser Plain and Voidsea Outlook. Kipumaki Cliff is a ring of jagged cliffs permanently under dark cloud; Cliffwatch Camp sits beside a lighthouse and a vehicle that marks its Meeting Point. The chasm of Endless Decay, the lair of the sealed fiend, lies within the area.

The whole of Kipumaki Cliff carries a special climate: Abyssal Decay builds up on travelers, and once the gauge is full the active character loses HP over time. Oath Lanterns scattered through the area let a visitor reduce or avoid it. Abyssal Riftlines and Abyssal Fog Barriers are exploration puzzles here. Local specialty: Winter Icelea.

Places: Kipumaki Cliff: a cliff perpetually shrouded in dark clouds, said by its loading screen to contain a sealed and undying fiend. Cliffwatch Camp: the Lightkeepers' investigation squad's long-standing sentinel post against threats from the north.

Cliffwatch Camp has a cemetery south of the camp with graves of fallen Lightkeepers, among them Veyde, Olsson, Chernov, Filaev, Pieris Asebov and Shonokovych; Bjorn's grave appears after the quest The Last Night, the First Light. Each grave carries only a short inscription. A diary found elsewhere says the cliff is often called the Sanctum of Departed Heroes, the resting ground of soldiers who fell in battle (see uncertainties). Chasm of Endless Decay is the lair where the fiend is finally confronted.

People: Lightkeepers (Ratniki) man the camp. After the world quests The Moonlit Watcher and Nightingale's Song, several Lightkeepers from those quests stand as open-world NPCs at Cliffwatch Camp: Anleifr, Egle, Rollon, Valdis and Vlaicu.

Illuga, a Lightkeeper and later a playable character, leads the Nightmare Orioles squad in When War Songs Rise. The Lightkeepers' leader, the Starshyna Nikita, directs the effort from Piramida, and the Traveler is invited to join their strategy meeting at the camp.

Governance: No civil government. The area falls under the Lightkeepers, the autonomous order that Solovei founded 500 years ago by royal edict to defend Nod-Krai against the Wild Hunt. Orders reach the camp from their headquarters in Piramida; the order is described elsewhere as thinly stretched, so small squads like the one at Cliffwatch often carry heavy duties.

History: Five hundred years ago, at the time of the Cataclysm, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, Aila, and the Torchforger Solovei, with Alia's help, subdued the Scourge of Endless Decay and sealed it with a sealing array under Kipumaki Cliff. The Scourge had been helping the mad scholar Rotwang (Rauthvangi) try to open the false sky to the Abyss through the Pillar of Embla. Since the sealing the area has been a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity, so the Lightkeepers built Cliffwatch Camp to watch it.

Three years before the present, a surge of Wild Hunt activity here caused a great catastrophe with many deaths among the Lightkeepers and civilians; the camp was afterwards rebuilt and the fight continued. Written accounts left by Lightkeeper squads describe being sent from Piramida to clear Wild Hunt nests around the cliff in support roles.

Atmosphere: Thin cold air, low dark cloud that never quite clears, jagged stone, the steady light of the camp lighthouse and rows of simple grave markers. Mood: wary, solemn, with dry gallows humour among tired soldiers.

Dangers: Wild Hunt and Abyssal enemies: Wilderness Exiles, Wilderness Hunters, Fishers of Hidden Depths and, as a boss, the Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares (the Scourge in its true form). The Abyssal Decay climate drains health in the open.

The Scourge first appears in the form of a Wilderness Hunter, then in boss form. It does not simply attack: it draws on the sorrow of those it faces. Allied Lightkeepers fight alongside the Traveler during the quest.

Travel: Reached by moving north through Wavechaser Plain and Pohjola. Cliffwatch Camp has its own Meeting Point; lanterns and Teleport Waypoints in the cliffs let travelers rest from Abyssal Decay.

Quests: When War Songs Rise (world quest, Nightingale's Song chapter, Act II; 6.3): starting at Cliffwatch Camp, the Traveler joins Illuga and the Lightkeepers' Nightmare Orioles squad to reestablish the ancient seal on the cliff.

The sequence runs Tower of Inversion (Pillar of Embla), When War Songs Rise, then The Last Night, the First Light. In the middle quest the Traveler and the squad rebuild the barrier by activating Verdant Crests, destroy the Evil Eye hanging above the cliff, and Bjorn is fatally wounded by the Scourge. Illuga pursues the fiend into its lair; it conjures illusions from his past losses to break his will, but with his squad's help he and the Traveler defeat it with the Spiralblade and cleanse the area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cliff is open to explore; the sealed fiend has been defeated and its influence cleansed, but the Wild Hunt remains a danger in the north.

Cliffwatch Camp continues as a Lightkeeper outpost. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the area.

13.content:
Kipumaki Cliff is a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity in northern Nod-Krai, perpetually shrouded in dark clouds. The Scourge of Endless Decay was sealed here 500 years ago after Aila, Alia and Solovei first banished it. The name echoes a Finnish myth place, the hill of pain.

All the cliff is under the Abyssal Decay climate. A puzzle near a waterfall in the south ends in a carriage opened with a forgotten key.

14.content:
Cliffwatch Camp is an outpost of the Lightkeepers that keeps watch on Abyssal activity at Kipumaki Cliff. It was built by their investigation squad and serves as a long-standing sentinel against threats from the north; it was rebuilt after the surge three years before the present.

Its graves record the dead of earlier squads. Some of the Lightkeepers who appear in The Moonlit Watcher and Nightingale's Song stay on as open-world NPCs.

15.comment: Ashveil Peak: The Scourge of Endless Decay
15.content: An Abyssal entity that helped Rotwang's plan to open the false sky to the Abyss through the Pillar of Embla. After Rotwang's defeat it was sealed beneath Kipumaki Cliff by Aila and Solovei. In When War Songs Rise it is the antagonist, first as a Wilderness Hunter, later as the Lord of the Hidden Depths. It exploits Illuga's experience of loss, and is defeated by the Traveler and Illuga. The wiki notes it may once have been human; canon does not say.

16.content:
Barrowmoss Barrens: Barrowmoss Barrens is a subarea of Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai: two plateaus lying north and south of Blue Amber Lake. It is a wild, open stretch where researchers and treasure hunters carry out odd projects, and where a Radiant Moonfly roams as a boss.

The Barrens are better known for the people working in them than for any history of their own. Canon gives the place no founding story or ruler; what it offers is a handful of quests about kuuvahki research and an engineer's hidden laboratory.

Geography: The name covers both the northern and southern plateau, with raised Blue Amber Lake between them. The map shows three levels: the Hidden Laboratory, the Windworn Path and the Pellucid Cavern. Thunderstorms occur in the northern part.

Blue Amber Lake itself has its own entry; it is described as a highland lake with a glow at every hour, and the only place where Stellafruit grows. A Radiant Moonfly, one of the Radiant Beasts (a Mystical Beast family), is the area's boss.

People: No settled population is recorded. Visitors seen here are the Fontaine Research Institute researcher Fanngel, the treasure hunters Anezka and Macola, and, in a Travelers' Tale, the Ratnik Flins and the automaton Ineffa.

Anezka and Macola look after a laboratory belonging to their friend Drzislav, who is absent. Aino and Ineffa are linked to Lempo Isle as a whole rather than to the Barrens specifically.

Quests: Three quests start here: The Power of Research (Fanngel needs his Airspace Data Collector lifted in a storm to gather kuuvahki data), Team Rigor, or Team Intuition? (Anezka and Macola recover Drzislav's all-terrain machine Bobik from Fatui troopers) and the Travelers' Tale Flins: Out of One's Depth.

In The Power of Research, Fanngel hopes kuuvahki studies will free people from reliance on Arkhium, and gives the Traveler a lightning-proof Collector 2.0 that works only in kuuvahki storms. In Team Rigor, or Team Intuition?, Bobik is hijacked, the group enters the lab, and the machine is restored from a backup module; Anezka and Macola stay to guard the lab afterwards. In Flins' anecdote, Flins and Ineffa talk about the Ratniki, who once lit street lights by oil and now struggle with kuuvahki-powered ones.

Dangers: The Radiant Moonfly alternates between Dendro and Pyro states and can envelop players in a Radiant Cocoon. Fatui Oprichniki troopers appeared around the laboratory during Team Rigor, or Team Intuition?. Lightning storms are dangerous without protection.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Barrens remain an open, explorable area of Nod-Krai with nothing new revealed after the 6.x quests.

17.comment: Barrowmoss Barrens: Drzislav's Laboratory and Bobik
17.content: Drzislav is an absent inventor whose hidden laboratory sits in the Barrens, guarded by his friends Anezka and Macola. His creation Bobik-131 is a civilian all-terrain transportation device; after Fatui interference the Traveler helps restore it from a backup program module, and it afterwards follows the Traveler's orders. Drzislav appears only through recorded voice messages.

18.content: Fanngel is a Fontaine Research Institute researcher doing field work on kuuvahki storms in the northern Barrens. He expects his thesis in a year or two and says the real impact of the work may take decades. His reward, the Nod-Krai Airspace Data Collector 2.0, protects only against kuuvahki thunderstorms.

19.content:
Big Bad Battle Base: The Big Bad Battle Base is an encampment on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai that the young inventor Aino set up to run the Clink Clank Clash, a limited-time event of version 6.0. It was the working base for a string of odd jobs: testing a self-defence gadget, chasing runaway recon robots and tracking down lost experimental machines. Thin canon: the wiki gives little more than its map description and a list of three clients.

The wiki lists three people tied to the base: Sarin of the Adventurers' Guild, the Fontainian engineer Ginette, and Gaudenty, who describes himself as a representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. Each commissioned Aino, and the Traveler and Paimon helped carry out the orders.

Geography: On Lempo Isle, in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai, filed by the wiki under the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop subarea. The map description calls it an encampment Aino created for the purposes of conducting the Clink Clank Clash. The event quests all start at the nearby Northern Training Ground, but no source states that the two places are the same.

Lempo Isle is also home to Nasha Town and the Krumkake Craftshop, Aino's workshop, which grew from a tiny workspace into a renowned machine shop. The surrounding country is kuuvahki-rich, which matters because several of the event's problems come from machines built elsewhere failing to cope with it.

People: Aino runs the show; Ineffa, her creation, is caught up in the crisis alongside her. Clients: Sarin (Branch Master of the Adventurers' Guild in Nod-Krai) wanted a self-defence device any adventurer could carry; Gaudenty wanted stray recon bots retrieved or destroyed; Ginette wanted help debugging and then finding robots that communicate over distance using kuuvahki.

Sarin admits his own design failed and that he lacks the talent to fix it. Aino remarks that the design uses technology from elsewhere and cannot adapt to kuuvahki-rich surroundings. Gaudenty is brusque and forgets nothing about his terms: payment is in recon-bot components rather than Mora, and he says he does not take retractions. Ginette, embarrassed, adds a second request after losing several test robots while trying different kuuvahki concentrations.

History: Created for the Clink Clank Clash, a Flagship Event of version 6.0 (Luna I) that ran from 2025-09-12 to 2025-09-29 by the wiki's dating.

The event's four gameplay modes were: chasing and shooting down rogue recon bots along Moonlanes with the help of kuuhenki; a self-defence-device combat test across Nod-Krai; a search for malfunctioning robots using kuuvahki remnants; and a stealth mission with the robot Zip-zap Spy-bot Number 1. Progress was measured in Legion Morale.

Atmosphere: A workshop-on-location feel: gadgets, prototypes and clients with half-finished problems. Aino is cheerful and brisk with them, and in the quests she has to ask more than once which order belongs to whom.

Quests: Three event quests supplied the work. An Adventurer's Woes (Sarin) unlocked Boom! Blast! Power Test!, a combat trial of the self-defence device; A Mysterious Outsourced Contract (Gaudenty) unlocked the recon-bot chase; Misplaced Creativity (Ginette) unlocked the search for her lost robots, which continues through The Last Step of Testing.

In Boom! Blast! Power Test!, the Traveler moves between challenge areas defeating waves of enemies while a self-defence device, charged by kuuvahki energy, emits shockwaves. Its routes were named Villain's Row, Elemental Storm and Heavy Metal. The event's weapon reward was the Etherlight Spindlelute, a Catalyst.

Status as of 7.1: The event is over. Nothing after 7.1 is recorded here, and the pages read do not say whether the base remains visitable.

20.comment: Big Bad Battle Base: Clink Clank Clash
20.content:
The Clink Clank Clash was a version 6.0 Flagship Event set in Nod-Krai in which the Traveler and Paimon help Aino and Ineffa with a run of commissions: a self-defence gadget for the Adventurers' Guild, runaway recon robots for a Design Bureau representative, and a Fontainian engineer's lost kuuvahki robots. The Big Bad Battle Base is the encampment Aino set up for it.

It ran 2025-09-12 to 2025-09-29 per the wiki. Requirements were Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III Archon Quest, with Song of the Welkin Moon Act II recommended for the best experience.

21.content: Aino is the child-prodigy inventor who founded the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop and built Ineffa. She treats her creations as family. She accepted the three commissions behind the Clink Clank Clash and asked for no extra pay for Ginette's order because it sounded fun. Her own character entry holds the full detail.

22.content:
Blue Amber Lake: Blue Amber Lake is a highland lake on a raised plateau of Lempo Isle in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai, between the north and south sections of Barrowmoss Barrens. Its unusual climate gives it an ethereal glow at every hour of the day, and it is the only place where Stellafruit grows. Travellers rest at its shoreside bonfires, and the inventor known as Papa Wrench once built a workshop beneath it.

The in-game expedition description calls it a highland lake of crystalline blue that cradles the sky's reflection, a place of tranquility amid the world's clamour when the stars come out. It is the setting of the World Quest The Tale-Telling Heart.

Geography: A lake on a plateau sitting between the two Barrowmoss Barrens plateaus on Lempo Isle. Rippleweeds beside the water, flytrap-like plants opened by throwing Kuuvahki Dewdrops, contain the Stellafruit that grows nowhere else. A teleport waypoint stands on its western side.

Portable Bearing is a local specialty. Barrowmoss Barrens around the lake hosts the Radiant Moonfly boss and contains the Hidden Laboratory, Windworn Path and Pellucid Cavern map levels.

Places: The shoreside campfire where the quest begins; the area near the western waypoint; and Papa Wrench's underground workshop, reached by a lift that needs missing parts recovered from Treasure Hoarders.

Papa Wrench's Messily-Scribbled Notes lie around the lake; the later two are readable only during the quest. An Opened Secret Letter near the western waypoint is a note between two treasure-seekers, mentioning money to be made, possible competition and a debt to be repaid double.

People: Papa Wrench, a gentle mechanic who lived and later died here, is the lake's presiding memory. Tolfin, a storyteller who knew him, gathers people at the campfire. Aino, builder of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, was Papa Wrench's pupil. The other participants in the quest are Danyusha and Zhorik Shesternin of Novokitezhgrad, and Huginn, who guides the Traveler through the workshop.

In the quest, Danyusha is Papa Wrench's daughter and Zhorik is her husband. Tinet, a child of the caravan Papa Wrench travelled with, was too ill to travel further, so the caravan made camp here; he stayed behind to look after her and built the workshop's machines to make her happy.

History: Papa Wrench's original name was Mr. Shesternin Sr., of Snezhnaya. About ten years before the events of the game he sailed on the ship Fortunate One, disappeared and was presumed lost overboard. He survived but lost his memory, took the name Papa Wrench and travelled between Nod-Krai's islands with a caravan, then settled at Blue Amber Lake.

There he found an underground warehouse containing the Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask, one of the Proofs of the Cognoscenti, and turned it into a workshop. Tinet did not survive her illness, and he later died of chronic illness and grief. He left his workshop and belongings to Tolfin.

Atmosphere: Stillness lit from within: water the colour of blue amber, a faint glow on the plateau, bonfires at night and the sound of stories being told. Under the lake is an old workshop of gears, lifts and half-finished toys.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders, hilichurls, Blazing Axe Mitachurls and Hydro Slimes appear in and near the workshop during the quest, and the Radiant Moonfly boss lives in the surrounding Barrens.

Travel: On Lempo Isle. A teleport waypoint stands on its west side, and the campfire is the quest start.

Quests: World Quest: The Tale-Telling Heart, part of the East of the Moon, West of the Sun chapter. Tolfin's campfire storytelling becomes a treasure hunt for a Proof of the Cognoscenti, guided by Huginn, and ends with Zhorik confronted by a picture and Tolfin's account.

The quest has the Traveler collect Stellafruit for a game of 'Colonel Iron Whale' and 'Sergeant Octopus', repair the lift, explore the workshop and stop a runaway machine, then ride the 'Aurora' in search of the treasure. Zhorik takes a flashy goblet to be the Proof; the real Proof is a mask he cast aside, which goes to the Traveler. Finishing unlocks the Iron Whale's Dream viewpoint and the achievement When the Aurora Shines.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lake is a peaceful stop on Lempo Isle, and Papa Wrench's workshop lies open under it.

Zhorik's fate after the quest is not shown.

23.comment: Blue Amber Lake: The Tale-Telling Heart
23.content: A World Quest at the lake campfire. Tolfin the storyteller and the Shesternins gather; he proposes a treasure-hunt tale about Papa Wrench's Proof of the Cognoscenti. The Traveler and Paimon collect Stellafruit, fix the lift, explore the workshop with Huginn and find the treasure; Zhorik flees after seeing a picture that implicates him in the Fortunate One incident.

24.content: Mr. Shesternin Sr. lost his memory after the Fortunate One incident, became the roaming mechanic Papa Wrench and later lived at Blue Amber Lake. He charged little for his repairs and sometimes none, told the caravan children endless stories and gave them candy. He built the workshop's machines for Tinet, and passed away from illness and grief afterwards.

25.comment: Blue Amber Lake: Stellafruit and Rippleweeds
25.content: Stellafruit is a star-shaped quest-item fruit that grows only here, found in Rippleweeds beside the lake. Rippleweeds open when Kuuvahki Dewdrops are thrown at them. The fruit seems to hold some mysterious power.

26.content:
Bubble Pool: The Bubble Pool is a lake subarea in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon, in Nod-Krai. It was added with the Frost Moon in version 6.7 (Luna VIII). Canon says almost nothing about it beyond its name and an in-game viewpoint titled "The Iridescent Lake".

Treat it as a quiet, water-filled stretch of the Frost Moon's highlands. Its in-game map label places it in the Frost Moon region alongside Ungien's Circle and the other highland subareas, and the wiki lists a handful of exploration quests tied to it.

Geography: The Bubble Pool sits within the Lunar Highlands subregion of the Frost Moon. The only descriptive handle canon provides is the viewpoint title "The Iridescent Lake", which suggests a shimmering body of water; no further physical description is established in the sources consulted.

The name is rendered in other languages as roughly "floating bubble lake" (Chinese) and "land of bubbles" (Japanese). The location is a subarea rather than a single point of interest, so it is a region to wander rather than one building or structure.

Atmosphere: Use a calm, luminous, slightly eerie lunar landscape: bubbles and a sheen on the water under the Frost Moon sky. Stay within these cues rather than inventing creatures, ruins or history for it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an explorable part of the Frost Moon with no revealed lore of its own.

27.content:
Chasm of Endless Decay (also: Dawn Over the Dark Chasm): The Chasm of Endless Decay is a cave beneath Kipumaki Cliff in Ashveil Peak, Nod-Krai. Five hundred years ago Solovei, the Torchforger, and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, imprisoned the Abyssal Scourge of Endless Decay here. In the quest When War Songs Rise, Illuga and his squad return to finish what they began.

Its viewpoint is named Dawn Over the Dark Chasm.

Geography: A cave under Kipumaki Cliff, in the Ashveil Peak area near Cliffwatch Camp. It is the point of interest the quest When War Songs Rise ends at, after the Lightkeepers reactivate the sealing mechanism above ground.

The sealing mechanism used a series of Verdant Crests around Kipumaki Cliff, which the Traveler and the Nightmare Orioles squad reactivate in follow-up quests (the Focal Point of Ancient Array trio).

History: After Rotwang's first defeat, the Scourge of Endless Decay, an Abyssal entity that had helped him open the false sky using the Pillar of Embla, was sealed beneath Kipumaki Cliff by a sealing array set by Aila and Solovei.

In When War Songs Rise the Scourge acts as the antagonist. It first appears in the form of a Wilderness Hunter and later as the Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares. The Traveler and Illuga's Nightmare Orioles squad work to reestablish the seal and defeat it. Bjorn is fatally wounded by it during the effort. After the seal is reactivated and the Evil Eye over Kipumaki Cliff destroyed, Illuga pursues it into the chasm.

Dangers: Before its defeat, Abyssal corruption, the Scourge's illusions of the past, and the Wild Hunt nests around Kipumaki Cliff. In its original form the Scourge resembles a much larger Evil Eye of Blightseep with a special core and large hands.

Quests: When War Songs Rise (Nightingale's Song, Darradarljod) starts at Cliffwatch Camp or at the chasm itself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Scourge of Endless Decay is dead and the chasm is cleansed.

28.comment: Chasm of Endless Decay: Scourge of Endless Decay
28.content: A quest-exclusive Abyssal entity allied with Rotwang. It said that its side had failed ten years ago and three years ago and vowed that this time it would not. It was imprisoned beneath Kipumaki Cliff and was killed by the Traveler and Illuga's squad with the Spiralblade.

29.content:
Cliffwatch Camp: Cliffwatch Camp is a Lightkeepers' outpost on Ashveil Peak in northern Nod-Krai, built by the Nightmare Orioles investigation squad to keep watch on the Abyssal activity at nearby Kipumaki Cliff. It has a lighthouse, a fortified perimeter, Moonwagons, a Statue of the New Moon at its entrance and a small cemetery to the south. It is a working post, busy and short of hands.

Illuga's squad runs it. His men are overworked, forever short of kuuvahki-refined fuel and supplies, and the camp feels like a place where people are trying very hard not to let the dark in.

Geography: The camp stands on Ashveil Peak in the cold north of Nod-Krai, near Kipumaki Cliff, a cliff perpetually shrouded in dark cloud. Nearby plants are rich in kuuvahki, which helps the camp's machines for a while but cannot replace the special refined oil needed for a lighthouse.

The Pillar of Embla lies in the same northern country. Supplies come in from Piramida on Moonwagons.

Places: The entrance with its Statue of the New Moon; a command post where reports and base data are kept; a Moonwagon parked near the lighthouse, which doubles as the meeting point; fortifications; and a cemetery just south of the camp.

The graves read simply 'Here lies Lightkeeper' followed by a name: Veyde, Olsson, Chernov, Filaev, Pieris Asebov, Shonokovych and, after the 6.3 victory, Bjorn. A final tomb, Patolichev's, is empty for now; its inscription is a mock epitaph, written as if a century from now, for the living Ratnik Patolichev, praising his service with the Frostgale Steeds.

People: Squad Leader Illuga is in charge. The camp's known members are Anleifr, Egle, Rollon, Valdis and Vlaicu, all of the Nightmare Orioles; after the world quests several of them become open-world NPCs there.

Rollon compiles data on the bases the Lightkeepers still hold. Vlaicu relays messages about clashes with the Fatui in the east. Valdis handles transport and likes to study insects and plants; he was trapped by mandragoras protecting him when he followed them off the road. Anleifr and Egle press Illuga about fuel.

Governance: Illuga reports to Starshyna Nikita in Piramida but shoulders the groundwork himself, so that Nikita is not worried by every detail. He is strict about orders but fair, and kept Valdis in a barrier until he had explained himself.

Illuga lets the Traveler and Paimon join the investigation squad as honorary members during the quest, and no longer treats them as outsiders.

Culture: Food and rest matter as much as battle. At Paimon's suggestion a food truck was set up at the camp; Illuga says filling stomachs is part of a Ratnik's work. The cemetery reflects the Lightkeepers' custom of honouring the dead; Illuga talks to Bjorn's grave and reports what has happened in the city.

History: Kipumaki Cliff became a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity after the Torchforger, Aila and Alia sealed the Scourge of Endless Decay beneath it about 500 years ago, and the Lightkeepers built the camp to watch it. Three years ago a surge of Wild Hunt activity there overran the Nightmare Orioles; only Illuga and a badly injured Ivar survived, and the camp was rebuilt afterwards.

In The Moonlit Watcher the camp is made into a permanent base, with fortifications and a lighthouse stocked with half a month of fuel, so that it can hold out in a major assault until reinforcements come. Later, in the 6.3 finale, the Lightkeepers launched the Arrow of Terpikeraunas from Piramida and destroyed the Scourge and its Cataclysm Egg.

Dangers: The Wild Hunt, which grows stronger around Kipumaki Cliff, and Abyssal Decay seeping from the cliff. Mandragoras in the area react to danger before humans do. In the east the Lightkeepers have clashed with Fatui.

Supply lines are the camp's weak point: a supply transport went missing in the quest, and a lighthouse needs a special oil refined with kuuvahki.

Travel: Moonwagons run between Piramida and the camp. It is the base for watching Kipumaki Cliff.

Quests: The Moonlit Watcher and The Moonlit Watcher (II), world quests in the Nightingale's Song series, centre on the camp. The first finds missing supplies and rescues Valdis, which unlocks the meeting point; the second has the Traveler visit Illuga's home in Piramida. Bjorn's grave becomes available after The Last Night, the First Light.

Atmosphere: Cold wind, the glow of the lighthouse on dark cloud, Ratniki at their posts and a smell of stew. Quiet moments are rare and treasured.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Cliffwatch Camp is a fortified, functioning Lightkeepers outpost; its original threat has been defeated.

The Scourge of Endless Decay was destroyed in 6.3, the Piramida bulletin board celebrates the Nightmare Orioles' victory, and Bjorn's grave has been added to the cemetery. Wild Hunt dangers continue in the north. No 7.0-7.1 content changes the camp.

30.content:
Moonwagons are Lightkeeper vehicles modified from Snezhnayan mechanical vehicles and powered by kuuvahki, described by Illuga as mobile lighthouses. Valdis, in charge of transport, was trapped by a ring of mandragoras after following them off the road to study them, delaying supplies for the camp's lighthouse. The Traveler helps rescue him, and the Wild Hunt monsters that the mandragoras had sensed attack.

Once the supplies arrive, Illuga finishes the camp: fortifications are complete, the lighthouse fuelled, and Illuga takes the Traveler to his home in Piramida.

31.comment: Cliffwatch Camp: Cemetery South of the Camp
31.content: Graves of fallen Lightkeepers lie south of the camp. After the victory at Piramida, Illuga and the Traveler visit Bjorn's grave. Illuga recounts the city's news to his comrade and says he would have been proud.

32.content:
Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop (also: Krumkake Craftshop, Clinky, Clanky Craftshop, Clink-Clank Krumkake Workshop): The Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop is a huge, rusty, scrap-metal workshop on the outskirts of Nasha Town, on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. Aino, a child prodigy, started it to build the world's best krumkake machine, and it became famous as a machine workshop through her many inventions. She lives there with her robot Ineffa, and the air smells of machine oil, metal and krumkakes.

The name is a pun on the sound of the place (clink, clank) and on krumkake, a Norwegian rolled cookie of flour, butter, eggs, sugar and cream. Locals know the building as a place where odd contraptions are born, from flower-shooting guns to floor sweepers that behave like puppies, according to Aino's character story.

Geography: The craftshop stands outside Nasha Town on Lempo Isle, a short walk from the port town. It is a single enormous weather-beaten structure that Aino's story compares to a mechanical beast sprawled along quiet ridges, with rusty mechanical arms that sway in the wind. A Meeting Point of the same name sits near its centre, and Aino's own home is inside it (see Aino's House).

A local specialty, the Portable Bearing, can be found on the isle. Only a few residents are named at the shop: Bozena, Lalli and Zaitseva, plus Chard Lombro who appears once the Traveler has helped with the world quest Problem-Sorting Robot.

People: Aino is an orphan who treats her machines and screws as her family; she is a young child, and the craftshop is both her laboratory and her home. Ineffa, a tall robot built here, helps with housework and makes the krumkakes. Members of the Conch Gang, the children raised at Speranza, helped Aino find the building and move in. NPCs at the shop include Bozena, Lalli, Zaitseva and Chard Lombro.

Aino's official description warns that anyone who fails to appreciate her creations will find the craftshop's door slammed in their face, so a visitor should praise her designs before making requests. Ineffa's character story says word spread through Nasha Town that the craftshop had made a robot, and rumors of impossible powers followed.

History: Aino was taken in as one of the children under Katya at Speranza and learned mechanics from a Snezhnayan mechanic called Papa Wrench before he left with his merchant convoy. At dawn one day, carrying a small robot and followed by a wheeled toolbox, she was led by Conch Gang members to the abandoned structure and named it the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, vowing to invent a machine that makes the most delicious krumkakes. The shop's own loading-screen text says it began as her little workspace and became a renowned machine workshop after her many intricate inventions and Ineffa's birth.

Katya later saw Aino come to Speranza holding hands with Ineffa to buy sweets, and noticed the once-gaunt girl had grown healthy and bright. Ineffa's story adds that Aino often worked late, falling asleep beside her unfinished creation while building Ineffa. The craftshop also keeps an old rusted robot, the first one Aino ever assembled, which is kept in a cabinet in her bedroom.

Quests: In the Archon Quest chapter Song of the Welkin Moon, Aino and Ineffa are part of the Traveler's circle in Nasha Town. Aino's self-built cannon in town is mentioned in Rest Beyond Reach, where the pair are also optional conversation partners. In Welkin Moon's Homecoming, Aino mentions the shop's habit of using eggs and heating tubes, and Flins describes the gathering as including "the adorable Krumkake Craftshop". When the group goes to confront Dottore in the far north, Aino and Ineffa stay behind with Varka and Jahoda to guard Nasha Town.

Atmosphere: Clanking, hissing and rattling day and night, with the warm smell of baking krumkakes mixed into machine oil. It is cluttered and cheerful: parts, gears and half-finished contraptions everywhere, run by a cheerful child inventor and a precise, literal-minded robot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the craftshop is open and in use as Aino's workshop and home. The wiki records no change to it after its introduction.

33.comment: Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop: Clink Clank Clash
33.content: The Flagship Event Clink Clank Clash (Version 6.0, September 2025) begins with the Traveler and Paimon finding that Ineffa and Aino have been dragged into a curious crisis. Its games involve chasing rogue recon bots along the Moonlanes, testing a self-defense device, finding malfunctioning robots and sneaking a stealth robot past guards. It was a time-limited event; it is not a standing feature of the shop.

34.comment: Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop: Aino's Krumkake Creed
34.content: Aino's stated goal for the shop is to invent the best krumkake machine in the world, and her creed is to build interesting machines for fun and enjoy krumkakes in between. Ineffa makes the actual krumkakes. Asked how to befriend Aino, Ineffa answers: say no to savory krumkakes, admire Aino's inventions and play with Aino often.

35.content: Papa Wrench is the Snezhnayan mechanic who taught Aino at Speranza. When he left with his merchant convoy, he put a screw in her hand and told her not to underestimate her talent or put down her tools. His full background is not given.

36.content:
Crab Tsar's Palace (also: The Crab Tsar's Palace): The Crab Tsar's Palace is an underground cavern on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai, home to the Crab Tsar, an enormous and normally gentle crab. The Traveler reaches it through a deep pit just west of the Frostmoon Enclave while helping Maite Veliu, a self-styled master thief, hunt a cursed stone that had changed the crab's temper. Rock Crabs live in its passages.

The palace has an upper and a lower level on the map. Mirrors left behind by the Frostmoon Scions, which only they and the Crab Tsar can pass through, stand in its way. After the quest it is a calm spot with a teleport waypoint, where Maite stays and the Crab Tsar can be fought as a Local Legend.

Geography: A cave system reached by a pit to the west of the Frostmoon Enclave, on Hiisi Island, the home of the Frostmoon Scions. It descends in two levels (upper and lower). Passages are blocked by Unipolar Crystonite and by crab-built obstructions, and a maze of mirrors hides the way to the crab's lair.

Rock Crabs live throughout and respond to Lakkaberries, which Maite uses to coax them into opening a blocked path. The mirrors are described by Maite as left behind by the Frostmoon Scions; the Traveler must approach the centre of one while empowered with kuuvahki, which shatters it and drops the party to the crab's lair.

People: The Crab Tsar rules the palace. Maite Veliu, who presents herself as heir to the legendary thief Reed Miller, introduces herself to the party here and, later, reveals she belongs to the Conch Gang. Aila, the first Moonchanter, appears only as a name in Maite's story. A priestess in Frostmoon attire guides the party obliquely.

Maite plays the master thief and insists she is no petty crook, but she admits she is really in the palace to gather intelligence for the Conch Gang, and that she cannot beat the Crab Tsar alone. She says she once nearly fell into the Frostmoon Scions' hands and was freed by a young girl after telling stories.

History: Maite says the Crab Tsar was docile until some months earlier, when it found a strange stone and began carrying it on its back; thereafter its temper turned vicious, it crushed other crabs and learned to travel through the mirrors. When the party defeats it the stone flies away; the Tsar hides, which Maite reads as regret for what it did to the little crabs.

Maite compares the stone to a rock that fell from the sky near the Frostmoon Scions' home and says that if it had reached the market it could have hurt many more people. She also repeats a legend that Reed Miller once took the Frostmoon treasure back from a greedy governor, and that a stone of desire once bewitched the High Priestess Lovia.

Dangers: Before the quest ends, the Crab Tsar is a hostile Local Legend; in the quest variant it uses different attacks and the player does not directly harm it. Afterwards the crab, stronger than before, can challenge the Traveler; Maite says it is under her protection and listens to her.

Atmosphere: Damp stone, echoing chambers and mirrors that hint at hidden routes. Maite's whispered theatrics and the scurrying of small crabs lighten what could otherwise be a dread-filled maze.

Travel: Approach the pit west of the Frostmoon Enclave and drop in. After completing the quest a teleport waypoint marks the palace and Maite can be spoken to there.

Quests: The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar (World Quest, chapter Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle) starts at the pit. The Traveler and Paimon meet Maite, break the Crystonite barrier, use berries to coax the crabs, shatter a mirror and confront the Crab Tsar. The quest rewards Maite's IOU and Maite's Notes and makes the Crab Tsar a Local Legend.

Maite tells the party to mention her name at Speranza restaurant in Nasha Town, but admits she has no pull yet and that Katya will still bill them; she gives an IOU and promises to work a few days to pay for a meal herself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the palace is open. The stone that corrupted the Crab Tsar flew away at the quest's end, and nothing recorded since changes that.

37.content:
The Crab Tsar is a giant crab and Local Legend living in the Crab Tsar's Palace. Maite says it used to be gentle but became vicious while carrying a stone of desire on its back, crushing smaller crabs. After the stone left it hid away, and Maite says it is under her protection and obeys her.

With a Seed Dispensary equipped, its drops yield Lakkaberry and Midsommar Berry seeds.

38.content: Maite Veliu, giving that as her real name, presents herself as heir to the legendary thief Reed Miller and later admits she belongs to the Conch Gang, gathering intelligence. She describes the gang as a mutual aid and coordination group for like-minded people of similar age. She sends the Traveler to find her informant Hidimbi in Nasha Town.

39.content:
Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab (also: Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Laboratory): The Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab is an ancient research site in the Moontide Sea on the Frost Moon. Here Professor Maagees's team learned that Moonshade Trees fused with "Blackbody Matter" and stimulated with Archaeolune Energy could throw off reflective waves that formed a curtain-like barrier. That was the first stage of Project Lunar Veil, a plan to hide the moon.

The site keeps terminal records describing four stages of the work: the discovery of Blackbody Matter, the curtain-form containment itself, Project Lunar Veil Phase I, and Phase II. An Ancient Moon's Remnant of the same name holds a Moonshade Tree.

The records are written by someone close to the project who worries about the plan and later identifies as the person who named it. Treat the author as unnamed in this lab; other sites on the moon identify Lusalim as the Veil's designer.

Places: Features found here include an Ancient Moon's Remnant with a Moonshade Tree, a terminal that plays the records, Archaeolune Energy machinery (barriers, an Ancient Moon Pearl system and a backup power generator), material storage, and a "Pioneer Source Structure". The elite machine "Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network" guards the area.

History: After the researcher Ungien fused with the Stellar Blackbody, his body began exuding a black filament-like substance; Maagees named it Blackbody Matter. The terminal author notes that the same substance coated the outer hull of the Moongazer and explains why the ship stayed hidden. Experiments showed that it reacts with Archaeolune Energy and can fuse with plants and animals, sometimes shifting their colour from blue to black.

The author fears sending signals into deep space, since nothing proves that whoever receives them is friendly, and sets out to build a safeguard based on Blackbody Matter. The ecological team had grown thousands of Moonshade Trees; Maagees's team picked specimens highly compatible with the matter. Under enough Archaeolune stimulation they emitted reflective diffusive waves, and with greater intensity the waves formed a stable curtain with a radius beyond the whole laboratory. The author wanted to extend that range next.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and ancient as of 7.1; it can be explored and read for lore but is not inhabited.

40.comment: Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab: Project Lunar Veil
40.content: Project Lunar Veil was a safeguard for Project Moongazer: a veil of Blackbody-fused Moonshade Trees meant to obscure the moon from whatever might answer its signal. The lab here produced the first curtain; Ungien's Circle hosted the Phase I trial.

41.comment: Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab: Blackbody Matter
41.content: Blackbody Matter is the black filamentous substance first secreted by Ungien after he merged with the Stellar Blackbody, and which also coats the Moongazer's hull. It reacts to Archaeolune Energy, bonds with plants and animals, and carries information in some specimens.

key: far side of the Frost Moon
42.content:
Dark Side of the Moon (also: far side of the Frost Moon, the Dark Fortress, Darkside Base): The Dark Side of the Moon is the half of the Frost Moon that never faces Teyvat. Dragon researchers built a hidden base here as part of Project Moongazer. Later the Dragon Lord of Darkness, Nibelung, returned from the stars and reforged the moon into a weapon: the far side became a cannon drawing on the lunar core, aimed at Teyvat. The Heavenly Principles defeated him, and the weapon is dormant. Visitors reach it through the Project Moongazer quests (6.7).

At the bottom of the launch silo lies Moonheart Gap, the moon's core, where Columbina and the Traveler learned what Project Moongazer was.

Geography: A fortress-like landscape of launch silos and transport levels sunk into the moon's far side. Gravity is unreliable: in the silo the Traveler can walk along its curved wall, then drift weightless when the guardian draws power from the core. Archaeolune Energy barriers, Pioneer Source Structures (including exploding Annihilation Modules and Transmission Modules that teleport intruders away), terminals and security control rooms guard the way down.

The base is entered from the surface and descends through security zones, the lower base level that holds Lusalim's Laboratory, a sealed zone, and finally the silo and Moonheart Gap. The viewpoint named The Dark Fortress looks out over it; its caption describes the Dragon Lord of Darkness returning from the starry firmament to shatter the throne of the winged usurper.

Places: Lusalim's Laboratory sits on a lower transport level; its terminals hold the dragon researcher's farewell to his pupil Nin-Kiggia. Beneath the silo's door, which opens with the Ancient Moon's Fount, lies Lusalim's final facility. His earlier work, the Lunar Veil Laboratory, became the lunar sea. At the very bottom is Moonheart Gap, the core and source of the moon's power.

The silo's guardian is a boss machine, the Warden of the Flame, which borrows power from the core and removes gravity as it fights. It must be destroyed by turning Archaeolune Energy against its subnodes while dodging the high-energy blasts fired down the silo. Columbina then disables the weapon, and she and the Traveler pass into the core.

History: Ibni-Belum led dragon researchers to the Frost Moon, and they built research facilities in the Lunar Highlands and, on the far side, a base serving Project Moongazer. Lusalim, a pupil of Ungien and Maagees, later worked here and inherited their data; his Lunar Veil project failed and became the lunar sea. His terminal records that he yielded to the Heavenly Principles and gave up the project's results, and that he entrusted Project Moongazer to Nin-Kiggia. Nibelung came back from the Sea of Stars, corrupted by the Abyss, and rebuilt the moon into a space weapon powered by Moonheart Gap, after imprisoning the Frost Moon Goddess Canon; the Heavenly Principles defeated him and the weapon went silent.

Canon's imprisonment and the plan to turn all three moons against the Heavenly Principles come from the Frost Moon lore; Columbina's own account in Project Moongazer (Part 2) states only that the primordial ruler reforged the moon into a weapon, that the core's power became artillery fire aimed at Teyvat, and that he was defeated. The moon was the only one of the three to survive the war of funerary flame whole, and it was banished beyond the false sky.

Quests: Project Moongazer (Part 1) takes the Traveler and Columbina into the base; Part 2 takes them down the silo to the core. There they meet a recording of Nin-Kiggia, who explains that Eggie, the black kuuhenki, was born from the data sea in the core, and that Project Moongazer means sending the message the dragons once received back out into space. The pair then return to the Eye of Ibni-Belum, where Eggie sends the message with Columbina shielding it using her moon-goddess power.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the weapon is silent and the base is a ruin that can be explored. Nothing there shows any Abyssal presence, as with the rest of the moon.

Dangers: The Dark Side is hazardous more for its machinery than for monsters: security systems that reset the intruder, gravity shifts that can drop a careless visitor, and the silo's cannon. When the silo's door opens and a huge mechanism appears, Columbina wonders aloud whether the system has detected them, and says it can do nothing to stop them.

43.comment: Dark Side of the Moon: Moonheart Gap
43.content: The core of the Frost Moon and the source of its power, lying at the bottom of the launch silo. Nibelung drew on it to feed his space weapon. Inside it is the data sea where Nin-Kiggia gathered the researchers' information and where Eggie was born.

44.comment: Dark Side of the Moon: Lusalim's Final Terminal
44.content: Lusalim, a dragon researcher and pupil of Ungien and Maagees, left terminal records on the Dark Side thanking his own good fortune: being born after Ibni-Belum, being taken in by his teachers, and having Nin-Kiggia, whom he calls a true child of the stars. He entrusts Project Moongazer to her, says he will not live to see it done because he has sinned against dragonkind by yielding to the Heavenly Principles, and hopes to drift among the stars afterwards.

45.content:
Dreadshade Mire: Dreadshade Mire is a fog-shrouded swamp in the Voidsea Outlook area of Nod-Krai. Solovei, the Torchforger, and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, used three ancient stone seals there to imprison the Serpent of All Evils. Wild Hunt creatures roam the fog, and the Lightkeepers' signboards at the mire's edge warn that entry is not advised.

The Serpent was once a man named Raimo, a rare human high official under the Belyi Tsar and a disciple of Rotwang. The seal held for 500 years until Fatui activity in the mire weakened it, which is the setting of the 6.3 world quest To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner.

The three sealing pillars each carry an inscription naming one of Raimo's three great sins; the seal had held for 500 years, but in 6.3 the Lightkeepers found it failing.

Geography: A swamp thick with fog, with low visibility. Three sealing pillars stand at the northeast, northwest and south; the Serpent's lair lies deeper in. Local flora and fauna include Cottonspring Flowers, Glimmerfruit, Mandragora, Spirebloom, Slothsheep and Winter Icelea.

The edge of the mire is posted with Lightkeeper signboards warning of low visibility and Wild Hunt creatures. A Fatui camp stands near the second pillar and was abandoned in a hurry. Puzzles include Abyssal Fog Barriers, Lunar Conflux Barriers and Overflowing Abyssal Power.

History: Over 500 years ago Raimo used coercion, entrapment and murder to remove Rotwang's political opponents under the Belyi Tsar. After Rotwang was defeated by the Torchforger, Aila and Alia, Raimo transformed into the Serpent of All Evils and went to the mire, where Solovei and Aila sealed him with three stone pillars. A pillar spell is engraved on each, naming one of his sins: using blood ties to coerce, spreading slander to wreck trust, and pushing others to their deaths.

In the quest the Lightkeepers Janusz and his apprentice Oskari are on patrol checking the seal when it fails. Janusz is badly hurt; the Traveler restores the pillars by purifying them with kuuvahki, leading the prism to the third, with Spirebloom flowers later weakening the Serpent during the fight. Oskari says the seal had stayed stable for five hundred years.

People: Lightkeepers Janusz, a joker who misses a cat named Jelly that left him over ten years ago, and his earnest apprentice Oskari, who writes the report. The Lightkeepers suspect Fatui involvement; they plan to investigate and file a protest.

Fatui survivors flee from a chasing monster near the first and second pillars; the camp held a Prospector's Command ordering the discovery of new pillars and observation of local kuuvahki without alerting the Lightkeepers.

Dangers: Wild Hunt creatures (Wilderness Exiles, Wilderness Hunters), Fishers of Hidden Depths, Radiant Glacial Wolves, Treasure Hoarders, Evil Eyes of Blightseep and Abyssal Riftlines. The thick fog makes it easy to wander into trouble.

Before the 6.3 victory the Serpent of All Evils itself, an enlarged Evil Eye of Blightseep with a special core, haunted the swamp's depths and could revive itself once.

Quests: To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner (Janusz and Oskari; purify the three sealing pillars, then fight the Serpent) is the mire's story quest.

It can start at the first or second pillar or by finding Janusz, 'initially ???' near the third.

Atmosphere: Thick fog, wet ground and glimmering plants such as Spirebloom, with the stone pillars standing as the mire's only landmarks.

Travel: Not advised by the Lightkeepers. When Janusz is wounded he asks the Traveler to fetch reinforcements from Piramida.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the three pillars are restored and the Serpent of All Evils is defeated, but the mire is still fog-bound and dangerous.

The Lightkeepers still plan to investigate the Fatui camp that may have weakened the seal.

46.comment: Dreadshade Mire: The Serpent of All Evils
46.content: Raimo was a human official of the Belyi Tsar's era and Rotwang's disciple who used coercion, entrapment and murder for his master. After Rotwang fell he became the Serpent of All Evils, a monster resembling a giant Evil Eye, and was sealed in Dreadshade Mire by Solovei and Aila. The Traveler defeated it in To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner.

47.comment: Dreadshade Mire: Sealing Pillars of Dreadshade Mire
47.content: Three stone pillars hold the Frostmoon Scions' seal on the Serpent of All Evils. Each is inscribed with a verse naming one of Raimo's three great sins and the words that the evidence of his crimes will be engraved upon the reefs, inscribed within the lantern's shade, and preserved beneath the moonlight. Janusz says the seal itself needs no special power: Solovei and Aila left their strength in the pillars, so channeling kuuvahki into each one restores it.

48.content:
Dunanna Forward Station (also: Dunanna Station): Dunanna Forward Station is a buried installation under Dunanna Pit, an area of Nod-Krai near Fontaine and east of Pohjola. It is an old moon-landing base that includes a chamber for computing the orbits of the Three Moons, a generator room and a Main Control Hall, and it launches a lunar shuttle. It appears in the world quest Pioneers (Version 6.7).

The Traveler and Paimon find it while following someone they believe is Columbina to a small island. The facility is dormant until the Traveler uses Archaeolune power to restart it.

Geography: The station lies beneath a small island reached by Moonlane from Misty Shoal, on the east side of Piramida. A huge pit filled with water lies on the island, and a hole in the ground leads down to the ruins. Floating Archaeolune rocks, broken machines and sealed doors fill the ruins. Dunanna Pit has no Meeting Point of its own; it shares the Ancient Moon's Remnant at Nuur Stone Circle with the Lunar Highlands.

The map shows the station as having a lower level, where the Main Control Hall sits. Inside the ruins are rings that fall to the floor until restored, and signs in Edict Module form label rooms (for example the Celestial Orbit Computation Chamber).

Places: The Celestial Orbit Computation Chamber holds a terminal that calculates the positions of the Three Moons (Trilune coordinates). Only the Frost Moon can be reached from it; the Eternal and Iridescent Moons return "connection lost". The generator room has a Backup Power Generator that does not respond until it is struck with Archaeolune Ripples. Another room simulates lunar gravity, and the Main Control Hall is the central hub for command reception and transmission for the whole station. A lunar shuttle waits beyond the hall.

Moving parts include Archaeolune energy pathways, blocked by Ancient Moon Pearls that must be lifted before power can flow. Intrusion defences include Transmission Modules that target visitors and a guardian called Anzu, a Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network, in the Main Control Hall; destroying it sets off a self-destruct countdown that asks for orbital coordinates.

Quests: In Pioneers (Moon Gazing, Act I), the Traveler and Paimon follow what looks like Columbina but is a black kuuhenki wearing her likeness. Before the reveal, the figure silently grants the Traveler the power of Archaeolune Energy so that together they can restore the station. The kuuhenki says Columbina had rescued it on the moon and taken it to Silvermoon Hall, and that it wants to return to the moon; Paimon names it Eggie. The Traveler decides to ride the shuttle with it.

Moon Gazing is a world quest series on the Frost Moon map whose later acts are Visitors From the Stars and Project Moongazer; this entry covers only the station.

Atmosphere: An underground complex of broken machines and drifting, weightless-looking rocks, empty of people. Automated voice announcements and alarms speak for it; once the Traveler restores power, the machinery comes back to life and treats visitors as intruders.

Dangers: Automated defences: Transmission Modules that attack intruders, Secret Source Automatons, and the Main Control Hall's guardian Anzu. The self-destruct system treats any visitor as an intruder.

Status as of 7.1: After Pioneers the station is working and its shuttle has left with the Traveler's party. Nothing after 7.1 is recorded.

49.comment: Dunanna Forward Station: Eggie the Black Kuuhenki
49.content: The black kuuhenki that leads the Traveler through the station first appears as Columbina and changes into its real form when the Traveler asks for the gesture they share in Silvermoon Hall. It can only speak in short, breathless phrases, and speaks more clearly through the shuttle's archaeolune spectrometer. It says it belongs on the moon, has a mission it has forgotten, and was rescued by Columbina. Paimon nicknames it Eggie after being tricked into boarding the shuttle.

50.comment: Dunanna Forward Station: Celestial Orbit Computation Chamber
50.content: The terminal prompts for Trilune coordinates of the Three Moons. In the quest only the Frost Moon coordinates are found; it then sends base engineering blueprints and a route map to the Main Control Hall for moon landing preparations.

51.content:
Dunanna Pit: Dunanna Pit is a mist-covered, island-like area of Nod-Krai added in 6.7 (Luna VIII), lying close to Fontaine and east of Pohjola. Its centre is Dunanna Forward Station, a half-buried ruin of a vanished civilisation with a huge mechanism and a chamber holding a spaceship. It is where the Moon Gazing quests start and where the road to the Frost Moon opens.

The area has no Meeting Point of its own. It shares the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Nuur Stone Circle (on the Frost Moon's Lunar Highlands) for Luna Treasure Compass progress. Few people are met here; it is a place of ruins, mist and machinery rather than settlements.

Geography: Dunanna Pit is a separate area of Nod-Krai, reached by sea from the main isles. The wiki places it near Fontaine and east of Pohjola, though the Pohjola page also counts it as part of that island (see uncertainties). Its named subareas are Misty Shoal, a shore under a strangely cloudless bright-blue sky, and Dunanna Forward Station, the ruin around the pit itself. A viewpoint text calls the place a deserted, mist-shrouded island with traces of a bygone civilisation, and the 'pit' of the name is a huge hole at the heart of the island.

The station has an upper level on the surface and a lower level underground. The Main Control Hall is on the lower level and, per its map description, is the central room for receiving and sending every command in the station. The area introduces the Gravimeter, an exploration mechanic that exists only here, and a Statue of the Seven. Unlocking that statue completes the achievement 'A Lamentation of Catastrophe'. The achievements for this area and the Frost Moon sit in a category called Unfettered Crescent.

Places: Misty Shoal: the landing shore, where the Moon Gazing quest begins. Dunanna Forward Station: the buried ruin and its mechanism; the Main Control Hall is its core.

The station is dotted with viewpoints. One, 'Mystery Pit of the Misty Isle', appears after the third step of the opening quest, Pioneers. Another, 'Moonbound Ship', appears after step ten and describes the Tonatiuh trembling as a heavenly ship sets sail for the moon. The area is linked to the Frost Moon through the mechanism described in the quests section.

People: No residents are listed for the area. The figure the Traveler meets in the opening quest is not a person: it is a black kuuhenki (a kuuvahki-formed being) wearing Columbina's likeness. The real Columbina does not appear in the station during Pioneers.

History: Canon gives no date or name for the civilisation that built the station. The only statements are the viewpoint's reference to a bygone civilisation and the Main Control Hall's description of a working command centre. The area was released in 6.7 with the Frost Moon map, which also introduced the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network enemy and the Ancient Moon's Remnant system.

Atmosphere: Fog, a clear but strangely cloudless sky over the shoal, silence, cold metal underground, and the feeling that a machine is waiting to be woken. Mood is eerie rather than hostile until the safety systems wake.

Because the shoal is cloud-free while the station is wrapped in mist, scenes can contrast the bright empty sky above with dim machinery below.

Dangers: In Pioneers, once the Traveler tries to board the spaceship, the safety system flags them as intruders and attacks. Aside from that, canon lists no special hazards for the area.

Travel: Reached by travelling to the area on the Nod-Krai map. There is no town or Meeting Point; progress is tracked with the Frost Moon's Ancient Moon's Remnant. A Teleport Waypoint network and the Luna Treasure Compass are available as in other Nod-Krai areas.

Quests: Moon Gazing (6.7) is the world quest series that unlocks the Frost Moon. Its first act, Pioneers, begins at Misty Shoal.

In Pioneers, the Traveler and Paimon see Columbina walking ahead and follow her to Dunanna Forward Station, but she does not answer them. Underground they find a disassembled giant mechanism and a dead energy device. The 'Columbina' figure grants the Traveler Archaeolune Energy, which powers the device. The mechanism, restored, shows a large blue sphere circled by three smaller spheres standing for the Three Moons, and a console lets the user pick Trilune coordinates; only the Frost Moon will connect. When the Traveler asks her to take their hand, as in Silvermoon Hall, she turns into a black kuuhenki and flees. The chase ends in a vast chamber with a spaceship, whose defences attack. Later acts are Visitors From the Stars and Project Moongazer; the wiki has no summary of them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is simply open to explore. No later change to it is recorded.

Moon Gazing continues past the opening act, with the Frost Moon open for exploration. The Project Moongazer thread is covered by its own entry.

52.content:
The Dunanna Forward Station is the buried ruin at the centre of Dunanna Pit.
