Its lower level holds the Main Control Hall, the station's central command room, and a large mechanism that is disassembled until the Traveler restores it with Archaeolune Energy. The mechanism shows the Three Moons as spheres and can reach only the Frost Moon. The builders are not named. A viewpoint calls the island deserted and shrouded in mist, with traces of a lost civilisation.

Beneath the control area is a chamber containing a spaceship whose safety system attacks anyone who tries to board without clearance. The viewpoint 'Moonbound Ship' later mentions the Tonatiuh and a heavenly ship setting sail for the moon.

53.comment: Dunanna Pit: Moon Gazing and the Pioneers Quest
53.content:
Moon Gazing is the world quest series (6.7) that unlocks the Frost Moon. Act I, Pioneers, sends the Traveler and Paimon to Dunanna Forward Station after a figure that looks like Columbina but never answers. It turns out to be a black kuuhenki. The restored mechanism can link only to the Frost Moon, and the chase ends at a spaceship that tries to repel them.

The series continues in Act II (Visitors From the Stars) and Act III (Project Moongazer). Detailed plot of those acts is not recorded in the sources used here.

54.content:
The Eye of Ibni-Belum (also: Eye of Ibni-Belum, the Moongazers' tower, Silent Barrens): The Eye of Ibni-Belum is a tower-like dragon station on the Frost Moon. The dragon pioneer Ibni-Belum, called the First Moongazer, built it after receiving a mysterious signal from deep space that he took to be from Nibelung, hoping to hear it again. When it never came, the researchers turned it into a lunar surface monitoring station. In 6.7 the Traveler and Eggie reactivate it, and in the end Eggie uses it as the antenna to send the dragons' message back out into the stars.

It is the first stop of the Moon Gazing quests and the base for the Traveler and Columbina's journey to the dark side.

Geography: Located in the southern Lunar Highlands, with a teleport waypoint, a viewpoint called Silent Barrens and another called A Gaze Toward the Stars. It has terminals, Backup Power Generators, Archaeolune Energy pathways, Pioneer Source Structures and a High-Speed Transit Lane, and an underground energy generation station below.

Reactivating the Eye requires finding other energy generation stations on the surface, restoring power underground and adjusting the signal locator at the top of the tower.

History: During his exploration of the moon and the space around it, Ibni-Belum received a signal he could not decipher. He believed it was a message from Nibelung and built the Eye as a transceiver to catch it again. He died, still waiting. Many years later the signal returned, the Eye recorded its coordinates, and the life scientist Ungien flew the Moongazer to find its source. He came back fused with a creature from space who carried a message of hope from a dying civilisation, delivered the message, and died.

The Eye then became central to Project Moongazer: a mission to send similar messages out so that other civilisations would know they were not alone in the dark. The Eye is the antenna for these messages. In one of its terminals, the First Moongazer's final text says that, although Ungien had been expelled from the team as an oath-breaker, his lunar biosphere work and test sites might still help landing on the distant star, and ends with praise to the Creator and the goal of journeying to the stars.

Quests: Pioneers (Part 2) activates the Eye. Project Moongazer (Part 2) returns here with the key; Eggie reads the project's purpose, gives up her mission briefly out of concern for her friends, then, supported by Columbina and the Traveler, sends the message as a toast to those who came before. A bundle of Saurus Crackers left near a terminal with a note in slime reading "They're all for you, Eggie" is a small post-quest detail.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Eye has sent the message and remains operational.

55.comment: The Eye of Ibni-Belum: Ibni-Belum the First Moongazer
55.content: A dragon pioneer, called the First Moongazer, who led dragon researchers to the Frost Moon and began Project Moongazer. He died long before the Traveler's time, and the record in his name shows his faith in Nibelung. His name resembles an Akkadian phrase meaning "the Lord has created". The wiki holds no character profile for him.

56.content: A black kuuhenki met on the moon who travels with the Traveler and Paimon. She is revealed as a new life born of the data sea in the moon's core and as the project's inheritor, sometimes called by the Nin-Kiggia recording's nickname Ninnin; she chooses to send the Moongazers' message from the Eye at the end of Project Moongazer (Part 2).

57.content:
Eye of Kratti (also: Beneath the Forsaken Sea): The Eye of Kratti is a small island off Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai, with a crystalline tree growing at its centre. It was once a whirlpool of the same name that became a forbidden zone because of its turbulent waters, rumours of monsters including the Kratti it is named for, and the many people who vanished in it. The wrecked ship Atlas lies here with many others.

Its quest, Whisper Beneath the Waves, belongs to the East of the Moon, West of the Sun series and involves ghosts of the Atlas' crew and the tree's roots.

Geography: A small island with a crystalline tree at its centre; the shipwreck of the Atlas and many others sit around it. A lower map layer, Beneath the Forsaken Sea, is entered by dropping into a pit near the wrecked ship on the eastern side, after breaking a scrap metal pile while in a kuuvahki-empowered state.

Below ground are caves with unipolar crystonite blocks and blue fields that switch on and off, and at the bottom the "roots" of the tree.

History: Before the island there was a whirlpool, the Eye of Kratti, which Ilmari describes as a forbidden zone with monster sightings and many lost souls. A few years before the present the ship Atlas sank near it, along with the Proof of the Cognoscenti that was aboard. Some time later a crystalline tree sprouted from the whirlpool and made a small island. Ilmari says rocks fell from the sky around that time and "little shiny things" began to appear, and a friend of his kept hearing strange singing nearby.

In Whisper Beneath the Waves the Traveler and Paimon meet the ghosts of the Atlas' fallen crew, follow them to the tree's roots and revive the tree with kuuvahki, so that it shines. Kuuvahki Dewdrops appear near the tree and the lost Proof of the Cognoscenti is found.

People: Ilmari is the NPC found here and the source of most of the local lore. Ghosts of the Atlas' crew appear in the quest.

Dangers: Caves with unipolar crystonite barriers and fields that switch on and off. Historically, the whirlpool's turbulent waters were the main danger.

Quests: Whisper Beneath the Waves (a world quest in East of the Moon, West of the Sun) begins here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the whirlpool is gone and the island with its restored tree stands in its place.

58.content:
False Moon Institute (also: Memories: Twilight of the Heretic): The False Moon Institute is a Trounce Domain in Nod-Krai, set at the Special Territory Research Institute in the far north of Ashveil Peak. It is a Fatui research facility, and the domain lets the Traveler relive the battle against the Heretic of the False Moon, the Fatui Harbinger the Doctor. The domain is presented as a memory of a fight over the fate of Nod-Krai, which was won by people standing together to defend their homeland.

It appeared in Version 6.3 and unlocks after the Archon Quest "Welkin Moon's Homecoming" (Song of the Welkin Moon, act True Moon). Its in-game name is "Memories: Twilight of the Heretic", and the final battle is remembered as one that tore the sky apart.

Geography: The Institute stands in the northern reaches of Nod-Krai, in Ashveil Peak, the northernmost part of the Pohjola region. The domain text hints at structures buried deep beneath its foundations, and at dusk the place is said to hold the memory of the great battle.

The arena is an open fighting ground that a rift can open into a second, separate space during the encounter (see the gameplay section).

History: The domain text calls the Institute a Fatui facility that hides secrets as deep as the structures under it. The Doctor, Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, is the Heretic of the False Moon: he seized the authority of the three moons and sought what the Archive calls the divine throne of a "new world". He is described as having sought godhood through the suffering of others. He met his twilight, brought down by those who stood together in defence of their home.

The Archive entry credits him with a creed that Teyvat's order was imposed, not natural: reason cast out what exceeded its limits; life and death bound people into mortal shells; time and space fenced the mind into obedience; and the gods who governed afterwards were false. Stripping every "shackle" away, he held, would reveal the essence of all things, and he called that the first light of a new world. These are the Archive's words for his philosophy, not a neutral statement of fact.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world events. This is a weekly-boss Trounce Domain whose rewards are the Mask of the Virtuous Doctor, Madman's Restraint and the Elixir of the Heretic. The Heretic uses Physical, Cryo, Electro and Hydro attacks. The Ley Line Disorder says he turns a rift from beyond the world against challengers, and that the authority from the marrow of the three moons lets him set prohibitions that must be obeyed briefly or punished.

Notable abilities: after surviving a single huge hit he raises all RES and recovers the damage ("Return of the False Moon"); Moonwither Realms are Cryo zones that grow and slow characters, with a rift to an alternate dimension where Moon Replica Shades can be defeated to remove them; his "Authority of the Three Moons" bans facing him (Iridescent Moon), moving far (Frost Moon) or reverses movement (Eternal Moon), with energy drain and a trap as punishment for breaking the first two; "Moonfall Impact" has Ancient Moon's Remnants fall and the party must shelter behind them. His voice lines include "With the marrow of the three moons in my hand, behold the false moon's fall!"

Atmosphere: Cold, clinical and quiet: a laboratory complex at the edge of the world under a night sky. The remembered fight leaves an afterimage of cracked moonlight, but the domain closes on calm, with the real moon back in its sky.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain remains available as a replay of a conflict that ended in 6.3. The Doctor's role as the Heretic is over; the domain does not suggest any ongoing Fatui activity at the Institute. What happened to the facility itself is not stated.

59.comment: False Moon Institute: Heretic of the False Moon
59.content: The Heretic of the False Moon is the form in which the Doctor, Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, appears as the weekly boss of the False Moon Institute; the Archive files him as "The Doctor". He holds the authority of the three moons and speaks coldly and efficiently, treating weak attacks as dull and stalling as inefficient. In the Song of the Welkin Moon arc he is the antagonist whose defeat ends the crisis at Nasha Town.

60.content:
Favonius Keep: Favonius Keep is the Knights of Favonius' camp in Nod-Krai, on Wavechaser Plain. It is the base of Grand Master Varka's long expedition from Mondstadt: tents, a command tent with a meeting point, and a small garrison that gathers intelligence on the Wild Hunt and other Abyssal threats. It is deliberately modest and a little scruffy, and it smells of Mondstadt dandelion wine whenever a shipment has come in.

Varka describes it as a station for sharing what the knights have learned about the Abyss with the Northern Intelligence Network, so the camp is half military post, half listening post. Any Knights of Favonius camp is open to the Honorary Knight (the Traveler), by Varka's own word.

Geography: The camp sits on Wavechaser Plain in northern Nod-Krai, a cold, windswept open country that the wiki links to the Pohjola island group; the Pillar of Embla and the Amsvartnir lake area lie in the same plain. Pine Amber can be gathered nearby.

Varka's justification for an outpost in Nod-Krai is that countless winds cross it every day.

Places: A large command tent (where Varka is usually found and where the meeting point stands), smaller tents for the knights and a quartermaster, a training patch used for drills, and a store of casks. A tent near the entrance houses Godwin once he has joined the force.

The camp is the knights' mail room too. Varka hands three letters to the knight Mika for the Lightkeepers' headquarters at Piramida, for Nefer of the Curatorium of Secrets, and for Mondstadt, with the instruction to keep up the same communication routine as before.

People: Commander Anselm ("Expedition Team" Garrison Commander, formerly Captain of the 6th Company) runs the garrison, with the knights Ekbert, Erminie, Laurent, Leifhelm, Nannina and Winfried. Grand Master Varka is the camp's leader and central figure. Anselm, Nannina and Laurent are described as handling administrative work left behind by Cardinal Seamus Pegg, who has since returned to Mondstadt.

Ekbert is from Springvale; he, Leifhelm and Winfried are the three who get sobered up with parade drills after the wine arrives. Erminie keeps the liquor stock and also helps devise safer explosives so the camp is not blown up after a night out. Godwin joined the force late: he missed the departure from Mondstadt, was later sent north by Varka to make his own way, and now serves in a tent at the entrance. Mika, a knight in Varka's force, carries the Grand Master's letters out of the camp.

History: Varka led the expedition out of Mondstadt on the strength of a warning of an Abyssal storm in the north, with no clear idea where it would strike. The Keep is where the force settled in Nod-Krai to gather intelligence and fight the Wild Hunt. After the Wild Hunt's leader Rerir was sealed, Varka told the Traveler that things had not entirely quietened and that the camp would become a long-term intelligence station.

Varka's own account, told on a night of feasting, is that the force marched knowing only that an Abyssal storm was gathering and that every hour of hesitation cost lives. He says different Abyssal disasters have been occurring all over Teyvat, always shifting and never alike, and wants the Northern Intelligence Network to share findings with the knights.

Culture: Drinking is treated as serious business and also strictly regulated. The expeditionary force may drink, but there are rules about when and how much, and one sober guard is always kept on watch over the rest. Varka has kept that duty for himself on the nights that matter, and jokes that the cup in his hand is the most special brew, only to reveal apple cider.

Barrel-rolling is a Knights of Favonius training drill, teaching force control and precision. Varka tells anecdotes of running it with Noelle, Razor, and the Spark Knight Klee, and of Lohen, who skipped it to poke a monster nest instead. The knights are homesick: the first taste of Dawn Winery dandelion wine in years makes Ekbert, Leifhelm and Winfried wistful for Mondstadt, and Ekbert asks the Traveler about his home village of Springvale.

Dangers: Wild Hunt stragglers wander the plain without a leader and with a primal urge to destroy; the Lightkeepers and Varka's knights hold them in check. Pale-Furred Wolves hunt on the slopes around the camp and cornered the wine courier Donatas at the foot of a mountain.

Varka expects a larger threat behind the stragglers. At the time of the Lupus Majoris story the knights faced a red wolf calling itself Roland, a Wild Hunt leader raised by the Abyss after Rerir fell, and the Keep served as the base where they brought samples and held council.

Travel: The Keep has a meeting point (unlocked by On This Intoxicating Night) that can be built up with the Traveler's help. Reaching it means travelling to Nod-Krai and crossing Wavechaser Plain; the Traveler's own trip north in Varka's story quest was made on Dvalin's back.

Supplies from Mondstadt arrive slowly: the Dawn Winery dandelion wine in On This Intoxicating Night is carried most of the way across the continent and nearly lost at the foot of a mountain near the camp.

Quests: On This Intoxicating Night (world quest, 6.3) starts here and unlocks the meeting point; Like Seeds on the Wind follows at construction level 5. Varka's story quest, To Those Who Embark on the Expedition (Lupus Majoris Chapter Act I, 6.4), ends with a council at the Keep. The anecdotes Varka: Communications and Varka: A Suitable Weapon are set here.

Anecdote text in A Suitable Weapon has Varka training with no suitable weapon or ore to hand, for himself or for Noelle; he concludes the matter will wait until everyone is back in Mondstadt.

Atmosphere: Canvas and woodsmoke against pale northern light, with the smell of Mondstadt wine and a few knights drilling or arguing over rations. The camp is understaffed, a bit of a ghost town by Varka's own joke, and cheerful about it. Evenings are the loudest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Keep is a small Knights of Favonius garrison in Nod-Krai that Varka still uses; most of the expedition has returned to Mondstadt.

The garrison is led by Commander Anselm, with Cardinal Seamus Pegg gone home and Varka present on his visits. The camp is a quiet intelligence post focused on the Wild Hunt and Abyssal activity. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 changes this.

61.content:
Final Night Cemetery (also: Light of Oaths Sworn): The Final Night Cemetery is a graveyard around a lighthouse on Paha Isle, in Nod-Krai. It was once an active outpost of the Lightkeepers (Ratniki). Several decades ago a fight with the Wild Hunt put out the lighthouse's light and killed most of the garrison, and the survivors buried their dead here. Flins, a Ratnik, now lives alone on the island, together with many ghosts of fallen Lightkeepers.

The Meeting Point of the same name stands at the lighthouse. The map description says that a certain Ratnik lives here alone but faithfully fulfils his duties. It is always dark at the cemetery.

Geography: A small, dark island with a lighthouse that has a telescope for signalling, a cooking stove, a monument bearing the Lightkeepers' oath, and rows of graves. The western part held a tavern long ago. The local specialty is Frostlamp Flower.

From the lighthouse telescope the player can view distant scenes: the coastal waters, the open sea with Fatui and mechanical constructs, and a far island with the city of Piramida in the north; the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau looms in the distance like a silent behemoth.

People: Flins is the island's only living Ratnik. Ghosts of dead Lightkeepers remain: the Loud Phantom (Dietrich), a Food-Obsessed Phantom (Jaakob, after The Chef's Tale) and a Ritual-Conducting Phantom.

The graves include those of the Lightkeepers Aimo, Dietrich, Eetu and Haapa, the chef Jaakob, the Khorin family (Danuta, Hamalainen and their young daughter Adina) and the Special Support Squad Sumrak. An engraved inscription honours "Aarnivalkea" Chudomir. The epitaphs read differently when Flins is the active character.

History: The island was an active outpost whose lighthouse guided merchants and Lightkeeper fleets and reported Wild Hunt movement; its light was never extinguished and became a symbol of hope. A mysterious blue lantern kept there became a Ratnik legend. Several decades ago the Wild Hunt put out the light, and ninety percent of the troops died. In despair the Ratniki turned to the lantern and coincidentally awakened Flins, who helped them fight despite being newly awake and limited in power. The survivors and Flins buried the fallen and made the cemetery; the Lightkeepers then left and only Flins remained.

The monument records the Lightkeepers' oath: that they foresaw a night sky devoured by deathly silence, vowed to use their bones and blood as fuel, and promised to keep the flame of hope burning in the snowy plains. The full text is shown when Flins or Illuga inspects it after the quest Lightkeepers' Oath.

Culture: Gravestones are inscribed with short blessings: wishes for dreams of wine, song, flowers, or the flavour of smoked fish. A notice board in the tavern advertised Dandelion Wine from Mondstadt and warned the ghost Loud Phantom's seat was not to be touched. The lighthouse follows a signal system: Distress, Guidance, Summoning, All Safe and Warning, each a pattern of short and long flashes.

Atmosphere: Always dark, quiet except for ghosts and sea, with a single steady beam from the lighthouse. Gravestones, a stove that someone relights if it is put out, and a long-closed tavern give it the feel of a place still kept up for the dead.

Quests: To the Lighthouse (Flins; Aimo and Eetu appear) starts here and unlocks the Meeting Point. It leads to The Special Support Squad's Tale. The Chef's Tale and Lightkeepers' Oath also involve the island.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Flins lives and keeps watch at the Final Night Cemetery's lighthouse.

62.comment: Final Night Cemetery: The Blue Lantern
62.content: A mysterious blue lantern was kept on Paha Isle. Ratniki made it a local legend: if followed, it would guide them far from the Wild Hunt. The Starshyna of the time ordered offerings to it. When the garrison was being overwhelmed, the survivors turned to it in despair and coincidentally awakened Flins.

63.comment: Final Night Cemetery: Lightkeepers' Lamp Signals
63.content: The Lamp Signal Handbook in the lighthouse lists signals as patterns of short and long flashes: Distress (short-long-short twice), Guidance, Summoning, All Safe and Warning (the entry for Warning is unreadable).

64.content:
The Flagship (also: The Flagship tavern): The Flagship is the rowdiest tavern in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. Drifters, treasure hunters and bounty hunters gather there to swap intel and pick up commissions, and the bartender Demyan runs it with a cheerful, lively air. It also rents rooms: the Traveler stays here in the Song of the Welkin Moon story.

The in-game map text calls it once a haven for drifters and treasure hunters, brimming with secrets, lies and raucous energy, and says recent management changes have made it safer. It still warns that a visitor who lets his guard down for a second might regret more than the choice of drink.

People: Demyan, a young man in a cap and cardigan, sells food and drinks and offers rooms. He says business is good, that a few small incidents beat a stale evening, and that his boss sent him here as a good fit. Others listed at the tavern are Kruchek, a Fatui recruiter, Leszek, an employee, Paavo, a host, Pentti, a nostalgic traveler, plus Suronja and Tapani.

Demyan keeps the stock honest: he tells Flins that he waters nothing and sells no poor quality drinks, even if it costs him some Mora. Flins, a regular, recommends wines that Demyan says sold out quickly; when Flins collects a bottle Demyan has kept in the cellar, Flins asks for two glasses so that they can share it. Katya, who runs Speranza, tells visitors who want gossip to go to the Flagship rather than to her.

Places: A bar with a jukebox and a bounty board, plus a hallway and guest rooms. The jukebox has four records: "A Carefree Cup", "Homecoming to Port", "A Borrowed Hour" and "Desire's Intent". The default is the leftmost record.

Demyan sells Berries and Fried Meat and the Roulette Special daily, with the drinks Piramida Nightingale, Frontier Land and Wildberry Trail, and the recipes for the two dishes. The Traveler's room has a desk where the Marionette's Notebook can be read after Welkin Moon's Homecoming.

Quests: The Intel quest The Dust Settles ends the tavern's bounty line about Hark the Crackjaw: Jahoda and Nefer of the Curatorium of Secrets meet the Traveler at the Flagship and conclude that the man living in the hermit's hut is the wanted Hark, who took over from the real hermit Derwent, probably dead. After Hark is defeated, the notice changes to say the bounty is fulfilled.

In Welkin Moon's Homecoming, the Traveler and Paimon wake in the Flagship after a restful night and later treat themselves to a feast there before heading to Speranza.

Bounty board: The board lists four notices. Hidimbi, a fortune teller from Sumeru, is wanted for suspected curses and large-scale fraud. Gonpachi, an Inazuman in Kairagi garb, is wanted by the Voynich Guild for attacks on traveling merchants. The New Iron and Salt Gang is wanted by Spina di Rosula for suspected smuggling of restricted hazardous goods. Hark the Crackjaw, former helmsman of the ship Atlas, is wanted for murder.

The notices change when the matching quests are done: Gonpachi's is marked fulfilled after Peco's testimony; the smuggling bounty is marked complete with Spina di Rosula's regards; Hark's refers visitors to the Curatorium of Secrets after The Dust Settles; and Hidimbi's becomes a search request because the buyer now suspects he was not sincere enough in courtship.

Atmosphere: Loud, crowded and full of rumors, with a jukebox playing and a bounty board on the wall. It is described as safer than it once was, but gossip about the Fatui and the Frostmoon Scions still travels fast.

History: Under its earlier management it was a place for drifters and treasure hunters to hide out. Demyan says that since the Fatui set up their Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle the atmosphere has changed a lot, that some resent how the Fatui throw their weight around while others want their new technology, and that the Frostmoon Scions' view of them has stayed constant. After the Bureau suffered a blow, he adds that many people were pleased but they must still do business with the Fatui.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and doing good business. Nothing in 7.0 or 7.1 content changes it.

65.content: Demyan is the bartender of the Flagship, a young man with light blond hair, light blue eyes and a dark brown cap decorated with a small flower. He greets visitors with a friendly invitation to sit anywhere, gives the Traveler a Guide to Elysium on first chat, and has a good-humored view of trouble: handling it is fun on its own. His full background is not given.

66.content: Hark is a former helmsman of the Atlas wanted for multiple murders. The Curatorium's finding is that the hermit Derwent is likely dead and that Hark took his place in the hut, even though Derwent apparently knew who he was when he took him in. The Traveler defeats Hark, with Nefer as a trial character.

67.content:
Frost Moon: The Frost Moon is the second of Teyvat's Three Moons, which the dragon king Nibelung created. It is the brightest of them and the only one that survived the war of funerary flame. The Heavenly Principles banished it beyond the false sky, where its goddess Canon faded and died. For thousands of years Teyvat saw only a fake "shadowmoon" in its place. In True Moon (6.3) the real Frost Moon was pulled back inside the false sky, and Columbina, its new Moon Goddess, became the Trilune Goddess. It is now a reachable lunar world, full of ruins left by ancient dragon researchers.

The game counts it as a subregion of Nod-Krai even though it lies off Teyvat's surface. Its three areas are the Lunar Highlands, the Moontide Sea and the Dark Side of the Moon. The Heavenly Principles hid the Traveler's own spaceship there.

Geography: The Frost Moon is a cratered world of grey highlands with much lower gravity than Teyvat: jumps carry far and falls are slow. Teyvat hangs huge in its sky. Turbulent Archaeolune energy shapes it. This is an ancient lunar power related to kuuvahki, which Columbina calls "blue kuuvahki". The near side is divided between the Lunar Highlands and the Moontide Sea, a glowing lunar mare that covers much of that face. The far side, facing away from Teyvat, was rebuilt into an enormous weapon. The moon's core, the Moonheart Gap, powers it.

The Lunar Highlands hold the Eye of Ibni-Belum, Traveler's Crater, Ungien's Circle (seen from space as a yellowed crater) and the Golden Hall. The Moontide Sea is a sea of concentrated Archaeolune energy. It was born when the Heavenly Principles destroyed a dragon laboratory, and floating stones rise from it. The far side holds the "Dark Fortress" of launch tubes, where gravity is strange enough to walk on the walls. Some zones are weightless, others under crushing hypergravity, and the dragons' gravimeters can change the local pull.

Places: - **Lunar Highlands**: the dragon pioneers' first settlement zone. It holds the Eye of Ibni-Belum (a deep-space transceiver later turned into a lunar monitoring station), Ungien's Circle (a biosphere for living things, with the Space Lifeform Capture Station) and Traveler's Crater, where the Traveler's spaceship rests.
- **Moontide Sea**: the lunar sea, with the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab beneath it and the ruins of Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory.
- **Dark Side of the Moon**: a high-security dragon base and launch silo. Lusalim's last laboratory is here, and the Moonheart Gap lies below.

People: No people live on the Frost Moon. Its inhabitants are kuuhenki, wildlife and machines. Small schools of kuuhenki live in the lunar sea. There are two "Mega Kuuhenki": Maggie, who is gentle and helps Columbina, and Ungie, who went berserk while overgrown with moonlit vines. Moonglow jellyfish and Moonglow Frostfin Whales also live there. The dragons' security machines still patrol. Columbina is its goddess but lives on Hiisi Island. She visits often, says she has to tidy the place up before she can receive guests, and hopes to bring willing kuuhenki there.

History: Canon, the second-born Moon Sister, ruled the Frost Moon. She and her sisters took turns over the night sky. Before the Heavenly Principles came, dragon researchers led by the pioneer Ibni-Belum settled the moon and built research facilities there. When Nibelung came back from the Abyss and made war on the Heavenly Principles, he imprisoned the hesitating Moon Sisters in the "moon's reflection" and began turning their moons into weapons. In return the Heavenly Principles shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and threw the Frost Moon, still intact, beyond the false sky. Cut off from Teyvat, Canon lasted for a time, long enough to lead Hyperborea's survivors to Hiisi Island, and then faded. Her worshippers, the Frostmoon Scions, prophesied that a new goddess would come. Columbina was born on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai some 400 to 500 years ago.

The Frost Moon is not dead. Skirk passed through the false sky centuries ago and saw two moons in lifeless pieces and a third that was whole and showed no life, though its will had not completely faded. While Columbina was trapped in the moon's reflection during the Archon Quest, she split herself into three parts across time. Her Trilune authority was hidden inside the Frost Moon. In Descending Moon (6.3) Sandrone's world-formula connected Columbina again. Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole dragged the real moon into Teyvat through the opening Dottore had torn, breaking the false sky there. The scattered parts of Columbina reunited and she descended as the Trilune Goddess. The shadowmoon became unnecessary and broke apart.

Atmosphere: Silent grey plains under a black sky, with Teyvat shining overhead. Bounding steps in low gravity. Pale-blue Archaeolune light runs through old dragon conduits, and huge machine-like structures that still work stand among the craters. The Moontide Sea glows and churns, and the far side looks like an armoured fortress. It feels lonely and very old, but not dead: kuuhenki drift by, terminals still hold the dragons' voices, and Columbina speaks of it as a second home.

Dangers: Archaeolune storms and the lunar sea cause exhaustion that can knock out anyone who stays in them; floating stones and storm-occlusion fields are the safe places. Gravity can change suddenly between weightless and crushing. The dragons' security systems still guard their bases: Pioneer Source Structures (self-destructing, patrolling and teleporting modules) and the elite Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network. The moon's local legends include a Prism Slime and the creature Mushteshir.

Travel: There are two known ways to reach the moon. Since True Moon, Columbina can open a path of blue moonlight from the Idol of the New Moon. It leads through murals to a crescent-shaped boat that sails to the moon, and she can teleport herself and others there. The second is the dragons' moon-bound ship at Dunanna Forward Station (Moon Gazing). Once there, travelers use the dragons' High-Speed Transit Lanes, which run on the ancient moon's power and double as waypoints.

Quests: - **True Moon** (Archon Quest, Song of the Welkin Moon Act VIII, 6.3): the moon is pulled into the false sky. In Welkin Moon's Homecoming, Columbina takes the Traveler to their spaceship on the moon.
- **Moon Gazing** (World Quest series, 6.7: Pioneers, Visitors From the Stars, Project Moongazer): unlocks the Frost Moon map and tells the Moongazers' story.
- **The Unmanned Vessel** (World Quest series, 6.7): three quests about the moon goddesses' vessel, with flashbacks of the Three Moon Goddesses.
- **Beneath the Lunar Sea** (World Quest, 6.7): leads into the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Frost Moon is back inside the false sky and visible over Teyvat again. Columbina reigns over it as the Trilune Goddess. She lives on Hiisi Island and travels freely between Nod-Krai and the moon. The shadowmoon is gone. The Moongazers' message was transmitted again in Moon Gazing. The Snezhnaya Archon Quest (7.0-7.1) adds nothing new about the moon.

After True Moon, Columbina gave back part of her power to Nod-Krai as kuuvahki. She said she could do so safely because the Frost Moon now lies inside the false sky and she is the Trilune Goddess. The Eternal Moon Marrow went to Lauma and the Iridescent Moon Marrow to Arlecchino. In Nasha Town, children now draw the "new" moon, which looks different from the old false one.

68.comment: Frost Moon: Project Moongazer and the Moongazers
68.content:
The Moongazers were dragon researchers on the Frost Moon. Ibni-Belum caught a mysterious deep-space signal and thought it came from Nibelung. Years after his death, Ungien flew the ship *Moongazer* to the signal's source and came back fused with an alien "Stellar Blackbody" that carried a warning and message of hope from a dying civilisation facing pitch-black annihilation. His wife Maagees-Geti began Project Moongazer to send that message on into space. Their student Lusalim stored the researchers' data in the moon's core, using creative power he borrowed from the Moon Goddesses, so that data-born messengers would be reborn again and again to repeat the transmission. In Moon Gazing (6.7) the black kuuhenki Eggie, the latest of these messengers, carried the transmission out from the Eye of Ibni-Belum with the Traveler, Paimon and Columbina. Columbina shielded the signal as it passed the false sky. Eggie's form dissolved afterwards.

One earlier transmission reached the Traveler and their sibling in deep space. Inspired, they replied with thanks and promised to visit once their own troubles were over. That reply sat sealed in the Eye's data until Eggie's broadcast unlocked it. Ibni-Belum himself disapproved of the later Moongazers and expelled Ungien as an oath-breaker; the title "first Moongazer" was given to him after his death. The messages are recorded in *Moongazer's Engraving*.

69.comment: Frost Moon: The Lunar Veil and the Moontide Sea
69.content:
Lusalim feared that broadcasting into space might draw hostile attention, so he and Maagees-Geti began Project Lunar Veil, a screen meant to hide the moon. It drew on Blackbody Matter, which reflects light and interacts with Archaeolune energy. A small test veil hid Ungien's Circle. Lusalim then built a generator large enough to cover the whole moon in his laboratory, but when the Heavenly Principles arrived, the laboratory and generator exploded. The blast left the Moontide Sea, a lunar sea dense with Archaeolune energy.

Lusalim then moved to a last laboratory on the Dark Side and finally handed his research to the Heavenly Principles. Columbina noticed how much a moon-hiding veil resembles the false sky. Canon does not say whether one led to the other.

70.comment: Frost Moon: The Dark Side Weapon and the Moonheart Gap
70.content: The hemisphere facing away from Teyvat was turned into a giant cannon powered by the moon's core, the Moonheart Gap. Nibelung built it after returning from the Abyss, as part of his war on the Heavenly Principles. Columbina calls it the masterpiece of a "Dragon Lord of Darkness" and says the Heavenly Principles defeated it, so it is no longer a threat. In Project Moongazer the Traveler and Columbina passed through its launch silo, disabled its still-active weapon core, beat its guardian (the "Warden of the Flame"), and reached the core. The core is the seat of the moon's will and the origin of Project Moongazer.

71.comment: Frost Moon: The Traveler's Spaceship on the Moon
71.content: The twins' spaceship crash-landed on Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai long ago. After the Cataclysm of five hundred years ago, the Heavenly Principles moved it to the Frost Moon, which was then beyond the false sky. With her Trilune authority, Columbina sensed it there. In Welkin Moon's Homecoming she took the Traveler to it in a great crater, since named Traveler's Crater. The flight logs show the ship had flown past Teyvat once thousands of years earlier without landing, travelled on for a very long time, and only later came back and crash-landed. The Traveler wonders whether their sibling left the ship during that first pass. They also took a matching outfit from a cabinet aboard.

72.comment: Frost Moon: Golden Hall and Prusmene
72.content: The Golden Hall in the Lunar Highlands keeps a song by Euthyphro, a boatman from Arcadia. He prays to Prusmene, Arcadia's name for the Frost Moon's goddess (Canon), and calls her the mistress of the Golden Hall. He says he steered her silver ship to carry pure souls up to the lunar palace above the clouds. He laments that the Primordial One on its eternal throne seeks to shroud the dreams of mortals with its own dream, and begs her to deliver him from the hands of his "dread master". The Unmanned Vessel world quests (6.7) feature the vessel of the Welkin Moon and include flashbacks of the Three Moon Goddesses; whether it is the same ship as Euthyphro's is not stated.

73.content: Archaeolune energy is the Frost Moon's ancient power, which the game describes as the primordial form of kuuvahki. Besides kuuvahki's own properties, it can act like phlogiston (programmable matter, an energy source and an information store), and like the Primordial Sea it has creative power, including the ability to make life. The dragons ran their machines on it. A body full of it becomes lighter and can leap, release bursts that change gravity on objects, or briefly dash in the form of a black kuuhenki. Columbina calls it "blue kuuvahki".

74.content:
Frostladen Machinery: Frostladen Machinery is a Domain of Blessing on Paha Isle in Nod-Krai, in the Maroon Basin. Its in-game description calls it a once-rumbling experimental outpost of colossal machines, built, used and then abandoned for the sake of ever grander visions. Now the goal feels close, the outpost's service is over and its devices sleep in cold silence.

It was added in Version 6.0 with the first Nod-Krai content. Challengers who defeat the dregs that dwell there can win artifacts.

Geography: Paha Isle is part of the Southern Isles. Before the Fatui came it was an unremarkable island known for sunset-coloured salt marshes and colonies of Tassel Jellies; everything changed when the heaviest fragment of a fallen moonstone crashed on its shores. The domain sits in the Maroon Basin on the island.

The giant devices are frost-covered and idle. The text says they were built to test certain principles or assumptions, and that once all conclusions were drawn the structures lost their reason to exist.

History: Many sacrifices and obstacles were met in building the machines, according to the domain text. Colossal devices were made and then abandoned, each serving a grander vision. The text gives no names or dates.

Paha Isle is the staging ground of the Fatui in Nod-Krai, operating through the high-tech Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau built over the fallen moonstone. This makes a Fatui experimental outpost plausible, but treat that as inference: the domain itself names no owner.

Dangers: The domain is guarded by Oprichniki infantry (Bombardiers, Medics, Grenadiers), a Cutting Edge All-Purpose Scout Landcruiser, and then the Wilderness Exile and Wilderness Hunter elites.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world events. It is a four-level Domain of Blessing recommended for Dendro, Electro and Hydro teams. Its Ley Line Disorder gives all party members 200 Elemental Mastery while the party's Moonsign Level is at least "Nascent Gleam". Artifact sets it drops: Night of the Sky's Unveiling, Silken Moon's Serenade, Resolution of Sojourner and Gambler.

Atmosphere: Frost on steel, stilled gears and the silence of something that once roared. Cold and abandoned, with no living caretakers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the outpost is described as at the end of its service. No later content in the pages read says anyone has reclaimed or dismantled it.

75.content: Paha Isle is an island in Nod-Krai's Southern Isles and the staging ground for Fatui personnel there, working through the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, a high-tech complex. Its expedition description says the heaviest fragment of the fallen moonstone crashed on its shores and changed it from an unremarkable island of salt marshes and Tassel Jellies. Its boss is the Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress.

76.content:
Frostmoon Enclave: The Frostmoon Enclave is the village-like home of the Frostmoon Scions, the moon-worshipping tribe of Nod-Krai, on forested Hiisi Island. It is a calm, book-filled place with a Grand Library, animals wandering freely, priestesses in quiet debate, and the Moonchanter Lauma at its centre. The Scions revere the Frost Moon and, since 6.3, the Moon Goddess herself lives among them.

The Scions avoid conflict with outsiders. Their doctrine treats kuuvahki as a sacred power, so using it for personal gain, including through kuuvahki devices, counts as blasphemy to many of them.

Geography: The Enclave lies on Hiisi Island, part of the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai. Under the Scions' stewardship much of the island remains untouched wilderness. Moonfall Silver and Frostlamp Flowers grow in the area, and the Moon Mirror, which once sealed a relic, stands on the island.

Silvermoon Hall, the hidden refuge where Columbina once rested, and the Sanctum of the Oathbearer, a pillar raised by Xiuhcoatl where Hyperborean survivors found refuge, are on the same island, along with the Light-Bathed Platform.

Places: The Grand Library is the Enclave's best-known building, and its meeting point stands inside. Shelves are uneven in height, like a flight of stairs, and are set up for reading undisturbed by moonlight. Cushions and perches have been put out so visiting animals can rest. A drum set stands in the open: striking its five drums summons animal companions if Lauma or Columbina is in the party (a gameplay interaction).

Lauma has been collecting the Scions' scattered texts, relics and records here; a huge, uninspiring running chronicle of the sayings and doings of past Moonchanters sits on a bottom shelf and doubles as a footstool. The plain carved Lunar Semblance, recovered from the Moon Mirror, is kept in the library as a relic that matters to the Scions but has little monetary value.

People: Lauma, the Moonchanter, leads the Scions. Priestesses include Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar; Zirnytsia is an acolyte, and Krodo, Ossian and Reetta are adherents. Others in the settlement include Ina, Kari, Mirsky and Wecksell, and the traveling merchant Rebane. Verna appears on the Enclave's list as a priestess but is ranked an acolyte on the Scions page.

Verna is trying to change the Scions' view of kuuvahki devices. Ehrnrooth has been shelving the library's books and, mildly puzzled, follows Lauma's unusual instructions, such as making cushions and stands for visiting animals. Men of the tribe cannot become acolytes or priests.

Governance: The Moonchanter leads. Beneath her are priestesses, acolytes (who have passed an exam on hymns and blessings) and adherents. The role replaced the earlier Archpriestess, abolished about 500 years ago by Aila, the first Moonchanter.

Culture: The Scions are quiet, benevolent and pacifist toward outsiders, appear to abstain from meat, and revere the Frost Moon. They remember the dead goddess Canon as Huurrekuutar and the present goddess as Kuutar. Their home is shaped by Aila's reform: no great towers or fortresses, reverence for nature and kindness to outsiders.

An emblem of a moon and deer carved in silver fir, called the Shadow of the Frostmoon, marks the Enclave, and the prayer Aila left is said to be etched in every Scion's memory. Tea is brewed in the Scions' own way, which most outsiders dislike; the Fatui's Sandrone learned it as an act of respect.

History: Before the reforms, the Scions' home on Hiisi Island held towers, fortresses and temples. About 500 years ago Aila, the first Moonchanter, had them torn down, because she thought isolation fed delusion. The pillar of the Sanctum of the Oathbearer was the one structure she spared. The wiki presumes the Enclave stands where those ruins were.

Under Archpriestess Lovia the Scions ran a eugenic Sacred Heir Project and committed murders in its name; Aila ended it, killed Lovia, and sealed the evidence in a separate court. The Scions later took the newborn Kuutar as their goddess but, as she realised, cared more for wishes granted than for her. The Fatui later pressed the island, hunting Columbina under the Palestar Edict, until Dottore was defeated.

Atmosphere: Stillness, silver-blue light, the smell of herbal tea and old paper, and the constant low conversation of animals only Lauma fully understands. Evenings feel unhurried. Children are curious about Columbina; the older generation is shy.

Dangers: Few are recorded. Before Dottore's defeat the Fatui threatened the island; since then the main annoyance is mischief, like the weasel thief who keeps digging holes looking for treasure.

Travel: Hiisi Island lies off the main Nod-Krai landmass in the Southern Isles; the meeting point inside the Grand Library lets the Traveler help develop the Enclave. Quests here include Blessings of the Frost Moon, Lauma's anecdotes and the Tea Party invitation with Sandrone.

Quests: Blessings of the Frost Moon (6.0 world quest) unlocks the Enclave and its meeting point: Lauma and the Traveler retrieve the Lunar Semblance from the Moon Mirror. A Small Overture (6.7) has Lauma and Sandrone share tea in the Enclave and begin a careful reconciliation between Scions and Fatui.

In the Lauma anecdote The Gathering she pretends to nap, with a cat in on the joke, and offers the Traveler fresh fruit and her blessing as Moonchanter.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Enclave is at peace. Columbina lives here among the Scions, Lauma still leads them, and the Fatui have apologised.

After Dottore's defeat, Columbina took Lauma's invitation to live with the Scions instead of hiding in Silvermoon Hall. The older Scions are timid around her, the children curious; she asks to be treated as a person, not a goddess. Sandrone apologised for the Fatui's treatment of the Scions, and the Palestar Edict is revoked.

77.comment: Frostmoon Enclave: Grand Library of the Enclave
77.content: The library holds Scion texts and relics. Lauma retrieved the Lunar Semblance, a plain, crudely carved statue sealed in the Moon Mirror by a previous Moonchanter, with the Traveler's help; she values it as proof that several old documents are reliable and says her job is to dig up stories, verify them and share them with people. She asked the Traveler to bring any texts about the Scions found on their travels so she can copy them. A weasel thief who helped now begs her for the next treasure hunt.

78.comment: Frostmoon Enclave: Aila's Reform of the Scions
78.content: Aila, the first Moonchanter, ended the Archpriestess's rule about 500 years ago and ordered the old walls, towers, fortresses and temples torn down, arguing that long isolation nurtured fleeting ambitions and hollow delusions. She wanted reverence for nature and kindness toward outsiders to define the tribe instead, so that there would be no second Lovia. Lovia's name was removed from the record; only priestesses and above know it.

79.content:
Golden Hall (also: the great golden house, The Boatman's Song-House): The Golden Hall is a small site in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. Its map marker reads like an invitation to board a silver ship and return to the great golden house, and its readable text, the Chanson of the Boatman, is a prayer written by a boatman who served a night goddess.

The viewpoint is called The Boatman's Song-House. An elite Tangled Vines enemy, Frostnight Scion, guards the area.

Places: A subarea of the Lunar Highlands. A High-Speed Transit Lane leads there, apparently unlocked by an exploration objective called To Quell the Storm.

Culture: The Chanson of the Boatman is a hymn from a man named Euthyphro of Arcadia, the eternal holy city. He prays to the ever-blessed goddess Prusmene, mother of the silver shuttle, to preserve him and bring him inspiration. He calls her ancient mother of the night, mistress of the Golden Hall, and says she guided his vessel many times as he carried unsullied souls to the lunar palace above the clouds, letting mortals sleep and dream dreams their own.

Yet it is a final night: he fears the eternal throne in the heavens, the Primordial One, a world-shaking lord who forges the bones of the earth and means to cover human dreams with its own, so that mortals live without beginning or end in dreamless rest. He begs deliverance from his dread master, saying he ushered the souls and steered the silver ship for her sake, and asks that he not sink beneath the silver tree to be sullied by dust.

Atmosphere: The site's mood comes from its text: a night-goddess hymn, a silver ship and a promise of rest set against fear of a dreamless end.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is open. The wiki lists a Golden Hall quest category but names no quest in what was read.

80.comment: Golden Hall: Chanson of the Boatman
80.content: A prayer written by Euthyphro of Arcadia, a boatman who carried souls to the lunar palace for the goddess Prusmene, fearing the Primordial One's plan for a dreamless world and begging to be delivered.

81.content:
Hiisi Island: Hiisi Island is a forested island in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai (accessible from 6.0). It is the home of the Frostmoon Scions, a religious sect devoted to the Moon Goddess, and under their care much of it is untouched wilderness. Its Frostmoon Enclave and the sealed Sanctum of the Oathbearer are the heart of their faith.

Its expedition description calls it a mysterious island of ancient forest where Moon Goddess worship endures, and says legends tell of descendants of the golden realm, guided by moonlight, who travelled countless miles to find refuge here.

Geography: A wooded island south of Pohjola, one of three that make up the Southern Isles with Lempo Isle and Paha Isle. Its subareas are the Frostmoon Enclave, the Scions' dwelling place, and the Light-Bathed Platform, a high plateau where the Sanctum of the Oathbearer lies. Local specialties: Frostlamp Flower and Moonfall Silver.

The island's boss is the Frostnight Herra.

Places: Frostmoon Enclave: home of the Scions, with a Grand Library that holds its Meeting Point. Light-Bathed Platform: a plateau with the Sanctum of the Oathbearer (also called the Court of the First Edict), sealed five hundred years ago and unsealed in the world quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past.

The Enclave is thought to occupy the remains of an older Scion complex of towers, fortresses and temples that Aila razed five hundred years ago to reform the faith. The Sanctum is reached from the base of the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper.

People: The Frostmoon Scions: priestesses such as Ehrnrooth, Rahetar, Sarakka and Verna; adherents such as Krodo, Ossian, Reetta and Kukkia; the acolyte Zirnytsia; and others including Ina, Kari, Mirsky, Wecksell and Eveliina. Rebane is a traveling merchant. Their leader is Lauma, the current Moonchanter.

Verna guides the Traveler in Echoes of an Unfinished Past. In the centuries after the fall of Hyperborea a prophecy arose among them that the Moon Goddess would one day return.

Governance: The Scions are led by the Moonchanter, with priestesses guiding rites. After the fall of Hyperborea a line of Archpriestesses issued strict decrees; one set found in the Sanctum was signed by Saredne, the thirteenth Archpriestess, and another by Lovia.

Culture: Worship of the Moon Goddess: the Scions revere the Frost Moon, the current goddess Kuutar and her predecessor Canon (Huurrekuutar). Their ancient rites used kuuvahki and a body of hymns called Runo, preserved in part in the book Hymns of the Far North.

Hyperborean teachings emphasised reason over sentiment; decrees in the Sanctum forbid marrying outlanders or those outside the faith, and speak of a prophesied sovereign who would one day awaken the sacred Sampo Mill. Hymns and prayer songs honour many figures, including the Heavenly Principles, the Four Shades, Anacharsis and Saarelainen. Statues of the New Moon dedicated to Columbina were set up across Nod-Krai by the Scions. People elsewhere in Nod-Krai find the Scions strange and do not approach them (per Helka).

History: After the Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, Canon guided the survivors to Hiisi Island and died. They found refuge at a pillar made by Xiuhcoatl, which became the Sanctum of the Oathbearer, and kept their rites although their goddess did not answer. Five hundred years ago Aila, the first Moonchanter, reformed the faith, tearing down the old insular towers and temples. The Sanctum itself was sealed five hundred years ago.

Aila's notes, found in the Sanctum, record that she lied when Solovei asked if she felt any hate, as Lovia and her own sister Alia had lied before her, and that she saw no reason to burden him with her suffering. The Traveler opens the Sanctum with Verna's help in the quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past.

Atmosphere: Silver light through old trees, quiet paths, ruined stone from older temples, the drum set in the Enclave and a feeling of watching and waiting. Peaceful, a little secretive.

Dangers: The Frostnight Herra is the island's boss; it can enter a state in which it absorbs an element. The wiki lists no other special hazards.

Travel: The island is one of the Southern Isles. The Enclave has a Meeting Point at the Grand Library; the Light-Bathed Platform is up in the hills.

Quests: Echoes of an Unfinished Past (world quest, Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle chapter): starting at the Light-Bathed Platform with Verna, the Traveler opens the sealed Sanctum and follows the Moonlane to the Court of the First Edict, where they find Aila's sword.

The chapter requires earlier quests: For a Green Island..., Gift of the Mirage, The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, and The Tale of the Gate Stone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island remains the Scions' home, open to explore, and the Sanctum has been unsealed.

Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the island.

82.content:
The home of the Frostmoon Scions, where they gather to listen to the teachings of moonlight. A drum set in the Enclave summons animal companions when Lauma or Columbina is in the party.

The ruins of towers, fortresses and temples here were torn down by Aila, five hundred years ago, so that the Scions would no longer be cut off from the world.

83.comment: Hiisi Island: Sanctum of the Oathbearer
83.content:
The Scions' place of refuge after Hyperborea, a pillar made by Xiuhcoatl, sealed five hundred years ago and opened in Echoes of an Unfinished Past. Inside are Aila's private notes and decrees of the Hyperborean Archpriestesses that govern marriage, rites and the Sampo Mill.

The decrees show a rigid, secretive order that guarded its bloodline and forbade emotion in recorded rites.

84.content: The tribe of Moon Goddess followers who are descendants of Hyperborea and live on Hiisi Island. They revere Kuutar, the Moon Maiden, who succeeded the late Canon. Lauma is the current Moonchanter.

85.content:
Idol of the New Moon (also: Statue of Kuutar): The Idol of the New Moon is a large statue on Hiisi Island, in the Light-Bathed Platform area, depicting the Moon Maiden Kuutar. According to the quests Where the Moon Rises and Hidden in the Shadows, it was carved five hundred years ago by Aila, the Moonchanter, from ore rich in kuuvahki.

Eveliina describes it as showing Lady Kuutar's original form. During The Homebound Moon the modern Frostmoon Scions add a pair of wings to the statue to represent their goddess's newfound freedom and autonomy.

Geography: It stands on Hiisi Island's Light-Bathed Platform. It is distinct from the many smaller Statues of the New Moon that unlock the map; this large idol exists only on Hiisi Island.

History: Aila carved it five hundred years ago from kuuvahki-rich ore, and Eveliina says it shows Lady Kuutar's original form.

In The Homebound Moon (part of the Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles), the Traveler meets Columbina in Silvermoon Hall, then Lauma, reports back to Columbina, and the quest's last step is to head to the statue of Kuutar. Afterwards the statue appears with wings.

Culture: For the Frostmoon Scions, the statue stands for the Moon Maiden whom they serve, and the added wings are a deliberate sign that she is free to choose her own path.

Atmosphere: A large idol on the Light-Bathed Platform, bathed in light, with wings in its present form.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the idol stands with wings, if The Homebound Moon has been completed.

86.content:
Interstice of the Nearing Moon (also: Engraving, the orbital positioning facility): The Interstice of the Nearing Moon is a hidden instance reached by riding a Moonlane, a path of moonlight, from a kuuhenki behind the Idol of the New Moon on Hiisi Island. In the World Quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past (6.0) it appears as the strange route Verna leads the Traveler and Paimon down while trying to break the seal on the Court of the First Edict. It is in fact an old orbital positioning facility of the dragons, which they call Engraving.

When the visitors approach, a draconic voice wakes it, checks their identity and matches them against known parameters.

Geography: An instance of floating pillars over concentric tracks, with Moonlane-like paths. Moving the pillars onto the right tracks lifts the seal, after which golden light runs down to a crevice at the base of the central pillar.

The only way down from the first platform is to slide the three floating pillars over the innermost, middle and outermost tracks; Verna compares the arrangement to lining up the grooves of a lock.

History: The Moongazer Ibni-Belum built it long ago in what was then called Nephilheim as Engraving, an advanced orbital adjustment and payload guidance system. A storage log by the dragon recorder Nu-ur-Gestug records the second phase of retrofitting: a data storage array was mounted, and downlink tests from the lunar terminal to the surface node exceeded expectations. The node was meant as a backup so that research could be recovered if the primary array on the moon were ever destroyed.

The log appears in the Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index at the Nuur Stone Circle (available after the quest Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu), and says the original Engraving was reinforced as well.

People: Verna, a self-proclaimed priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, leads the Traveler and Paimon in, believing they are inside a sanctum. Other Scions (Ehrnrooth, Krodo and Rahetar) hunt the intruders after the seal breaks.

Quests: In Echoes of an Unfinished Past the Traveler throws special fragments at a floating rock to open the way, follows the Moonlane, and enters the Interstice. After the pillars are set, the sealed Court of the First Edict opens; the quest goes on in the Sanctum of the Oathbearer, where a lingering image of the first Moonchanter Aila appears, and the sword Moonweaver's Dawn can be found.

The voice's authorisation message changes with the player's progress in Natlan: it welcomes an unnamed Master if the quests were not completed, the sovereign ruler of Natlantea after one Natlan quest, and King Xiuhcoatl after a later one. Before that the voice reports only a moderate match with the parameters of the Dragonlord of Flame. These are lines of the 6.0 quest as the wiki records them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Interstice is reachable and dormant after the quest. Its connection to the later Moongazer story is by name and builder only.

87.comment: Interstice of the Nearing Moon: Engraving
87.content: Engraving is the dragon term for the orbital positioning facility, an Advanced Orbital Adjustment and Payload Management Guidance System by Ibni-Belum, today called the Interstice of the Nearing Moon. A backup data node was installed in it by the recorder Nu-ur-Gestug.

88.comment: Interstice of the Nearing Moon: Moonlane
88.content: A path of moonlight formed by a kuuhenki. Riding the Moonlane behind the Idol of the New Moon leads into the Interstice and, in Echoes of an Unfinished Past, onward to the Court of the First Edict.

89.content:
Kalag Guarding Grounds: The Kalag Guarding Grounds is a security area in Ungien's Circle, the biosphere on the Frost Moon. It is named for Kalag, the moon's Security Chief. A Local Legend automaton, Mushteshir, can be fought here after two combat challenges.

A terminal at the back of the room carries an order concerning the Stellar Blackbody: all seven Kings have been informed, and to protect the biosphere, the administrative authority of the researchers Ungien and Maagees is temporarily suspended. Objections are to go to Kalag, who holds supreme clearance.

Places: The area has a combat arena and, at the very back of the room, the terminal. Mushteshir, "The Pioneer That Gazes at the Stars", is a Hydro automaton of the Secret Source family; after the first visit it enters the arena immediately on respawn.

People: Kalag (Security Chief, supreme clearance) is the authority named here. Lusalim's research log in Maagees's Greenhouse complains that Kalag took control of the biosphere and blamed the loss of control over the Moonlit Vines on Blackbody contamination caused by Maagees's research.

In his own lab logs Lusalim hopes Kalag's force does not learn of the research and notes it has no access to his laboratory yet; he adds that the Eye of Ibni-Belum team chose to stand with Maagees even against Kalag's force.

History: The suspension order shows the Kings were told of the Stellar Blackbody and that the biosphere's safety was the stated reason. Kalag's security force then took control of Ungien's Circle, according to Lusalim's log, and the Project Lunar Veil wiki page says this forced Lusalim to continue Project Lunar Veil elsewhere, in the Moontide Sea.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned as of 7.1, with the Local Legend as its only active occupant.

90.content:
Kipumaki Cliff (also: Kipumaki): Kipumaki Cliff is a cliff in northern Nod-Krai, perpetually shrouded in dark clouds. It is said to hold a sealed, undying fiend: the Scourge of Endless Decay, an Abyssal entity that Aila (the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions) and Solovei (the Torchforger) subdued here 500 years ago. The area has been a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity ever since, and the Lightkeepers watch it from Cliffwatch Camp.

Its name echoes Finnish myth: kipumaki means "pain hill", the home of a spirit who takes human pain upon herself. The cliff belongs to Ashveil Peak in the north of Nod-Krai.

The 6.3 quest When War Songs Rise (Nightingale's Song, Act II) is the cliff's defining story: the seal failed, and Illuga's squad and the Traveler had to rebuild it and kill what it held.

Geography: A windswept cliff under permanent dark cloud, with a waterfall in its south, a clifftop camp and a cave system beneath it. Local specialties include Winter Icelea, and Oath Lanterns, Mandragora and other kuuvahki sources are scattered across the slopes.

Beneath the cliff lies the Chasm of Endless Decay, the cave where the Scourge was imprisoned and where Illuga later followed it. The sealing array's focal points are Verdant Crests set on the cliff face; in the quest they respond to the Silver Lampwick the Lightkeepers carry. Cliffwatch Camp, the Lightkeepers' outpost, stands near a lighthouse and keeps a cemetery for fallen Lightkeepers.

History: 500 years ago the Scourge of Endless Decay, an Abyssal entity that had helped Rotwang try to open the False Sky to the Abyss through the Pillar of Embla, was banished and sealed here by Aila and Solovei, with Alia's help, using a sealing array. The site became a standing source of Wild Hunt activity, so the Lightkeepers founded Cliffwatch Camp to monitor it.

Three years before the present day a surge of Wild Hunt activity under the cliffs caused a catastrophe: many Lightkeepers and civilians died, among them Captain Olsson, and the monsters spread out beneath the cliffs before they could be cleared. The camp was rebuilt and the fight went on. Illuga, who rushed back to report to Nikita, and Rollon, who answered the emergency order, both recall that day.

Dangers: Wild Hunt creatures, Abyssal Riftlines and Evil Eyes. The cliff has a special climate, The Wild Hunt Lurks...: staying in it builds an Abyssal Decay gauge (a game mechanic) that drains HP once full and narrows vision, unless the traveller shelters near Oath Lanterns or other kuuvahki sources.

The heavy cloud limits sight, and the standing Abyssal presence keeps the cliff dangerous even after the 6.3 victory.

Atmosphere: Dark cloud overhead, lanterns glowing where kuuvahki is strong, and a camp run with the discipline of people who have buried comrades here.

Travel: Reached through Cliffwatch Camp. Outsiders are not casually welcome: when Anleifr meets the Traveler there his first reaction is that this is the front line against the Wild Hunt and they should not be present.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the seal has been restored and the Scourge of Endless Decay defeated, but Wild Hunt pressure on the cliff has not ended and the Lightkeepers still hold the line.

Bjorn died in the 6.3 fighting and has a grave at Cliffwatch Camp.

91.comment: Kipumaki Cliff: Chasm of Endless Decay
91.content: The cave beneath Kipumaki Cliff where Aila and Solovei imprisoned the Scourge of Endless Decay. In When War Songs Rise it is the scene of the final battle between the Scourge and Illuga's squad with the Traveler, who destroy it with the Spiralblade.

92.content: The Lightkeepers' outpost watching Kipumaki Cliff, near a lighthouse. Its cemetery holds graves for Lightkeepers who fell on the cliff, including Veyde, Olsson, Chernov, Filaev, Pieris Asebov, Shonokovych and, after the 6.3 quest, Bjorn. One grave is an empty tomb prepared in advance for a future Lightkeeper named Patolichev.

93.content:
Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau (also: Design Bureau, Experimental Design Bureau): The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau is the Fatui's enormous steel-and-stone research and arms complex on Paha Isle, in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai. The Expedition text calls it a colossal structure whose bulk is an unsubtle declaration of power and control. It studies kuuvahki, the moon-derived energy found only in Nod-Krai, and co-developed war machines, notably the Landcruisers, with Snezhnaya's Armory Palace. Sandrone (Marionette) oversaw its construction and ran it during the Nod-Krai crisis; Poruchik Raskolnikov keeps order there. Locals, especially the Frostmoon Scions, resent it.

It stands as a deliberate challenge to nature itself, in the words of the in-game description. It is guarded by Oprichniki troops and automated Landcruisers, and its upper levels are a maze of dormitories, archives, a disposal workshop and a command platform.

Geography: The Bureau fills much of Paha Isle, once an unremarkable island known for salt marshes and Tassel Jellies until the heaviest fragment of the fallen moonstone crashed on its shores. Its levels (the map lists Top, Middle, Lower and Bottom levels, a Southern Zone and a Disposal Workshop) climb up from the water. South Harbor, with a console that starts one of its quests, is one way in.

Beneath it lies the classified Underground Research Center. Certain parts of the Bureau are Strong Kuuvahki Environments: while inside, the player is in a kuuvahki-empowered state whose polarity (red or blue) follows the environment.

Places: The Bureau is a layered compound rather than one room. Known areas include the South Harbor intake, containers moved inside by lift, a dormitory for the garrison, archives where the Cognoscenti chest was taken, the Disposal Workshop where defective products are destroyed, a command platform above it, and the highest point of the complex where Raskolnikov waits. Inside, the Disposal Workshop has moving "destruction modules" that can crush even a Landcruiser.

The Underground Research Center holds jars of kuuvahki, research records and barrier generators. Its Secret Research viewpoint is described as a classified underground Fatui facility with experiments on kuuvahki. It gathers data from three collection hubs on Paha Isle to research high-density energy barrier generation. A barrier there can be dropped only if all its generators verify an ID card within a time limit.

People: Sandrone (the Seventh of the Fatui Harbingers, also called Marionette) ran the Bureau during the Nod-Krai crisis, with her automaton Pulonia as her companion until Dottore destroyed him. Poruchik Raskolnikov, a lieutenant from Novokitezhgrad trained by Police Chief Stalanov, maintains order and efficiency; the lower-ranked Oprichniki dislike him for strict rules such as a ban on drinking parties. Rank-and-file Fatui (Oprichniki troopers, medics, grenadiers and cannoneers) staff it, among them Podporuchik Kholodov, who leads the guard against intruders at the Underground Research Center.

Dottore, Second of the Harbingers, was said to be present at the Bureau's opening and stayed in Nod-Krai alongside Sandrone, but see the uncertainties on his actual role. The Armory Palace's engineers contributed to the Landcruiser designs. In the Song of the Welkin Moon quests, Fevroniya and Ozerov guard its entrance.

Governance: Fatui chain of command applies: a Harbinger (Sandrone) at the top, officers such as Raskolnikov below, Oprichniki troops beneath them. Raskolnikov's orders come from superiors; he describes his own role as guarding the Bureau and ensuring its efficient operation, and he admits that handing over the Cognoscenti was insubordination. Staff grumble that the higher-ups do not like him either.

History: The Fatui came to Nod-Krai under the Tsaritsa's Palestar Edict, the highest of commands, to retrieve the defector Columbina. The Harbingers were dispatched there; Sandrone oversaw construction of the Bureau over ancient moon ruins, which brought the Fatui into conflict with the Frostmoon Scions, who revere the moons. Helka remarks that the Fatui brought many building materials without explaining their plans. Most Harbingers then returned to Snezhnaya; Sandrone later says Arlecchino went back once work on the facility was completed, and Dottore and Sandrone stayed on.

Kuuvahki research gave the Fatui barrier generators and war machines. The Landcruiser, an autonomous "armed ship that cruises on land", was first engineered by the Armory Palace's finest engineers and is now deployed across Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. The Super-Heavy Landrover "Type Drzislav" was jointly developed by the Armory Palace and the Bureau; the in-game description says it was originally built for civilian heavy transport (drills and cutters) before later models were militarised. The Cyclic Military Kuuvahki Core, an ascension material, comes from these machines.

Culture: Fatui life here is regimented and a little absurd. The garrison grumbles about reports, pay, hidden savings and an unpopular officer. Locals see the complex as an invader's fortress. The wider Nod-Krai attitude is hostile to Fatui rule, though some rank-and-file Fatui, like those who helped in the Dottore crisis, prove decent.

Dangers: Oprichniki patrols, Landcruisers and, at the upper levels, an alarm system that calls reinforcements. The Disposal Workshop's destruction modules and Strong Kuuvahki Environment zones damage intruders; the Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress is a normal boss on Paha Isle.

Atmosphere: Cold iron and stone, steady machine noise, alarms and ventilation. Corridors lined with crates, chests, dormitories and archives. A bureaucratic military feel: stamped forms, strict schedules and officers who value precision. Outside, the sunset salt marshes of Paha Isle make a strange contrast with the fortress.

Travel: Paha Isle belongs to the Southern Isles; South Harbor is one way in. Intruders can hide in cargo containers; upper levels open as the World Quest The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot progresses. Using the Moonstriders and the Special Lightning Storm lets one jump to the top level.

Quests: World Quests set here: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot and Priorities First (with its follow-up Priorities First: Afterword). Special Operation, part of the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest, begins here; Just Like Old Times, a Tea Party quest, uses the top level.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bureau remains a Fatui facility in Nod-Krai, now with a tense peace with the Frostmoon Scions.

Sandrone died in the crisis, was revived in Fontaine and has since returned to her duties in Snezhnaya, so who now oversees the Bureau at Harbinger level is not stated in the sources read. Raskolnikov can still be fought there as a Local Legend, and Sandrone holds a tea party with Arlecchino, Tartaglia and Columbina on its top level in Just Like Old Times.

94.comment: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot
94.content:
In this World Quest the Traveler and Paimon hide in a supply container and are carried into the Bureau. They are mistaken for accomplices of Netochka, a thief hunting the Proof of the Cognoscenti, a treasure tied to the legendary thief Reed Miller. Together they slip through the dormitory and archives to the Disposal Workshop. Raskolnikov, who knows Netochka from Novokitezhgrad, springs a trap and fights with Landcruisers. After defeating him on the top level, the Traveler receives the goblet Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication. Raskolnikov loses willingly and warns that a repeat intrusion will meet his full strength. Netochka leaves, calling herself the Traveler's rival.

Raskolnikov says the treasure belongs to the Tsaritsa and that bringing it to Snezhnograd could earn promotion, then reveals that keeping it at the Bureau only invites thieves. Netochka's feelings about him and her father, Police Chief Stalanov, are tangled: she says Stalanov cares for his cases and promising juniors, and she once admired Raskolnikov. Hidimbi in Nasha Town had given her clues, which Netochka later suspects were not meant only for her.

95.content: The Poruchik (lieutenant) in charge of the Bureau's order. He wears the inverted-colour uniform of an Oprichniki Fireblade Shock Trooper and holds to rules and efficiency. He respects strength (Stalanov and the Traveler) and has contempt for people he regards as lucky fools. His character entry holds the full detail.

96.comment: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau: Underground Research Center and Priorities First
96.content: Entered by defeating a Cutting Edge All-Purpose Storm Landcruiser, the Center is a classified Fatui lab filled with jars of kuuvahki and records on barrier generation. In Priorities First, the Traveler retrieves data cassettes, submits them and escapes Podporuchik Kholodov's guards. The sounds that follow lead to a white Weasel Thief that had been stealing from Fatui and from Paimon, tracked down by Jurva, Maisie and Mikko.

97.comment: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau: Landcruisers and the Armory Palace
97.content: Landcruisers are automated war machines first engineered by the Armory Palace, which is run by Sandrone and based in Glupov in Snezhnaya. The Bureau co-developed the newer generations, including the Super-Heavy Landrover. The wiki lists close-combat, force-recon and cutting-edge variants. Landcruisers are common in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, and they were repaired inside the Bureau by Freminet's help in the Song of the Welkin Moon quests.

98.content:
Lempo Isle: Lempo Isle is one of the three Southern Isles of Nod-Krai, accessible from 6.0. It is home to Nasha Town, the region's main port and commercial centre, and to the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop where the young inventor Aino works. Its settlements are crowded, industrial and run by no single authority.

The island also has the glowing Blue Amber Lake, the beaches of Starsand Shoal where the Traveler and their sibling's ship landed, and the Eye of Kratti, a crystal-tree island over an old whirlpool.

Geography: Lempo Isle is one of the Southern Isles (a group also called the Lempo Isles), south of Pohjola, together with Hiisi Island and Paha Isle. Nasha Town sits on the coast; the Craftshop lies inland; the Blue Amber Lake sits on a raised plateau between the north and south parts of Barrowmoss Barrens; Starsand Shoal is the western beach, and the Eye of Kratti is a small island off the coast.

Local specialties: Frostlamp Flower and Portable Bearing. Bosses include the Knuckle Duckle and the Radiant Moonfly. The Southern Isles with Piramida are the most populated parts of Nod-Krai.

Places: Nasha Town: seaside settlement, Nod-Krai's main port and commercial centre, built mostly of scrap metal with cargo rails across the sky and kuuvahki-powered machines on every corner. Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop: workshop begun by Aino. Blue Amber Lake: highland lake of crystal blue with bonfires on the shore. Starsand Shoal: western beaches. Eye of Kratti: island with a crystalline tree.

Nasha Town hosts an Adventurers' Guild branch (Katheryne, receptionist; Sarin, branch master), the Curatorium of Secrets, Mimisbrunnr Books, a branch of Northland Bank, Nuts 'N' Nuts, the Rossum Workshop, the restaurant Speranza, the Flagship and the Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse. The Craftshop's Meeting Point stands near its centre. Blue Amber Lake's unique climate makes it glow at all hours and is the only place Stellafruit grows; Papa Wrench's scribbled notes lie there. The Eye of Kratti holds the wreck of the ship Atlas and others.

People: Nasha Town's locals include merchants, sailors, engineers, harbor officers, Fatui soldiers, Ratniki, and adherents of the Frostmoon Scions (for example Kantor and Lyylikki).
