Aino and her creation Ineffa are associated with the Craftshop; the shop's NPCs include Bozena, Lalli, Zaitseva and, after Problem-Sorting Robot, Chard Lombro.

Others in the town include Iratxa (a Marechaussee Phantom agent), Liouba (a researcher from the Fontaine Research Institute), Zompaynco (an investigator for the Saurian Relics Association), Kaunea (a fashion consultant), Golitsyna (who owns a place called Mead-Boy), Hjerson (a detective) and Urwa, representing Lord Sangemah Bay. At the Eye of Kratti the Traveler meets Ilmari.

Governance: Nasha Town has no official governing body. Several factions hold influence: the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets, Speranza and the Fatui. The wiki says this makes it both a paradise of freedom and a lawless jungle.

Culture: Nod-Krai's limited resources shape the town: it is mostly built of scrap, industrialised and noisy. People from all over Teyvat gather in Nod-Krai, and it has a reputation as an 'Elysium'. The Craftshop began as Aino's small workspace to research the 'World's Best Krumkake Machine' and grew into a renowned machine workshop after her many inventions and Ineffa's birth.

Aino is a child prodigy and an orphan who regards her creations and screws as her family. A krumkake is a Norwegian cookie, per the wiki's etymology note.

History: Starsand Shoal's description says that when the dark disaster engulfed Nod-Krai many heroes made their last stand on its sands. The Eye of Kratti was once a whirlpool, known as a forbidden zone for turbulent water, monster rumours and lost souls. A few years before the present the ship Atlas sank there with the Proof of the Cognoscenti aboard.

The Frostmoon Scions told Libuse the Atlas was cursed by something at sea. Soon after, a crystalline tree sprouted from the whirlpool and made a small island; rocks fell from the sky, shiny things appeared, and a friend of the NPC Ilmari heard strange singing. In the quest Whisper Beneath the Waves the Traveler and Paimon follow the ghosts of the Atlas's crew to the tree's roots, revive it with kuuvahki, and recover the lost Proof of the Cognoscenti.

Atmosphere: Nasha Town: scrap-metal walls, cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki machines on every corner. The Craftshop: a busy machine workshop. Blue Amber Lake: quiet, starlit bonfires on the shore. Starsand Shoal: whispering waves over a battlefield of heroes.

Dangers: Nod-Krai as a whole is harsh: people suspected of holding a lot of Mora are painted as targets, and the Fatui have a presence in the town. The wiki lists no further hazards for the island beyond its bosses. Bosses include the Knuckle Duckle and the Radiant Moonfly. The Eye of Kratti is a forbidden zone with a haunted history.

Travel: Nasha Town is Nod-Krai's main port and has a Bulletin Board. Hiisi Island and Paha Isle are the neighbouring Southern Isles.

Quests: Quests and series set here include Whisper Beneath the Waves (Eye of Kratti), The Tale-Telling Heart (Blue Amber Lake), Problem-Sorting Robot (Craftshop). Details of those quests were not read for this entry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lempo Isle is open to explore; Nasha Town remains Nod-Krai's trading hub.

Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the island.

99.content: Nod-Krai's main port and commercial centre, built from scrap metal with rails across the sky. It has no official government; the Voynich Guild, Curatorium of Secrets, Speranza and the Fatui all hold influence, making it both free and lawless. It has an Adventurers' Guild branch.

100.content: A workshop begun by Aino to build the 'World's Best Krumkake Machine'. Following her many inventions and the birth of Ineffa, it became a renowned machine workshop.

101.content: A small island with a crystalline tree at its centre, over a former whirlpool. The ship Atlas sank here a few years before the present with the Proof of the Cognoscenti. The quest Whisper Beneath the Waves revives the tree with kuuvahki and recovers the lost object.

102.content: A highland lake of crystalline blue on a plateau between the north and south of Barrowmoss Barrens. Its climate gives it a constant glow, and Stellafruit grows nowhere else. Papa Wrench's notes about his life after his supposed death aboard the Fortunate One lie near it.

103.content:
Light-Bathed Platform: The Light-Bathed Platform is a subarea of Hiisi Island, the home of the Frostmoon Scions in Nod-Krai. It is the final destination of the pilgrimage route where wishes are offered to Lady Kuutar, the Moon Maiden, before the great Idol of the New Moon. A sealed sanctum, the Court of the First Edict, lies beneath a huge edifice nearby.

The Idol is a statue of Kuutar in her original form, said to have been carved by the first Moonchanter, Aila, 500 years ago from kuuvahki-rich ore. Two Scions look after the platform: the acolyte Eveliina and the adherent Kukkia.

The platform appears in the world quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past, which opens the sealed Court, and later in the 6.3 quest The Homebound Moon, in which wings are added to the Idol.

Geography: An elevated, open stone platform on Hiisi Island overlooking the Frostmoon Enclave camp below, with the Idol of the New Moon at its heart and Moonfall Silver, a local specialty, gathered nearby. Its map level connects to the Sanctum of the Oathbearer.

A towering pillar-like edifice beyond the platform marks the entrance to the Court of the First Edict, closed by a Moonchanter's seal. Eveliina says the huge structure fell from the sky and that its fallen fragments mostly landed to the west at Thunderclap Reef, with one in the camp below.

People: Eveliina is an acolyte of the Frostmoon Scions who greets visitors with a blessing of moonlight and wonders aloud whether Kuutar would like the statues. Kukkia is an adherent who prays at the Idol and tidies it after prayer, an act she considers equal to praying.

Kukkia offers pilgrims a freshly picked flower and offers to lead prayer; later her faith looks troubled and Lauma comes to speak with her. Eveliina describes herself as a humble acolyte who will not go into the details of Kuutar's birth or miracles.

Culture: The Scions treat the platform as a pilgrimage endpoint. Praying here, cleaning the statue and offering flowers are acts of devotion; Eveliina says even those who did not come to pray should feel Kuutar's blessing.

Eveliina greets visitors with 'may the moonlight shine upon your path ahead' and Kukkia with a prayer that the Moon Goddess guard their path.

History: The Court of the First Edict was an ancient sanctuary that a Moonchanter sealed off 500 years ago. The Scions regard it as forbidden ground. The Idol was carved at about the same time.

In Echoes of an Unfinished Past the Traveler and Paimon help Verna open the Court by throwing the fragments into the seal, then explore the sanctum, follow a Moonlane, and find the sword Aila left behind.

Quests: Echoes of an Unfinished Past (Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle, a world quest that starts at the platform) and The Homebound Moon (Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles).

No other quest in the pages read is tied specifically to the platform.

Atmosphere: Quiet reverence under open sky: moonlit statues, hushed prayers and a sense of an ending to a long walk.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Idol stands winged, the Court has been opened, and the platform remains a place of prayer.

After In the Shadows of Night, Kukkia keeps praying but appears troubled about the Scions' faith in the Moon Goddess; Lauma comes to talk her round.

104.comment: Light-Bathed Platform: Idol of the New Moon
104.content: A large statue of the Moon Maiden Kuutar, carved by Aila 500 years ago from kuuvahki-rich ore, at the platform's centre. After The Homebound Moon (6.3), the Scions add wings to it for Kuutar's newfound freedom.

105.content:
Lightless Capital: The Lightless Capital is a Domain of Mastery on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai: the corpse of a once-prosperous city that later fell into ruin. Hundreds of years ago Nod-Krai had its own golden age, and this city carried humanity's arrogant dreams at the edge of the world, with steel sinews and iron bones reflecting industrial and technological glory. Then calamity descended and the city was dragged into darkness and buried by time.

It was added in Version 6.0 and is cut off from remembrance. Its enigmatic structure is said to hint at its future, and those who destroy the foes within may gain insight to improve their Talents.

Geography: The ruin lies on Lempo Isle, part of the Southern Isles, the same island as Nasha Town. The domain is built of rusted-steel and iron architecture.

The text describes a city bearing "the weight of humanity's arrogant dreams", with prosperity and opulence later buried by the ruthless march of time. The Chinese name means roughly "lightless deep capital".

History: Hundreds of years ago adventurers and treasure hunters gathered in droves at this prosperous city during a Nod-Krai golden age. A calamity then dragged living and non-living things into darkness, and the city decayed into ruin.

The wiki links the calamity to the Wild Hunt, whose ghouls have plagued Nod-Krai since the Cataclysm; the domain text does not say so. Treat the identification as inference.

Dangers: Oprichniki Line Troopers, Vanguards and Fireblade Shock Troopers, then a Cutting Edge Fire Support Ground Effect Landcruiser with Hailstorm Cannoneers at the highest level.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world events. A Domain of Mastery that gives Character Talent Materials, recommended for Hydro and Electro teams. Its Ley Line Disorder releases an AoE shockwave (once every 5 seconds) when a character triggers Electro-Charged or Lunar-Charged. The three weekday challenges are named Fallen City (Teachings, Guide and Philosophies of Moonlight), Shadowed Legacy (Elysium) and Overturned Roost (Vagrancy).

Atmosphere: Dark, metallic and desolate: cold iron corridors, dead industry, and a faint sense of a vanished crowd.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a ruin only; the pages read add no later information about the city.

106.content:
Lost Mooncourt: Lost Mooncourt is a Domain of Forgery on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai. By its in-game text, the Frostmoon Scions once used the place as a sacrificial site and raised a lunar court here, hoping to summon lost moonlight back, but now only desolation and frozen silence remain. Weapon-enhancement materials are earned here.

It was added in Version 6.0. Hiisi Island is the Frostmoon Scions' present home, a religious sect devoted to the Moon Goddess, and the ruin is an older altar on it.

Geography: A forgotten altar of stone carvings with a "labyrinth of time" feel, on a forested island that is largely untouched wilderness under the Scions' care.

Moonlight once flowed through the stone carvings and has now stopped. The text calls the setting the "border realms" of Nod-Krai.

History: The domain text describes an age when three moons rose together. The lunar people read the phases and tides, and what they touched surged with moonlit might. In the waning days the light dimmed and the leaderless people scattered. Legend says the Frostmoon Scions built a lunar court in Nod-Krai to summon the lost moonlight back.

This echoes the wider Nod-Krai lore: the Three Moons, the Hyperborean golden realm and its survivors, who were guided to Hiisi Island. The court is the remains of oaths from that era ("echoes of ancient oaths"), and the text says secrets unveiled in the quiet still swirl in time.

Dangers: Oprichniki Line Troopers, Medics and Thunderblitz Gvardiya, then Cutting Edge All-Purpose Storm Landcruisers at the top level.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world events. A Domain of Forgery giving Weapon Ascension Materials, recommended for Dendro, Hydro, Electro and Pyro teams. Its Ley Line Disorder raises Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon damage by 150% and Lunar-Bloom damage by 50%. Weekday challenges are Radiant Splendor (Artful Device), Prayers Sung (Long Night Flint) and Lunar Oblation (Far-North Scions).

Atmosphere: Silver-grey and hushed: frost on carved stone, a ceremonial space that has long lost the moon it was built to call.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a dormant altar. The real Frost Moon has returned to the sky (Song of the Welkin Moon), but no source read says the court has been restored.

107.content:
Lunar Highlands (also: Highlands of the Frost Moon): The Lunar Highlands is the main stretch of the Frost Moon open to explore: a pale, low-gravity upland scattered with ruined facilities left by the ancient dragon researchers of Project Moongazer. It includes the Eye of Ibni-Belum, Ungien's Circle (a living biosphere), the Archaeolune Storm Research Center, the Nuur Stone Circle, the Golden Hall and Traveler's Crater, where the Traveler's spaceship rests. The moon opened to travellers in 6.7 through the Moon Gazing quests.

Teyvat hangs in the sky above it, and travel between its sites is by High-Speed Transit Lanes, which dragon terminals bring back to life.

Geography: Outside Ungien's Circle the moon is blanketed by turbulent Archaeolune Energy, which weakens gravity: standing jumps are much higher and falls much slower. Stormy zones lie across the moon, and the Moontide Sea, a lunar mare, covers a large part of the near side and is the failed product of the dragon scientist Lusalim's Lunar Veil project.

In-game, the Archaeolune storms and the lunar sea tire the traveller until they are carried back to the last safe place; safe refuge is found on floating stones and inside Storm Occlusion Fields. Dragon-built machines in the highlands run on Archaeolune Energy: Ancient Moon Pearls, Pioneer Source Structures, Backup Power Generators, Gravimeters that change local gravity, and terminals that unlock transit lanes. The Teardrop of the Moon is a local specialty.

Places: The Eye of Ibni-Belum is the dragon antenna and monitoring station and the first stop in the Moon Gazing story. Ungien's Circle is a biosphere built by the dragon life scientist Ungien and the one place where normal gravity holds. The Archaeolune Storm Research Center observed the moon's energy storms. The Nuur Stone Circle stored the dragons' research data. The Golden Hall is a quieter stop marked on the map with a line about a silver ship and a great golden house. Traveler's Crater holds the Traveler's spaceship.

The Dark Side of the Moon is a separate area behind the highlands, reached through the Project Moongazer quests. Dragon facilities across the moon use the Secret Source technology of the ancient dragon civilisation, and elite guardians of the Overseer Network patrol them.

History: Before the Heavenly Principles first invaded Teyvat, the dragon scientist Ibni-Belum led a group of researchers to the Frost Moon and set up the facilities that begin Project Moongazer. The project dealt with signals from deep space, which a later dragon, Ungien, followed; his return with a message of hope from a dying civilisation shaped the project's final mission. Lusalim, Ungien and Maagees's pupil, collected the group's research.

Much later the Frost Moon was moved beyond the false sky. After Canon's death the Frostmoon Scions foretold a new moon goddess, and Columbina took that place. During Song of the Welkin Moon the moon was drawn back inside the false sky. In the Moon Gazing quests (6.7) the Traveler, Paimon and Eggie crash-land on the moon, and Columbina guides the Traveler to the dark side.

Dangers: Archaeolune storms, disturbance zones, the lunar sea, and dragon guardian machines, chiefly the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network. Local legends include Prism Slime and Mushteshir.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the highlands are open, uninhabited by anyone but kuuhenki and the occasional visitor, and show no trace of Abyssal presence even after thousands of years outside the false sky.

108.comment: Lunar Highlands: Moon Gazing quest series
108.content: A three-act World Quest series that unlocks the Frost Moon: Pioneers, Visitors From the Stars and Project Moongazer. It is the first exploration World Quest series with full voice-over and animated cutscenes. It begins when the Traveler follows Columbina and ends with the message sent from the Eye of Ibni-Belum.

109.content: Fast routes between moon sites, active once the nearby Transit Station is switched on. Each station then doubles as a waypoint. The lanes connect the Eye of Ibni-Belum, Ungien's Circle, the Nuur Stone Circle, Traveler's Crater and other sites.

110.content:
Lusalim's Laboratory (also: Lusalim's research lab, Lusalim's final facility): Lusalim's Laboratory is the dragon researcher Lusalim's final workplace, tucked deep inside the vast hidden base on the Dark Side of the Moon in the Frost Moon (Nod-Krai). Its terminals hold his farewell: he confesses that he sinned against dragonkind by bowing to the Heavenly Principles, and he entrusts the last step of Project Moongazer to Nin-Kiggia (Ninnin), the data-born "daughter" he created.

The laboratory is a place of records, not machinery: three terminals and a book-like engraving preserve what Lusalim wanted remembered. It was reached by the Traveler, Paimon and Eggie (who is Ninnin's successor in the story) in the second act of the Project Moongazer world quests, when Columbina had mysteriously gone missing.

Geography: The laboratory lies inside the Dark Side of the Moon base, past the front hall and its security systems. In-game it sits on the base's transport level. A left corridor, a central terminal and a right corridor each hold one readable record. The base around it was built much later than the other dragon facilities and is lit and powered by a fissure that reaches down to the Moonheart Gap.

To get there the party had to disable the base's security by shutting down two control rooms in quick succession, slip past patrolling searchlight machines by hiding beside storage chests, and open a door sealed by an Archaeolune Energy barrier.

Places: Left corridor terminal: Lusalim's farewell record, written to Ninnin. Central terminal: a dedication in Ninnin's voice, addressed to "my father, Lusalim", crediting him as chief architect of Project Lunar Veil, designer of Nin-Kiggia's Game of Life and executor of Project Moongazer. Right corridor terminal: the Moongazer's Engraving (volume I), a digest of the message carried by the Stellar Blackbody.

Volume II of the Moongazer's Engraving is given to the player automatically during the quest and is addressed by Lusalim to "my daughter, Ninnin". The engravings are text only; they record the alien message in a condensed translation, with Lusalim's note that terms he could not understand were replaced by his own equivalents.

People: Lusalim: a dragon researcher, student of Ungien and Maagees-Geti, and one of the Moongazers who inherited their work. Nin-Kiggia ("Ninnin"): the data-based life he made and raised as a daughter; her record is the one that addresses him as father. Neither is present: the laboratory is empty and only their words remain.

Lusalim's record names three pieces of good fortune: living in the age after Ibni-Belum so that he could reach the moon, being taken in by Ungien and Maagees, and having Ninnin. He expects to die before the project is completed and hopes to leave a line of stars that says "The dragons were here." Eggie, the black kuuhenki who travelled with the Traveler, was born from the moon's data sea as part of the same project and carries the mission.

History: After the Heavenly Principles arrived, the Lunar Veil Laboratory in the Moontide Sea was destroyed and Lusalim moved his work to this laboratory on the Dark Side. He tells Ninnin he surrendered the precious results of their research to the "terrifying sovereign who was not of this world", and does not expect to escape judgment for it. The quests suggest this bargain kept the moon's other facilities from being destroyed.

The laboratory therefore stands inside a base that, according to data the party found at the entrance, serves the will of the "Lord of Darkness who returned from the Sea of Stars". The Traveler identified that figure as the returning dragon king Nibelung; that base was built to turn the moon into a space-based weapon. Lusalim's rooms are tucked inside that later installation rather than being part of it.

Atmosphere: Cold, sterile and quiet. After the pursuit through searchlights, the laboratory is a hush of old terminals whose records are addressed to someone who never came; the contrast between the machine-hardness of Nibelung's base and the intimate, grateful tone of Lusalim's words is the point of the place.

Dangers: Approaches to the laboratory are defended by security systems: patrolling machines with searchlight-like Transmission Modules, annihilation modules, a base-wide alarm and guard constructs. The laboratory itself is not shown to be hostile.

Travel: Reached through the Dark Side of the Moon base: in the quest the party, led by Columbina, flew across the edge of the lunar sea to the base's gate and then worked inward through the front hall.

Quests: Project Moongazer (Part 1), Moon Gazing chapter Act III (6.7): the party find the laboratory while searching for Columbina and read Lusalim's records. Project Moongazer (Part 2) continues down to the Moonheart Gap and the moon's core.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the laboratory is intact and unattended inside the Dark Side base on the Frost Moon; its records stand as Lusalim's last testament.

Project Moongazer was carried through to its conclusion in the quest by Ninnin's successor, with Columbina shielding the transmission. Nothing in the laboratory itself is shown to change afterwards.

111.content:
In the record left in the left corridor, Lusalim looks back on three pieces of good fortune and then entrusts Project Moongazer, "now only one step away from completion", to Ninnin, whom he calls a true child of the stars. He says the missing step is a way for life, information and memory to be inherited and to circulate, and that the power of the moon's origin, granted by the Moon Goddesses, is enough to do it.

He confesses that he will not live to see it finished because he sinned against dragonkind: he capitulated to the sovereign who was not of this world and surrendered the fruits of their research, and he does not intend to escape judgment. He adds that Ninnin knows why he chose this, because he had his own mission. His last wish is to journey into the sea of stars, shed a few tears there in tribute to his teachers, and set stars in a line saying "The dragons were here."

112.content: The engraving in the right corridor is Lusalim's translated digest of the message carried by the Stellar Blackbody, the alien lifeform with which Ungien fused. As quoted in the quest, it is an address to a friend in a distant world, hoping the voices of the Moongazers will at least drive away a little cold silence from a lonely universe and that the listener's civilisation will know it is not alone. Lusalim notes that unintelligible terms were rendered with the researchers' own concepts. The message is the content Project Moongazer was designed to keep transmitting.

113.content:
Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory (also: Lunar Veil Laboratory): Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory is what is left of a hidden laboratory in the Moontide Sea, where the dragon researcher Lusalim carried on Project Lunar Veil after his teacher Maagees fell ill and Kalag's security force took control of the biosphere. It is unlocked in the Moontide Sea by repairing the High-Speed Transit Station.

Two terminal logs are kept here. The first speaks of Containment Object-1, a black creature fused from Archaeolune Energy and blackbody matter, which keeps growing. The second is Lusalim's farewell to Maagees before he performs the operation she asked for.

Places: A ruined laboratory with a terminal holding the two logs. It lies in the Moontide Sea and is a point of interest rather than a district.

History: Log I: Maagees operated on Containment Object-1 with an experimental technique, turning it into a new living being; Lusalim notes it is bigger every day and that "it will never be the Professor Ungien we knew". He hopes Kalag's security force does not find out, as it could endanger Project Lunar Veil, and observes that they have no access to his laboratory yet.

Log II: Lusalim will perform on Maagees the same creative operation she once did when she created Ungie, as she wished; the experience will serve the upcoming Project Moongazer. He admits he took her insistence on sending the message for grief turned obsession until she showed him the whole message brought by the Stellar Blackbody, and he now understands why the Eye of Ibni-Belum team stood with her against Kalag's force, even though the first Moongazers considered her and Ungien traitors.

Status as of 7.1: Destroyed and ruined as of 7.1. Only terminals remain for exploration.

114.content: Lusalim is a dragon researcher, student of Maagees and the other pioneers (he calls them his teachers), and the designer of the full-scale Lunar Veil. His own entry carries his biography; this lab holds his logs.

115.content:
Maagees's Greenhouse (also: Maggie's Greenhouse): Maagees's Greenhouse is a greenhouse in Ungien's Circle, the biosphere of the Frost Moon, reached by an elevator. It belonged to the dragon researcher Maagees and held Containment Object-1, a black specimen that began sending a message once shown starfield footage. Its terminal logs tell how the research broke down.

Three research logs and a terminal describe the specimen's early days, the discovery of blackbody matter, Maagees's collapse after feeding the specimen with her own body, and the biosphere's takeover by Kalag. Lusalim finishes the record, which ends with the specimen being moved elsewhere.

Places: At the bottom of an elevator there is an entrance and a Cultivation Area. The logs and terminal are found there. The in-game loading text elsewhere calls Ungien's resolve something later passed on to the "mistress of the greenhouse".

History: Log I (by Maagees): Day 1 the specimen's glossy black surface showed no response to stimuli. Day 30 it vibrated at a high frequency when shown starfield footage. Day 37 the Eye of Ibni-Belum team decoded the vibrations as a message in the researchers' own language, roughly "I'm glad this message reached you", and Maagees asks whether it is Ungie.

Log II: by Day 89 it deteriorated rapidly after almost a month of decodable output, and medullary tissue was extracted. On Day 92 she named the black filamentous ejecta blackbody matter, the substance that drives the transmissions. On Day 98 she found that pure energy raises its activity, especially the Archaeolune Energy in living bodies, and fears that this is why Ungie ended as he did.
Log III (by Lusalim): on Day 107 Maagees was in a coma after feeding the specimen with her own body; Lusalim takes over, insisting the thing is no longer Ungien. Day 137 he fumes that Kalag has taken control of the biosphere and blames Maagees's research for the lost control over the Moonlit Vines. Day 138 he writes that the biosphere is no longer safe and that Containment Object-1 will be moved that day.

Status as of 7.1: Ancient and derelict as of 7.1; the greenhouse is used for exploration and lore.

116.content: Containment Object-1 is the specimen logged here and later in Lusalim's laboratory, treated by the logs as the transformed Ungien. It fuses Archaeolune Energy with blackbody matter and keeps growing.

117.content:
Main Control Hall: The Main Control Hall is the central control room of Dunanna Forward Station, an underground installation in the Dunanna Pit area of Nod-Krai. The in-game map marker describes it as the core processing room for every command the station receives and transmits.

It is a point of interest on the lower level of the station's map, reached in the world quest Pioneers (added in 6.7).

Places: In Pioneers the Traveler and Paimon follow Columbina into ruins beneath Misty Shoal, restore power at a generator room, and later enter the hall while chasing a black kuuhenki. A message at the Celestial Orbit says the Frost Moon coordinates, the station's base engineering blueprints and a route map to the Main Control Hall have been transmitted. The hall is guarded by an Anzu array, and a lunar shuttle is reached afterwards.

The hall is one stop in a sequence of station spaces in the quest: the generator room, the Celestial Orbit, the Main Control Hall, and the lunar shuttle where the black kuuhenki is confronted.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hall remains part of the explorable Dunanna Forward Station; the sources read record no later change.

118.content:
Maroon Basin: Maroon Basin is a wide beach of distinctive pink stones on Paha Isle in Nod-Krai. It was once a thriving habitat for Tassel Jellies, but the Fatui's activity on the island has left it barren.

Notes left by Fatui personnel there show a guarded, kuuvahki-controlled installation that struggled with stray jellyfish.

Geography: A broad shoreline of pink stones on Paha Isle, the island associated with the Frostladen Machinery. The wiki notes that the German name may nod to a real red-sand beach in Finland, which is a naming observation and not lore.

The stones give the beach its look; the surrounding waters were the Tassel Jellies' home before the Fatui moved in.

People: Fatui personnel patrol the area. Two named patrol staff, Riku and Dima, appear in logs found there, taking morning, afternoon and night shifts.

Their logs are casual and complaining in tone: Dima keeps forgetting his ID card and hides a spare near the door, Riku nods off on night shifts, and both are glad when higher-ups hand the jellyfish problem to recon bots.

Dangers: The installation sits in a managed kuuvahki environment. A found note describes the open state as a weak kuuvahki environment and the closed state as strong, and warns that equipment must be given kuuvahki through the separator and never the reverse.

The main hazard is the Fatui presence itself.

History: Earlier the basin was a thriving Tassel Jelly habitat; Fatui activity on the island then made it barren. The patrol records show that jellyfish kept slipping into the barrier: the guards at first released them by hand, and some that could not leave were disposed of. Management later assigned recon bots to the problem.

Quests: The wiki lists three quests touching the area: Drifting Toward a Promised Sky, Flins: Patrol and Jahoda: Cat! Hey! Cat! Their content is not summarised here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the basin is described as barren of Tassel Jellies; no later change is recorded in the sources read.

119.comment: Maroon Basin: Maroon Basin Patrol Records
119.content: A set of logs written by two Fatui guards, Riku and Dima, alternating shifts around a kuuvahki barrier. Jellyfish repeatedly got inside; they were released or, when unable to leave, disposed of, until higher-ups gave the task to recon bots. The logs repeatedly record "no abnormalities".

120.content:
Mimisbrunnr Books: Mimisbrunnr Books is a bookshop in Nasha Town, on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. It is owned by Dhabit and sells books.

Its stock does not refresh, and each book can be bought only once. The shop has been available since Nod-Krai opened in version 6.0.

People: Dhabit owns the shop and is its vendor. The wiki lists Hannu (described as a newsy), Pechna and Viliana among the NPCs found at the location.

Culture: The name echoes Mimisbrunnr, the well beneath the world tree in Norse myth, a real-world reference noted by the wiki as trivia. The game does not explain it.

Status as of 7.1: Operating in Nasha Town as of 7.1; no change recorded.

121.content:
Misty Shoal: Misty Shoal is a small island subarea of Dunanna Pit in Nod-Krai, east of Piramida, introduced in version 6.7. The sky above it is perfectly clear: there are no clouds at all. Beneath it lie ruins linked to a moon-landing project.

The island is reached by Moonlane. Its only quest in canon so far is the World Quest Pioneers, part of the Moon Gazing chapter.

Geography: A deserted island with a lake-filled pit, drifting kuuhenki and a Statue of the New Moon. An entrance in the ground leads down to underground ruins. Floating rocks, broken machinery and fallen rings fill the lower halls.

A terminal inside the ruins labels the area as a celestial orbit computation chamber. A separate sign names Dunanna Forward Station, so the base is associated with the wider Dunanna Pit installations. A lunar-gravity simulation room and a main control hall lie deeper.

Quests: In Pioneers, Paimon and the Traveler spot Columbina heading onto the island and follow her underground. Columbina passes on a new power, Archaeolune Ripples, which restarts a backup generator and clears the energy pathways. A terminal finds the Frost Moon coordinates and offers a route to the main control hall for moon landing preparations.

At the terminal the Traveler offers Columbina a hand and she turns into a black kuuhenki: an impostor. It flees through guarded halls; after the Traveler defeats a defence array in the control hall, the base begins to self-destruct and asks for orbital coordinates. If the right three are given, the kuuhenki, speaking in fragments, asks for rescue on the moon and points to the lunar spaceship. The quest then ends at the shuttle; its aftermath belongs to later Moon Gazing quests.

Dangers: The ruins' automated defences treat visitors as intruders: transmission modules fire on the Traveler and the control hall's guardian attacks. The self-destruct countdown is the quest's main hazard.

Atmosphere: Bright, windless calm above and silent, half-powered machine halls below: floating stones, humming rings, terminal voices repeating alerts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is explorable and the base's story continues in Moon Gazing content; nothing here is described as resolved.

122.comment: Misty Shoal: The Lunar Shuttle Base
122.content: Beneath Misty Shoal is a ruined installation concerned with reaching the Frost Moon. Its terminals compute Trilune coordinates and prepare moon landings, and its power is restored using Columbina's gift of Archaeolune Ripples. Whoever built it is not stated in the quest text; treat that as unknown.

123.content:
Moonchild's Treasures: Moonchild's Treasures is a Domain of Blessing on Ashveil Peak in Nod-Krai, the sacred vault of a ruined tower. By the domain's text, descendants of the far north raised the tower for followers of the morning star, as a sign of resolve to resist fate and the will of the gods. Priests of the Moonchildren hid the last sparks of an ancient civilization's splendor here. Villains and owls now infest the ruin.

It was added in Version 6.3. The priests hoped that when the light of the Welkin Moon returned to the earth, it would guide the wandering and displaced back to their former paradise.

Geography: A ruined tower and its vault in the mountains of Ashveil Peak, the northernmost part of Pohjola.

The text says the tower bore witness to a dream that shone radiantly before sky-fire reduced it to ash. The top level pits challengers against Fishers of Hidden Depths, listed among Ashveil Peak's elite enemies.

History: The tower was raised by the far-north descendants of Hyperborea, the golden realm of the three moons, as an act of defiance for the followers of Koitar, the morning star. When the tower fell, its sacred Mekhaneikos were carried off by those with ill intent. The last generations of that era let even their hope fade, and drifted into ignorance and confusion.

"Mekhaneikos" is the Hyperboreans' own term for their advanced apparatuses, developed under Koitar and Anacharsis; wider lore says Hyperborea was destroyed by a Celestial Nail launched by the Heavenly Principles, which the domain text's "sky-fire" probably refers to, though it does not say so. Hyperborean records also mention a tower meant to reach Celestia, but the wiki does not connect it to this vault. The owls are the only ones left to voice what was forgotten.

Dangers: Oprichniki Vanguards and Fireblade Shock Troopers with Force Recon Storm and Ground Effect Landcruisers, and Fishers of Hidden Depths on the final level. The in-game description calls the invaders villains seeking sacred relics.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world events. A four-level Domain of Blessing recommended for Hydro, Geo, Electro and Dendro teams. Its Ley Line Disorder gives all party members +35% Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Crystallize and Lunar-Bloom DMG and +30% DEF for 10 seconds after a character triggers one of those reactions. Artifact sets: Aubade of Morningstar and Moon, A Day Carved From Rising Winds, Tiny Miracle and Instructor.

Atmosphere: Elegiac and moonlit: broken stone, hooting owls and an old hope still faintly kept.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the vault is held by invaders seeking relics, and its Mekhaneikos were carried off long ago. The real moon has returned to Nod-Krai's sky, but no source read says the priests' hope has been carried out here.

124.content:
Moongazer (also: the Moongazer spaceship, The Fallen Moongazer, Moongazer Log): The Moongazer is the spaceship the dragon researcher Ungien built to chase a mysterious deep-space signal. He flew it out across the sea of stars and vanished; years later it crashed, cloaked, into the Space Lifeform Capture Station on the Frost Moon, carrying a round black spiky creature that was all that remained of him. Its wreck still lies beside the station.

The ship is not the Moongazers (the dragon researchers) nor Project Moongazer, though it is named for their ideals. It is where Ungien's fusion with an alien creature took place and where that creature, speaking through him, delivered its message to the dragons.

Geography: The wreck lies outside the Space Lifeform Capture Station in space above Ungien's Circle, among debris from the collision. Columbina notes that the station looks seriously rammed and that a ship is more likely the cause than a creature. In the quest, a mechanism inside the wreck holds the Moongazer Log.

A viewpoint named "The Fallen Moongazer" overlooks the wreck from the station. The ship sits next to the damaged Space Capture Arm, the corridor that was meant to bring captured alien creatures aboard.

History: The Eye of Ibni-Belum, the transceiver tower built after the first Moongazer received a strange signal from deep space, later recorded a second signal and its coordinates. Ungien, a life scientist, who had made the Moongazer, piloted it to find its sender and send word back, even though the coordinates were too far for the ship to return from. He disappeared into the sea of stars and no messages came back.

During the journey the ship and Ungien met an unknown creature. The ship's log shows that it did not attack him; he chose to fuse with it so that it could overcome the language barrier and speak to the dragons. Years later the station's Space Capture Arm was struck by an unknown, cloaked object, and after emergency repairs the researchers found it was the Moongazer. Ungien's partner Maagees-Geti entered first and found only a round, black, spiky creature that matched his data signature.

Atmosphere: Drifting, weightless wreckage, silent against a view of the moon and Teyvat. The mood is of a quiet monument to a scientist's conviction rather than a battlefield.

Dangers: The station and wreck are in weightless space; the party is limited to the Traveler and, if owned, Columbina while inside the station. The surrounding lunar sea can be harmful to non-kuuhenki during Archaeolune storms.

Travel: Reached via the Skymount elevator from Ungien's Circle to the Space Lifeform Capture Station, then outward from the station.

Quests: Visitors From the Stars (Part 2) reveals the ship's story; the hidden exploration quest A Journey's End makes its log readable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Moongazer is a derelict wreck beside the Space Lifeform Capture Station; no one is shown repairing or flying it.

125.content: A mechanism inside the wreck, readable after the quest A Journey's End, replays fragmentary lines in a haunting voice: the fall of a star, the soul of a star that calls like broth to a table, an address to "Ysna'qurel, Ruler of Throgg" who is said to be swallowed by darkness, a request to carry a message onward, and the string "Bad-Uru-Namu-Ungien-Blackbody". The last line states that the speaker and the addressee are one. Canon does not explain Ysna'qurel or Throgg.

126.content:
Moonheart Gap (also: Moonheart Chasm, the moon's core, Heart of the Moon): The Moonheart Gap is the fissure at the bottom of the Frost Moon's Dark Side base that opens onto the moon's core, the source of its power. The dragon king Nibelung, returned from the stars and corrupted by the Abyss, tapped it to power a weapon that would fire the moon at Teyvat; earlier, the dragon researcher Lusalim used the core to gather the data of the Moongazers for rebirth.

Columbina and the Traveler descended through the weapon's launch silo to reach it. The core is also where the black kuuhenki Eggie was born, and where an imprint of Nin-Kiggia waits to explain Project Moongazer.

Geography: At the very bottom of the Dark Side base, a carved fissure leads into the moon's core, from which an endless stream of ancient-moon energy surges and powers the base. Above it lies a circular launch silo with shifting gravity, entered by a door sealed with a key.

The silo's walls are walkable, with gravity that changes along the way; the core is a dark floating space with a very high concentration of Archaeolune Energy. Columbina says the core is the origin of the moon's life and the seat of its will.

Places: The launch silo (with the weapon's core and an engineered guardian, the Warden of the Flame). Below it, the moon's core as a sea of gathered data. The door key is the Ancient Moon's Fount, the energy entity Lusalim made at the Lunar Veil Laboratory.

The weapon is guarded by Pioneer Source Structures, Annihilation Modules and a blast cannon that fires repeatedly; the party hides in alcoves in the silo wall to avoid the shots.

History: The moon's core was the origin of its life and power. Lusalim gathered the researchers' ancient-moon energy data there and pleaded with the Moon Goddesses to lend the primordial power of creation. With it, the data of past Moongazers could be reborn as data-based lifeforms, so that the Stellar Blackbody's message could be sent again and again. Nin-Kiggia's recording says a cute black kuuhenki, the Traveler's Eggie, was born in this sea when that power was triggered.

After the Heavenly Principles arrived, the dragon king Nibelung returned from the stars as the "Lord of Darkness", building the Dark Side base to turn the moon into a space-based weapon, a launch silo whose artillery would use the core's energy. Columbina says the primordial ruler was defeated by the Heavenly Principles, so the weapon is no longer a threat.

Atmosphere: Dark, weightless and beautiful: Columbina calls the core beautiful, while the silo above it is cold, mechanical and echoing with warning announcements.

Dangers: Gravity shifts, engineered mechanisms that explode, the silo's repeating energy blasts, and the Warden of the Flame guardian that borrows power from the core, making gravity vanish. High Archaeolune Energy concentration is harmful if you are not shielded by Columbina's power.

Quests: Project Moongazer (Part 2), Moon Gazing chapter Act III (6.7).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the weapon is stopped and the core is quiet; the gathered researcher data is preserved.

Columbina and the Traveler stopped the weapon and entered the core together, then returned to the Eye of Ibni-Belum for the transmission.

127.content: At the core waits a recorded imprint of Nin-Kiggia, addressed to the one who inherits the mission. She tells the visitor they are a new life created by the will of the moon, thanks the Moon Goddesses for allowing the transgression of borrowing the power of creation, and names those who came before: Ibni-Belum, Ungien, Maagees and Lusalim. She says the visitor's mission is to continue sending the message into the universe, and signs off with a salute to all fellow Moongazers.

128.content:
Moontide Sea (also: lunar sea, Sea of Broken Skies): The Moontide Sea is a lunar sea on the Frost Moon, a body of liquid-like Archaeolune Energy so dense that it can harm any living being that is not a kuuhenki. It formed after a terrible calamity wrecked Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory; it is home to the Mega Kuuhenki Maggie and Ungie and to shoals of small kuuhenki that can mimic jellyfish and whales.

Its centre holds the Ancient Moon's Fount, an energy entity made by Lusalim. When the Mega Kuuhenki fought, the sea stirred into an Archaeolune Storm that spread toward Ungien's Circle; the Traveler fetched the Fount while Columbina tended the wounded Maggie.

Geography: A sea on the Frost Moon, reached in the quest by floating down from the Space Lifeform Capture Station beside Maggie; the Dark Side of the Moon lies beyond its edge. Blue areas of the sea hold high concentrations of ancient-moon energy and incapacitate anyone who touches them; floating islands and stones rise from it. A "Sea of Broken Skies" viewpoint overlooks it.

Features include Archaeolune Energy Barriers, Nodes and Surges, Ancient Moon Pearls, high-speed transit lanes, material storage chests, Pioneer Source Structures, shoaling kuuhenki and wondrous black kuuhenki, and elite enemies such as the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network. The local specialty is the Teardrop of the Moon.

Places: The Ancient Moon's Fount at the sea's centre. The Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab, a site tied to Lusalim's research. Floating islets used as footholds.

The sea is the site of Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory, his second-to-last facility; the last was the one on the Dark Side.

People: Maggie (the Mega Kuuhenki who was Maagees-Geti) and Ungie (the Mega Kuuhenki born from Ungien) live here, with schools of shoaling kuuhenki. Columbina guides visitors.

Ungie was irritable, his body tangled in Knotted Moonlight Vines that held data from Ungien's Circle, until the party cleared them. Eggie absorbed Ungie's stored information to learn what had happened at the Capture Station.

History: The sea was once Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory. After the miniature Veil on Ungien's Circle succeeded, the researchers built a massive Veil generator here to hide the entire moon. Before it could take shape, a being from beyond the stars pierced it; the device went haywire, the laboratory exploded and all came to nothing. Only deep underground might traces remain.

Lusalim and Maagees designed the Lunar Veil to protect Project Moongazer's transmission from hostile listeners, using the reflective properties of Blackbody Matter. Columbina notes the Veil resembles the false sky in miniature and suspects that Lusalim bargained with the Heavenly Principles with his research, which would explain why other dragon facilities survived.

Atmosphere: A glimmering, weightless sea where you float by kuuhenki, with distant whales drifting overhead. It is beautiful but hazardous, like a storm of moonlight.

Dangers: Contact with the blue energy zones incapacitates non-kuuhenki; Archaeolune Storms stirred by Ungie's attacks; Frostnight Scions; Ungie's sticky bombs; and the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix guardians.

Travel: Crossed with the help of shoaling kuuhenki, which can mimic jellyfish to bounce travellers across or whales to ferry them. Columbina or Maggie can keep the party weightless and shielded nearby.

Quests: Visitors From the Stars (Part 2) (Moon Gazing Act II, 6.7). The related Beneath the Lunar Sea quest opens the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab Ancient Moon's Remnant.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sea is calm after the Fount's removal and the Mega Kuuhenki's reconciliation, though its energy remains dangerous.

129.comment: Moontide Sea: The Ancient Moon's Fount
129.content: The Ancient Moon's Fount sits at the heart of the Archaeolune Storm. Eggie senses that it is artificial and, on touching it, recalls that it was made by the researcher Lusalim. It is also the key later used to open the door in the Dark Side base's launch silo.

130.content:
Nasha Town (also: Nasha): Nasha Town is the main port and commercial centre of Nod-Krai, on Lempo Isle. It has no official government. Merchants, adventurers, exiles, treasure hunters and Fatui all rub shoulders there, and the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets do the most to keep it working. It is built largely of scrap metal, and kuuvahki-powered machines and cargo rails fill the sky above it.

It is both a haven of freedom and something of a lawless jungle. The Traveler first reaches it in the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest (6.0), guided by Ineffa. Landmarks include the Flagship tavern, Speranza restaurant, the Adventurers' Guild in the central plaza and the Curatorium of Secrets.

Geography: A seaside settlement on Lempo Isle in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai, with a harbour and docks on one side and a central plaza at its heart. Because Nod-Krai has few resources, much of the town is built from scrap metal. Cargo-transport rails criss-cross above the roofs and kuuvahki-powered machines stand on nearly every corner, giving it an industrial look unusual for the region.

The Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Aino's workshop, lies on the same isle just outside town. The town has no clear plan: official furnishing text says it has no true administrator and no clear planning structure, so countless narrow passages and gaps run between buildings. To most residents they are just channels for noise; to people who gather information they are routes for secrets and shortcuts.

Places: The Flagship tavern, Speranza restaurant, the Adventurers' Guild in the central plaza, the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets, the port, and a handful of shops.

- The Flagship: a tavern run by the bartender Demyan, where treasure hunters and bounty hunters swap intel and pick up commissions. It has a bounty board and a jukebox.
- Speranza: Nod-Krai's main restaurant, run by Katya and home base of the Conch Gang. A prize wheel on its side, joked about as a repurposed roulette, tells daily fortunes.
- Adventurers' Guild: in the central plaza, with Katheryne as receptionist and Sarin as branch master.
- Curatorium of Secrets: an information broker's headquarters directly behind the Voynich Guild's.

Mimisbrunnr Books (a bookshop owned by Dhabit), Rossum Workshop (a smithy), Nuts 'N' Nuts (groceries and repairs, with an alchemy bench), Northland Bank's local branch, the Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse, and the Voynich Guild's souvenir outlet managed by Tarno.

The port holds a harbour office, warehouses, foremen, repairmen and sailors; the central plaza has stalls, merchants and fashion and research visitors. A guide map handed to newcomers advertises a Mimisbrunnr Books investment scheme, Speranza's wheel, sugar sculptures by the confectioner Hunajatta and the experiments of Fontaine researcher Liouba.

People: Residents include Nefer and Jahoda of the Curatorium, Katya of Speranza, Demyan of the Flagship, and the stray children of the Conch Gang. Ineffa and Aino of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop are frequent visitors.

Tarno is a Voynich Guild employee who manages its souvenir outlet and later speaks for the Guild in the League. The newsy Alida sells the paper "Nasha Express". Fatui soldiers, Snezhnayans, exiles and travellers from Sumeru, Liyue and Fontaine pass through the port. Many locals are Ratniks, treasure hunters or dockworkers.

Zinaida, now a treasure hunter employed by the Voynich Guild, was once a mid-level leader of the Seahook Gang and brought Jahoda into it. Lauma and Flins of the Frostmoon Scions visit town and have friends there. Nicole of the Hexenzirkel helped defend it during the 6.3 crisis, and Durin and Albedo were assigned to it.

Governance: Nasha Town has no formal government. Wiki summaries say it is under the influence of the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets, Speranza and the Fatui. The Voynich Guild is a commerce guild of local merchants that handles trade deals, import and export, business certificates and dispute resolution, so it is the nearest thing to a regulator. Nefer leads the Curatorium and is also a Guild member.

The Curatorium's information network gives it quiet leverage. After the Dottore crisis a new League was formed as a joint effort of Nod-Krai's factions. Tarno hosted its opening ceremony as the Voynich Guild's representative, and Flins persuaded Illuga to represent the Lightkeepers; Aino and Ineffa helped hand out food on behalf of the Frostmoon Scions.

Culture: A mixed, frontier-style port culture of trade, bargaining, gossip and street food, where outsiders are accepted as long as they do business. Speranza's hot dog is a local favourite, and locals take their fortunes from its wheel. The town is also a stage for Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, with stalls, games and candy.

Information is a currency here: Nefer says that with the town in turmoil everyone wants intel, and the Curatorium's reception desk is staffed in shifts by different characters, Nefer included. Children are given real freedom; the Conch Gang raise themselves under Katya's wing.

History: Little of Nasha Town's founding is recorded. The Conch Gang's own story is that a gang of children first 'conquered' the empty site, calling gatherings with a conch shell, until the settlement grew too big for them. A bandit group, the Seahook Gang, is said to have once held hidden control of the town before its boss was killed and the gang scattered. The town was first mentioned in 5.3 and first visited in 6.0.

Before the Song of the Welkin Moon, the Fatui built the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on nearby Paha Isle. In Fulminations and Undercurrents, repeated Wild Hunt attacks strained the few Lightkeepers stationed near town under Sergeant Major Sousi, whose cannon was waiting on repairs from Aino, and Nefer remarked that with Nasha Town in turmoil everyone wanted intel.

Atmosphere: Clanking, steam, rails overhead, and smells of fried sausage, sugar and sea. The sky is full of cargo lines and the lanes between houses are narrow and loud. Everyone seems to be selling, buying or listening, and there is always a rumour moving through the crowd. At night the lamps and fishing boats glow, and during Moon-Prayer Night the whole town is hung with lanterns and games.

Dangers: Pickpockets, shady deals and local rivalries are the everyday risks, since nobody enforces law uniformly. Wild Hunt incursions and Fatui activity have threatened the area, and the town was besieged once. Outside town, the surrounding isle has monsters and kuuvahki hazards.

Travel: Nasha Town is the arrival point for sea travellers heading into Nod-Krai and a hub for the islands. The Traveler comes in by sea from Natlan in the 6.0 Archon Quest. The Adventurers' Guild and the Flagship are the usual first stops.

Quests: Where the Moon Rises (6.0) introduces the town; Fulminations and Undercurrents is set here and at the Flagship; The Night the Moon Returns Home hosts the Moon-Prayer Night festival; Descending Moon and Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3) cover the siege and its aftermath. Intel quests from Nefer and Jahoda also take place here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Nasha Town stands, recovered after the siege. It remains a free port with no formal ruler, and the new League of factions first met there.

The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya; the sources read describe no new upheaval in Nasha Town.

131.content:
A tavern run by the young bartender Demyan, where treasure hunters and bounty hunters gather. It has a jukebox and a bounty board. In Fulminations and Undercurrents Nefer brings the Traveler to the tavern's invitation-only Banquet, where they mix drinks for guests and gather intel.

The wheel at Speranza is jokingly said to be a repurposed roulette from the Flagship. Demyan sells food and drinks, including the Roulette Special.

132.content: Nod-Krai's main restaurant, run by Katya, who also looks after the Conch Gang children and employs them. It sells hot dogs and other dishes, and a prize wheel outside gives daily fortunes. Completing a certain quest gives permanent discounts.

133.content: Stray children who live and work at Speranza with Katya's care and a great deal of freedom. Their legend is that kids once conquered Nasha Town and called meetings with a conch shell. New members need unanimous approval.

134.content: A once-notorious bandit gang said to have secretly controlled Nasha Town, taking in exiles from across Teyvat. A merchant, Ratfan, had its boss betrayed and killed and the gang scattered. Jahoda later avenged her boss. Imposters now use the name. Details come largely from Jahoda's account.

135.content: A commerce guild of local merchants and one of Nod-Krai's most powerful factions. It manages trade, issues business certificates and resolves disputes. Nefer is a member, and its headquarters sits directly in front of the Curatorium's. Tarno runs its souvenir outlet and represents it in the League.

136.content: An information-trading institution in town led by Nefer. Its second floor holds a reception and Nefer's office; the Traveler can later enter Nefer's secret room. Jahoda works for it. Loading screens call it a deep chasm of intelligence tied to a northlands-wide network.

137.comment: Nasha Town: Moon-Prayer Night in Nasha Town
137.content: A Nod-Krai festival held when the moon is closest to Teyvat and kuuvahki peaks. In The Night the Moon Returns Home, Nasha Town hosts it with games by the Hexenzirkel, the Frostmoon Scions and locals, including "Hundred-Flavored Moon-Prayer Candy", "Bitey the Frostfin Whale" and "Kuuhenki Concentration".

138.comment: Nasha Town: Siege of Nasha Town
138.content: In the climax of the Song of the Welkin Moon, Dottore's forces attacked Nasha Town after its civilians were evacuated. The Traveler and allies, with Nicole's help and Albedo and Durin posted to the town, repelled the attack before Dottore confronted them there as the Heretic of the False Moon. Afterward the town recovered and hosted the opening of a new League of factions.

139.content:
North Harbor: The North Harbor is one of two harbors serving the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle in Nod-Krai. A posted notice says its operation is suspended and cargo is rerouted to the South Harbor.

The notice tells anyone sending goods into the Design Bureau to use the South Harbor instead and promises a separate announcement of reopening.

Places: A dock for the Bureau's freight, now shut. Two readable items stand here: the official suspension notice and a notice board with scrawled complaints from workers.

One scrawl curses a Poruchik, Raskolnikov (name partly blacked out), over rules that forbid drinking; another orders machines to clean up before the Poruchik catches the staff holding a drinking party again. They suggest a strict officer and a crew that bends the rules.

People: No resident NPCs are listed. Raskolnikov, the Bureau officer named on the board, has his own entry.

Status as of 7.1: Closed to operations by notice as of the version read; goods go through the South Harbor. The sources read record no reopening by 7.1.

140.content:
Northern Training Ground (also: Vaino's training ground): The Northern Training Ground is a small obstacle-and-target course on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai, built by Vaino, a thirty-four-year-old former treasure hunter who has retired to run it. It offers light challenges such as shooting targets and dodging, and it has become tangled up with a cave of target-stealing Sniffer Moles the local children call the Hollowhands.

The course is on the map as the Northern Training Ground. A Hidden Exploration Objective in its southwest corner has three treasure hunters spar with the Traveler, and the Clink Clank Clash event quests of 6.0 begin here.

Geography: A landmark on Lempo Isle, with a teleport waypoint close to where Vaino stands; its map area is labelled Tundra Gap and includes two separate caverns. The course has three challenges: a first one near the waypoint, a second whose entrance Vaino marks, and a third he rebuilds during the quest. A cave elsewhere nearby holds the Hollowhands' trading box.

Some targets fly, and in the second half of the second challenge they move, so the Traveler must shoot on the run. The Hollowhands' cave has a box where Nasha Town's children leave goods for trade and a hidden nest chamber the moles treat as a treasure room.

People: Vaino is the owner, a retired treasure hunter who worries he is too old for the trade and hopes the course will bring in customers, especially children and Fatui stationed in Nod-Krai. Sisko, a girl from Nasha Town, tells the Traveler about the Hollowhands; Lalli and Bozena, two other townspeople, are asked about target-making materials. Terho, Bielov and Incali are treasure hunters who spar in the southwest corner.

Vaino gets the sales pitch he uses from Bozena, whom he credits with teaching it to him in Nasha Town. Terho is the boss of his small crew and, after losing, jokes that he might ask Vaino for a job.

Culture: Treasure-hunter humour and folklore surface here. A joke Vaino tells says the only place a thirty-five-year-old treasure hunter is called young is at their funeral. The children tell different stories about why the Hollowhands trade by having people count to seventy-seven with eyes closed: Sisko mentions Reed Miller stealing seventy-seven treasures from the governor's palace, while Bozena says it was seventy-seven loyal followers.

Paimon adds a joke version of her own. No source settles the number's origin.

History: Vaino built the course after leaving treasure hunting, using nearly all his savings. Vaino's targets kept vanishing from it; the quest reveals the Hollowhands, a group of Sniffer Moles, were taking them as bedding, and the children had been collecting materials to sell him new ones. In effect, Vaino paid again and again for the same targets.

After the quest Vaino chooses not to demand money back from the children, and says Sisko's feedback and friends coming to play are worth more than Mora. He has since worked out trading rates with the Hollowhands that leave him a decent profit.

Dangers: None of note. The sparring with Terho's crew is a friendly challenge, and the Sniffer Moles are harmless.

Atmosphere: Grassy and informal, with Vaino cheerfully self-deprecating and signs that spoil their own surprises. A relaxed tune that wiki notes call the training ground's unofficial theme, Loafing on the Grass, accompanies it by day.

Quests: The Stress of Changing Careers (World Quest) begins when the Traveler is stopped by Vaino near the teleport waypoint. After testing his three challenges and finding that his targets have been stolen, they use Old Portable Bearings from Nasha Town's children to trade with the Hollowhands, discover the moles, and help Vaino improve his final challenge. It unlocks the Hidden Exploration Objective Triple Training Time (the wiki's unofficial name) and an achievement.

The Clink Clank Clash quests An Adventurer's Woes, A Mysterious Outsourced Contract, Misplaced Creativity and The Last Step of Testing all start here during the event of 6.0.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the training ground is open and Vaino remains its boss. Nothing recorded after 7.1.

141.content: Vaino is a former treasure hunter, thirty-four, who has started a new career running a training ground in Nod-Krai. He is anxious about age and funerals, but friendly. He originally believed the Hollowhands were old enemies and nearly put his affairs in order before learning they are Sniffer Moles.

142.content:
The Hollowhands are a group of Sniffer Moles that live in a cave near the Northern Training Ground and trade with Nasha Town's children through a small box. The children leave goods, close their eyes and count to seventy-seven, and find a gift in return. The moles took Vaino's targets to line their nests.

Sisko thinks of them as an unseen, good kind of thief like Reed Miller and kept the trading rules secret. After the quest the moles continue to exchange goods; Vaino says he is still searching for a better nest material than his targets.

143.content:
Northland Bank (Nod-Krai) (also: Northland Bank Nasha Town branch, Nasha Town Northland Bank): This is the Nasha Town branch of the Northland Bank, the Snezhnayan bank with branches around Teyvat. It is managed by Jarosznski. From the outside it looks unremarkable, but its inside is a fortress of defenses and alarms.

Northland Bank hails from Snezhnaya and, according to a loading-screen text, the Fatui use its funds and sometimes its branches as bases when they operate abroad. The Nod-Krai branch is a regional office, separate from the bank's headquarters in Snezhnograd.

People: Jarosznski is the smooth-talking manager who sells loans. He greets visitors by offering a business loan or the "Happy Home Loan", which has zero interest for the first three installments. Asked about the catch, he says there are packages for different needs and that the bank needs a name, address, guarantor and a detailed three-month travel log, all to offer a more professional payment plan. Drahomira and Kamenka are listed as NPCs of the branch; Kudratov is an agent.

Jarosznski admits he doubted locals would pay but says the branch's reimbursement rate is higher than Fontaine's branches. He credits this to telling at-risk clients that Northland Bank will find "suitable" jobs for people who cannot pay their debts, after which, he jokes, they settle within days. Whether that means anything darker is not stated.

Places: The branch is a common-looking shopfront in Nasha Town that blends in with the town's other shops; the furnishing text describes a two-story building. The interior, per that text, is an intricately built fortress rigged with defenses and alarms that will teach trespassers a painful lesson.

The vault-like layout is a security measure, as the furnishing text says that security is paramount to a bank.

Atmosphere: A businesslike shopfront in a town otherwise built from scrap metal. Outwardly ordinary, it hides tight security behind polite offers of credit.

Governance: It belongs to the Northland Bank, a Snezhnayan institution, and acts as a branch office. The bank's map text names Regrator, Pantalone, the Ninth Fatui Harbinger, as the master of its web, but the Nasha Town branch is not shown doing Fatui work.

Wiki lore on the bank says it was founded by Pantalone and that new branches may be set up by other Harbingers; nothing specific is stated about who opened the Nasha Town branch.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the branch remains open in Nasha Town, with Jarosznski as manager.

144.content: Jarosznski is the manager of the Nasha Town Northland Bank. His idle line asks whether a customer needs a loan for their business. He is polite and persuasive, pushes the "Happy Home Loan", and deflects questions about the catch by pointing to flexible packages and a thorough personal history requirement.

145.content:
Nothing Passage: Nothing Passage is a narrow mountain pass cutting through the northern end of Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. A whole Fatui company, the 6th, was wiped out here after dubious experiments by two rival researchers of the Armory Palace; only one private, Smirnova, escaped. After the world quest series Colors of Emptiness the entire passage becomes a strong kuuvahki environment.

The Fatui sealed the area off as a Military Administrative Area under an Imperial Edict, and a weathered notice at its entrance still warns off intruders as hostile agents. Inside lie abandoned camps, dormant Landcruiser defence machines and a barrier controlled by authorisation terminals.

The pass is bound up with two things: the Fatui's competing kuuvahki research under the Tsaritsa's wishes, and the eerie coloured lights the Traveler follows in Colors of Emptiness (6.0).

Geography: A narrow pass through the mountains of northern Lempo Isle, with a Teleport Waypoint at its northern end. Abandoned Fatui camps lie along it, among them one southeast of the northern waypoint.

Inside the pass are patches of mist and a Fatui kuuvahki barrier whose authorisation terminals lock sections by ID card, a source of the researchers' feud. Moonlanes, red and blue kuuhenki and Unipolar Crystonite appear within it during the quest series, and the soldiers hunted goats in the surrounding hills.

History: The Fatui's 6th Company was posted here to guard two professors of the Armory Palace, Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky and V. A. Preobrazhensky, working on moon fragments reported to hold kuuvahki energy. Both wanted to be first to a breakthrough that would win praise from the Tsaritsa, and their rivalry became open hostility. The experiments ended in catastrophe: the whole company died except Private Elena Smirnova, who escaped to send the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau a distress call.

Private Pyotr Dmitriyevich Orlov's notes record the slide into disaster: the Poruchik posted him to the pass; Karnatsky despised Preobrazhensky, whom he called a lunatic and who is the fiance of his daughter; strange marks, a bitter cold and the smell of decay appeared; a goat was found living but transfixed, its eyes clouded; Karnatsky boasted of drawing out the purest primal light from a moon shard and tearing open the veil of the world. Orlov's last note, written near the end, blames the two men for waking the fallen moon rocks, says a 'color' devoured everything, and asks that Smirnova be cleared as no deserter. Karnatsky's own research notes, found in a camp, treat the energy of the 'Ancient Moon's Remnants' as a primordial life form that can be taught to feed on living things, and he plans to use it to plug the gaps left in Nod-Krai by Abyssal corruption.

People: No living residents. The dead are the 6th Company's soldiers, among them Private Orlov, Captain Volkov and a soldier named Petrenko in Orlov's diary, and the two researchers. Smirnova, the sole survivor, is covered in her own entry.

Orlov records Karnatsky calling the soldiers 'dim-witted lackeys', and Preobrazhensky answering a tirade by reeling off a diatribe in Fae, which Orlov could not understand. Karnatsky's own notes call Preobrazhensky a poor whelp of a fae.

Dangers: Defensive Landcruisers, recon bots, Fatui patrols and a kuuvahki barrier. After the disaster the pass is permeated by strange coloured presences: the Traveler is chased through it by glowing red and blue orbs that behave like some kind of life.

In Colors Out of Space the two orbs collide, pull the Traveler into a purple space of floating ruins, and leave the passage a strong kuuvahki environment. Afterwards Paimon, thrown elsewhere by the blast, does not know what the lights were.

Quests: Colors of Emptiness is a world quest series with Crimson Cleansing and Blues of the Old World (either order), then Colors Out of Space. The series is ambiguous: no one explains what the orbs are. Nothing Passage is also the meeting point where Lauma waits before the Traveler's infiltration of the Fatui's Experimental Design Bureau in In the Shadows of Night (Song of the Welkin Moon, Act I, 6.0).

Quest props include the Private's Notes (I-III), Preobrazhensky's messy note threatening Karnatsky over the authorisation terminal, and Karnatsky's research notes.

Atmosphere: Silent, cold and unnaturally still. Camps hold untouched bedrolls and the dust of a place that was left in a hurry; colour seems to drain and return in blue and red.

Travel: Reached from the north of Lempo Isle by the waypoint at the passage's mouth. The Fatui notice forbids entry, but the camps are empty.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fatui presence is gone from the passage, the dead company remains a mystery to the Fatui archive, and the pass sits as an eerie kuuvahki-saturated place.

No later quest through 7.1 resolves what the orbs were.

146.content: Two senior Armory Palace researchers, Karnatsky and Preobrazhensky, feuded over moon-fragment research in Nothing Passage while a Fatui company guarded them. Their experiments with moon fragments destroyed the company; Private Elena Smirnova alone escaped, at the cost of Volkov's life, to send a distress call. Private Orlov's notes say she was no deserter.

147.content:
Nuts 'N' Nuts: Nuts 'N' Nuts is a combined grocery and repair shop in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, run by Cairuo and Lestocq.

Cairuo sells the goods and her stock restocks daily; Lestocq is the shop's engineer. An alchemy bench stands in the shop. Completing the Archon Quest Rest Beyond Reach gives a 10% discount here, a gameplay reward.

People: Cairuo is the food merchant and vendor; Lestocq is the engineer who does the repair work.

The Chinese name translates as 'Nuts and Bolts', a pun that fits a shop selling food (nuts) and doing mechanical repairs (bolts).

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1; no change recorded.

148.content:
Nuur Stone Circle (also: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array, Silent Stone Circle): Nuur Stone Circle is an ancient dragon facility on the Frost Moon, in the Lunar Highlands, that records and stores the dragon researchers' data. Its tablets, once repaired, preserve notes about Project Moongazer, the Moongazers' backup research, and the plan to engrave a researcher's hopes into a data-born life that became Nin-Kiggia.

It was maintained by a dragon recorder, Nu-ur-Gestug ("Nuur"), who described himself as a recorder, not a researcher. The site also holds an Ancient Moon's Remnant, the Frost Moon's reputation shrine shared with Dunanna Pit, which unlocks after the quest Origin of the Sequence.

Geography: A subarea of the Lunar Highlands on the Frost Moon. It has a high-speed transport station, a teleport waypoint, underground halls and ruins, and viewpoints named "Silent Stone Circle". The Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index tablets stand in three places: inside an underground hall entered from a crater south of the transit station, near the waypoint, and in ruins north of the station.

Features include Archaeolune Energy Nodes and Surges, Ancient Moon Pearls, a Gravimeter, terminals, Secret Source Dragon Idols and high-speed transit lanes. Elite enemies include the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network and Surging Currents: Frostnight Scion. The player repairs four data-storage areas in the objective Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu to read the tablets.

Places: The Ancient Moon's Remnant hub; the three Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index tablets; the crater hall; a transit station connecting to other Lunar Highlands sites.

Index I is titled "Researches Concerning Life", Index II "Concerning the Engraving" and Index III "Researches Concerning Cognition". Each shows an expired index and asks the reader to contact Nu-ur-Gestug or Nin-Kiggia for the main text.

People: Nu-ur-Gestug, recorder of the system log; Lusalim and Maagees-Geti, authors of the research on self-sustaining informational processes; the dragon king Xiuhcoatl, who offered suggestions; Ibni-Belum, author of the "Engraving" orbital system. Nin-Kiggia refers to Nu-ur-Gestug as "Uncle", though not in a genetic sense.

Nu-ur-Gestug was not affiliated with Project Moongazer and opposed Project Lunar Veil, according to the wiki; he researched cognitive hazards as an alternative defence against the Abyss.

History: Index I's log records Nu-ur-Gestug's conclusion that Maagees-Geti was right: any system of sufficient complexity is computationally equivalent, so a simulated self-awareness is no different from organic consciousness. He writes that Lusalim proposed engraving a researcher's affections, desires and ideals into data so that an "immortal life" could re-emerge infinitely, even if no longer a dragon, to broadcast the Moongazers' ideals across the ages. Lusalim planned to name that life Nin-Kiggia, "messenger".

King Xiuhcoatl visited and showed interest, noting parallels with his own work to manifest life through phlogiston (computronium), hoping to bring the surface-dwelling dragons some relief. When Nu-ur-Gestug let slip Lusalim's plan, the king offered practical suggestions, which Nu-ur-Gestug forwarded to Lusalim despite regretting the lapse. Index II is Nu-ur-Gestug's public log about retrofitting the "Engraving", the orbital positioning facility in Nephilheim built by Ibni-Belum, as a backup storage array, ending with a wish that "the Creator", Nibelung, be crowned with supreme glory.

Atmosphere: Silent standing stones glowing with faint inscriptions, dim halls and ruined arrays; the feel is of an archive nobody has visited in an age.

Dangers: Frostnight Scions and the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix guardians, and Archaeolune Energy Surges.

Travel: Reached by the high-speed transit lane from other Lunar Highlands sites; the transit station is the site's anchor.

Quests: Origin of the Sequence unlocks the Ancient Moon's Remnant; Nuur Stone Circle quests add the Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu exploration objective.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the circle is a quiet ruin whose array can be repaired and read.

149.comment: Nuur Stone Circle: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index
149.content: The Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array Index is a set of three tablets that list the dragons' research and backup data. The listed items include research by Maagees-Geti and Lusalim, a completeness analysis based on computronium by Xiuhcoatl, and joint work by Lusalim and Nu-ur-Gestug. Their system logs are the source of how Nin-Kiggia came to be named.

150.content:
Paha Isle: Paha Isle is an island in the Southern Isles of Nod-Krai, accessible from 6.0. Once an unremarkable island known for sunset-hued salt marshes and Tassel Jellies, it changed when the heaviest fragment of the fallen moonstone crashed on its shores. It is now a staging ground for Fatui personnel in Nod-Krai, who work from the huge Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, and it also holds the Lightkeepers' abandoned Final Night Cemetery.

The two halves of the island contrast: a cold steel Fatui installation that dominates the landscape as a statement of power, and a lonely lighthouse outpost lit by a single Lightkeeper who looks after the dead.

Geography: Paha Isle is the island south of Voidsea Outlook across the water, part of the Southern Isles with Lempo Isle and Hiisi Island. The Design Bureau is a colossal structure of iron and stone built by the Fatui; the Final Night Cemetery lies around a lighthouse on the island. Local specialty: Frostlamp Flower.

The Bureau has several levels (top, middle, lower, bottom, a disposal workshop and a southern zone). The island's boss is the Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress.

Places: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau: the Fatui's high-tech complex. Final Night Cemetery: the former Lightkeeper outpost, lighthouse and burial ground, always dark.

In the Bureau, lower levels hold ordinary enemies, and the upper levels open during The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot; most combat areas trigger a 20-second alarm countdown that calls in reinforcements. The wiki suggests the Bureau's name echoes the Soviet-era 'OKB' design bureaus (an editor's note, not stated in the game). The cemetery has a lighthouse with a lamp signal handbook (distress, guidance, summoning and all-safe signals), a cooking stove, a monument, an engraved inscription and a tavern bulletin board.
