Atmosphere: Warm and busy, with hot food, young staff and a fortune wheel and a food-hunting dog outside. Katya keeps an eye on the children and is firm about not letting them be endangered.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Speranza is open, still run by Katya, and still the Conch Gang's base.

204.content: The Conch Gang is the group of stray children under Katya's care. Members include Auni, Semyon, Helka, Jurva, Maisie, Maite and Mikko; former members include Aino, Linnea and Tapani. A new member needs the agreement of all existing members, and the gang traditionally accepts children and asks members to leave at a certain age, though there is precedent for admitting an older person. Maite calls the Traveler an official friend of the gang during The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar.

205.content: Katya is the owner of Speranza, a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired after injuries. She welcomes visitors, sells food, jokes that the kids are happy to work for their share, and tells people to look elsewhere for treasure rumors. After The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, once only, she gives the Traveler Nod-Krai Hot Dogs and Fonta because of Maite's message.

206.comment: Speranza: Pavlov and the Lucky Spin
206.content: Pavlov is a dog at Speranza who asks guests to spin a wheel because, once it has been spun and stopped, good food falls. He is understood by people who can hear animals, such as Lauma and Columbina. Passers-by are allowed to spin the wheel too, but a notice reminds visitors that everything belongs to Speranza and Pavlov is watching.

207.content:
Starsand Shoal: Starsand Shoal is the western beach of Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. The wiki records it as the place where the spaceship of the Traveler and their sibling landed. Its expedition description says that when a dark disaster engulfed Nod-Krai many heroes made their last stand on these sands, and that the whispering waves still sing of their valor.

It lies in the Southern Isles on the island's west coast. Stones placed by the Lightkeepers, the Tideseal Stones, stand to its north and south to dispel the permeation of the Wild Hunt, and Wild Hunt pockets lie close by.

A small cluster of world content touches the shoal: a young reporter's notes recovered from the Fatui, a Remarkable Chest holding a boat-shaped workshop blueprint, and the first act of Durin's story quest A Mother's Last Wish.

Geography: Open sand and shallows on Lempo Isle's western edge, with a Teleport Waypoint near the middle. Tideseal Stones stand north and south of it, each with a Wild Hunt area.

A Remarkable Chest on the shoal holds the blueprint for Workshop Cabin: Ship Ashore, a boat-shaped sheet-metal building common around the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, said to be the result of a would-be iron ship that leaked before it left the shallows.

History: The in-game description ties the shoal to an unspecified past disaster: heroes made their final stand here when darkness overran Nod-Krai. The wiki records a later arrival: the Traveler's and their sibling's spaceship came down on this shore.

The Lightkeepers' Tideseal Stones north and south of the beach appear in the world quest The Bell of Mourning Echoes, in which the Traveler gathers relics from three stones to honour a local legend, Sigurd, and later in the hidden objective Secrets of the Tideseal Stones.

People: Semyon, a child near the waypoint, hopes to publish a report on the Fatui. Alice, as seen in A Mother's Last Wish, arranges a meeting with Durin on the shoal.

In the hidden objective Crimes Against Jelly-kind, Semyon asks the Traveler to retrieve notes the Fatui took, evidence of the Fatui's facilities and machines on Paha Isle that have driven out animals; he has just come back from Maroon Basin, where the jellyfish are barely hanging on. If the Traveler has finished Drifting Toward a Promised Sky and tells him what happened at Maroon Basin, Semyon concludes it is already too late but that the matter must still be reported. He asks the Traveler to credit him by name if they repeat the story.

Quests: Crimes Against Jelly-kind (hidden objective, unofficial name; rewards Semyon's Notes and the Ice Cream Cutie blueprint), The Bell of Mourning Echoes and Secrets of the Tideseal Stones (Tideseal Stones nearby), and the start of A Mother's Last Wish (6.2).

In A Mother's Last Wish the Traveler meets Durin amid fallen Radiant Beasts on the shoal, after Alice's invitation; Durin says the Abyssal power in him is stable since Albedo gave him his body but that his strength has been harder to control recently. Alice draws them into a story world made from the book of Durin's late mother, the author Anya "Marie" Andersdotter.

Dangers: Wild Hunt creatures patrol the areas by the Tideseal Stones; Radiant Beasts appear in A Mother's Last Wish.

Atmosphere: Sea wind and pale sand; waves quietly breaking where old battles were fought.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an open beach on Lempo Isle's west coast, with Lightkeeper stones holding the Wild Hunt at bay.

Nothing in the pages read marks any change to the shoal after 6.2.

208.content:
Thunderclap Reef: Thunderclap Reef is a rocky reef in the southwest of Hiisi Island, Nod-Krai. Its kuuvahki has been unstable since at least 500 years ago, giving it a strong kuuvahki environment, and the Frostmoon Scions treat it as a forbidden place. Two large Moon Fragments fell there recently and made things worse.

In the world quest For a Green Island..., the Traveler and Paimon help the self-styled priestess Verna remove the fragments and partly stabilise the kuuvahki. Afterwards the weather there is perpetually rainy.

Geography: A rocky reef on the southwest of Hiisi Island, with caves, a high summit and a Moon Mirror at the top. Before the quest the area is a red strong kuuvahki environment.

During the quest the environment turns into a stormy one with lightning, which can be deflected with the Airspace Data Collector 2.0. After the quest it becomes a blue strong kuuvahki environment.

People: Verna, a young woman in Frostmoon robes who calls herself a priestess and the finest mechanic on Hiisi Island, works here with small helper robots named Kraka (models III, V and VII appear). She says she is a direct apprentice of the mechanic known as Papa Wrench.

She describes her work as a secret mission to restore the reef's kuuvahki balance, and says she cannot bring others because they lack her resistance; her robes ward off kuuvahki, and she says she gets nosebleeds without them. A second robed woman, who speaks in cryptic prayers, waits at the Moon Mirror; Verna accuses her of impersonating a Moonchanter.

History: Verna says the kuuvahki at the reef has been unstable since the time of the first Moonchanter, Lady Aila, and that the trouble grew worse after two large rocks fell from the sky.

The quest plan is to throw kuuvahki-charged fragments at the two boulders to cancel the disturbance. The first attempts flip the kuuvahki into what Verna calls a reversed chaotic state, and a third fragment, held by the robed woman at the Moon Mirror, is needed to calm it. A Frostnight Scion awakens at the mirror and must be defeated.

Dangers: Strong, unstable kuuvahki, and (during the quest) lightning storms. Cave collapses also occur; one blocks the original exit while the Traveler and Paimon search for fragments.

Quests: For a Green Island... (world quest, chapter Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle): begins automatically when approaching the reef. The wiki also lists Animal Research: Chic Badgers and Everlasting As the Moon as touching the area; they are not summarised here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the reef's kuuvahki is partly stabilised but still strong, and rain is constant.

209.comment: Thunderclap Reef: For a Green Island...
209.content: In this world quest Verna recruits the Traveler and Paimon to calm the reef by throwing fragments at two boulders. The plan briefly makes the kuuvahki worse; then a robed woman holding the final fragment at the Moon Mirror lets them have it, cryptically speaking of a newborn "god" and saying she will await them at the Court of the First Edict. The kuuvahki is afterwards somewhat steadier and the weather turns rainy.

210.content:
Traveler's Crater (also: Wayfarer's Crater): Traveler's Crater is the huge crater on the Frost Moon in whose centre the Traveler's spaceship rests. Columbina led the Traveler here in Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3), when it was a quest-only location, and from the Moon Gazing quests (6.7) it can be visited freely. Teyvat hangs in the sky above it.

The viewpoint here is called The Next Journey. The crater can be reached by the High-Speed Transit Lane from the Nuur Stone Circle.

Geography: A wide lunar crater under low gravity, with the star-shaped, white-and-gold spaceship standing at its centre. Columbina first reached it on foot across the lunar plain, after crossing a path of moonlight and a boat on a lake of Moon-Prayer Blossoms from Teyvat.

Atmosphere: Open lunar ground under a sky where the world of Teyvat is visible. Columbina remarks that she could spend a whole day looking at Teyvat from here, and that she took off her eye mask to see it.

History: The Heavenly Principles hid the spaceship on the Frost Moon after the Cataclysm. Columbina sensed it after she became the Trilune Goddess and took the Traveler there. The Traveler read the logs aboard, collected an old outfit, and learned that the ship had flown over Teyvat once, much earlier, without landing. See the spaceship entry for details.

Quests: Visited during Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3), then made permanently available in the Moon Gazing quests. A post-quest conversation with Columbina here follows Project Moongazer (Part 2).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the crater is open and the spaceship remains where the Heavenly Principles placed it.

Columbina told the Traveler she was unsure why it was hidden here and urged them to go in alone while she waited, humming a tune. When the Traveler came out, they said the truth was neither good nor bad, and that they considered Teyvat their home.

211.content:
Underground Energy Generation Station: The Underground Energy Generation Station is one of three stations that generate energy for the Eye of Ibni-Belum on the Frost Moon. It makes Ancient Moon Pearls, spheres that store and transport Archaeolune Energy.

After Pioneers (Part 2), its terminal shows a dedication to Ibni-Belum, the pioneer who went ahead of everyone, "the first Moongazer", for his contributions to Project Moongazer.

Geography: It lies below the ground in the Eye of Ibni-Belum area. The Ancient Moon Pearls can be rolled around and pushed into power stations, which then pass the energy along Archaeolune Energy Pathways to run machinery.

In-game, a pearl cannot be moved after it is packed in a container, and a launcher can fire pearls (or characters standing in it) into the air to reach otherwise inaccessible places. These mechanics are exploration gameplay, not lore.

History: The station is part of the power supply of the Eye of Ibni-Belum, the facility from which the Moongazers' message is later sent into space. Beyond the terminal dedication, canon gives no building date or builder for this station.

Status as of 7.1: Ancient and explorable as of 7.1.

212.content:
Underground Research Center (also: Secret Research): The Underground Research Center is a classified Fatui research site below the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle in Nod-Krai. It holds experiments on kuuvahki, the lunar energy, and collects data from three surface hubs to study how to generate high-density energy barriers.

The Traveler finds it through the world quest Priorities First (Version 6.0). It is a Strong Kuuvahki Environment. A notice there says Command raised the alert level because of recent suspicious activity around the Design Bureau, to protect military secrets and personnel.

Geography: The center is reached from the Paha Isle surface by an entrance and a long elevator shaft that descends well underground. The first area has a sealed barrier and moving barrier traps, and a further elevator leads deeper to the laboratory.

The quest begins when the Traveler defeats the Cutting Edge All-Purpose Storm Landcruiser in the center. One door then stays shut, so the party takes another elevator deeper. Three data collection hubs on the surface of Paha Isle feed the center, each yielding a Data Storage Cassette.

Places: The laboratory holds many jars of what looks like kuuvahki, a large jar in the center, piles of papers and experiment machines. Notices and notes here include an alert from Command raising the security level, a research log and a set of research records, all describing barrier tests.

The research log mentions a tenth stability experiment on the barrier generator, a prototype now a third of its original size, and an energy bottleneck, and its writer's transfer request being refused because the project is highly classified. The research records state that harnessing kuuvahki to produce high-density energy barriers of various shapes, including spheres, has been proven feasible, but long, intense use causes overheating, material fatigue and slight energy leakage whose long-term effects are uncertain.

People: Only unseen researchers are present; one log writer complains about sharing a space with those who tinker with plants and animals. The Fatui officer Kholodov, a Podporuchik, arrives with soldiers when the party submits the data, and accuses them of being the criminals who ruined an experiment site.

Quests: In Priorities First, the party gathers three data cassettes from the surface hubs, enters the lab and submits them. A large barrier traps them inside and Kholodov's Fatui attack; the Traveler breaks the barrier and defeats them. Afterwards the machine shows no result, and a white Weasel Thief steals Paimon's Mora.

The quest ends with the thief running off. Later, at Speranza, the Conch Gang children catch it and return the Mora. The quest also awards the achievement Tempus Fugit, Pecunia Fugit.

Dangers: Sealed and moving barriers, the Cutting Edge All-Purpose Storm Landcruiser at the entrance, Force Recon Scout Landcruisers around the data hubs, and the Fatui who arrive when the data is submitted.

Atmosphere: A sunless place of glass jars, machines and dry bureaucratic notes. Paimon jokes that the lack of sunlight is meant to stop workers from knowing when to clock off.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a Fatui research facility; the quest's results were never revealed.

213.comment: Underground Research Center: Data Storage Cassettes
213.content: The three data collection hubs on Paha Isle store experiment data on cassettes. The Traveler collects them and inputs them into the lab's computer. The data tracks high-density energy barrier generation; submitting it triggers a barrier that traps the party inside.

214.content: Kholodov is a Podporuchik of the Fatui who commands the soldiers that trap the party in the lab. He is angry because the Traveler had ruined an experiment site, and he is defeated in combat. The wiki does not give further background.

215.content:
Ungien's Circle (also: Ungien Biosphere, Sanctuary of Life, Bad-Uru-Namu-Ungien's biosphere): Ungien's Circle is a living biosphere built on the Frost Moon by the dragon life scientist Bad-Uru-Namu-Ungien. Seen from space it is a yellowed crater, and inside it plants, creatures and the kuuhenki thrive while the rest of the moon is barren and storm-lashed. It was a home for living beings on the moon, and it is where the Traveler and Eggie learn what became of Ungien (Visitors From the Stars, 6.7).

Its loading-screen description calls it a place holding Ungien's conviction, later passed on to the mistress of the greenhouse. A giant tree grows at its heart, and above it floats the Space Lifeform Capture Station.

Geography: The only region of the Frost Moon not subject to the low-gravity effects of turbulent Archaeolune Energy. Its landscape includes a large tree, vine-choked turbines, a Power Engine that must be restarted, a Transit Station with a waypoint, and a Skymount lift to the Space Lifeform Capture Station in orbit overhead. Moonlit Vines and Knotted Moonlit Vines grow thickly; kuuhenki, including Wondrous Black Kuuhenki, live there.

Local specialties and hazards match the rest of the moon: Teardrop of the Moon, Archaeolune Energy surges, Pioneer Source Structures, and Precursor's Secret Source Matrix guardians, along with Geo Slimes, Cryo Whopperflowers and Stretchy Geo Fungi.

Places: Ungien's Circle: Power Engine (the turbines whose vines the Traveler clears), Ungien's Circle: Transit Station (waypoint), the Skymount (elevator) and the Space Lifeform Capture Station above. The last station contains a main observation room with a model showing Teyvat and its three moons, a gravity control room, the capture arm and the wreck of the Moongazer, the dragons' ship.

A terminal inside the Circle holds a note from a teacher who calls his pupil Ungien a rebellious, obdurate mule who respects neither teacher nor king, saved only by talent; it credits Ibni-Belum with design and engineering support.

History: Ungien, a dragon life scientist and the pupil of Ibni-Belum, built the biosphere. He and his partner Maagees-Geti worked on the Frost Moon. After the Eye of Ibni-Belum recorded a new deep-space signal, Ungien flew the Moongazer to find its source. He returned fused with a creature from space, a data-based lifeform carrying a message of hope from a dying civilisation. He delivered the message and died. Maagees used an experimental method to convert him into an enormous kuuhenki of pure Archaeolune Energy, called Ungie.

Maagees's study of that visitor is credited as the foundation on which Eggie was later born. The Space Lifeform Capture Station was Ungien's, built to catch creatures from space.

Atmosphere: A sheltered pocket of life in an otherwise stormy, low-gravity moon: overgrown vines, great dragon machines and kuuhenki, with normal gravity underfoot.

Quests: Visitors From the Stars (Part 1) leads the Traveler and Eggie here by transit lane, helps kuuhenki fend off monsters, restores the power engine and ends at the Skymount. Part 2 reveals Ungien's fate. The Circle also appears in Project Moongazer (Part 2), where Columbina names it as one of the stops on the path of the project.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Circle still stands, its machinery working, vines cleared from the turbines, and kuuhenki living in it.

216.content: Ungien was a dragon life scientist of the Frost Moon; Maagees-Geti was his partner and fellow researcher. After his death delivering a message from a dying civilisation, Maagees transformed what remained of him into Ungie, a huge artificial kuuhenki. Their pupil Lusalim later collated the group's research. Both are named as benefactors by Nin-Kiggia's recording in Project Moongazer (Part 2).

217.comment: Ungien's Circle: Space Lifeform Capture Station
217.content: An orbital station above Ungien's Circle where Ungien intended to hold creatures from space. The Traveler reaches it by the Skymount and is weightless inside; the Moongazer lies wrecked there.

218.content:
Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse: The Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse is a flower shop in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, run by Richeza.

It sells local specialties and cooking ingredients, and Richeza's stock restocks every three days.

People: Richeza is the employee who runs the shop and its vendor; Viljami is also listed at the location.

Culture: The name is Serbo-Croatian in style; the wiki glosses it as "Heralds of Spring".

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1; no change recorded.

219.content:
Voidsea Outlook: Voidsea Outlook is the area at the southern end of Pohjola, the large northern island of Nod-Krai, north of Paha Isle (added in 6.3). It holds Piramida, the mountain city that is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers, and Dreadshade Mire, a fog-choked swamp where an ancient Abyssal evil is sealed behind three stone pillars.

Together with the Southern Isles, Piramida is one of the most populated places in Nod-Krai. The area mixes a living, watchful military city with a hazardous swamp the Lightkeepers have posted warnings around.

Geography: Voidsea Outlook lies at Pohjola's southern edge, facing the Southern Isles across the water. Piramida stands on a mountain around a huge lighthouse; Dreadshade Mire spreads as a swamp whose thick fog limits visibility and is edged with warning signboards.

Local specialty: Winter Icelea. The swamp has wild plants (Cottonspring Flowers, Glimmerfruit, Mandragora, Spirebloom) and wildlife (Slothsheep). Puzzles here include Abyssal Fog Barriers, Lunar Conflux Barriers and Overflowing Abyssal Power.

Places: Piramida: a city built atop an ancient castle; Lightkeeper headquarters. Dreadshade Mire: a fog-shrouded swamp, the prison of the Serpent of All Evils.

In Piramida: the Torchforger Statue, honouring Solovei the Torchforger, the founding Starshyna; a grand mead hall at the top, with a long table for feasts after victories; and a bulletin board for Ratniki notices. A note headed 'Prospector's Command' found in the swamp tells its reader to find new sealing pillars, observe whether the kuuvahki there behave unusually, gather data and avoid alerting the Lightkeepers; its author is not named in the sources read.

People: The Lightkeepers: volunteer soldiers called Ratniki under squad leaders, sergeant majors and the Starshyna (currently Nikita), who is based in Piramida. In the swamp, Lightkeeper observers such as Janusz and Oskari appear in the world quest.

Beryna, an open-world NPC, stands beside an oven in the area. After the hidden exploration objective A Memory of Warmth, she grants the recipe for Mushroom Phantasm (a dish that needs mushrooms, rye flour, onions and Midsommar Berries).

Governance: Piramida is the seat of the Lightkeepers, an order founded 500 years ago by royal edict of Anastasya as an autonomous military body within Nod-Krai. Command runs from the Starshyna through Sergeant Majors to Squad Leaders and Ratniki. Because the order is stretched thin, outsiders sometimes view its headquarters as aloof, and relaying information to it is said to be hard.

Members swear an oath when they join, promising to use their bones and blood as fuel so that life may be made greater than death. Every Ratnik carries an Oath Lantern that lets other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna detect them.

Culture: Lightkeeper culture centres on the vow to keep a light burning in the long night: a nightingale holding a burning wick is their traditional insignia. Banquets in the mead hall celebrate victories and honour the fallen; by long custom the first pour of the feast is offered to the dead.

The banquet form comes from the old Snezhnayan court but has changed beyond recognition. In-game character interactions (Flins, Illuga) show how generations of members regard the statue and the feasts; Illuga recalls helping in the kitchens as a youth, before he joined, and not understanding why older members wept after a few drinks.

History: Piramida was built atop the ancient ruins of Prokhor Trubetskoy's castle, with a giant golden-age lighthouse at its centre. The Lightkeepers have made it their headquarters since their founding by Solovei. Dreadshade Mire is where Solovei and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, imprisoned the Serpent of All Evils with three ancient stone seals.

The Serpent was once Raimo, a rare human high official in the days of the Belyi Tsar and a friend and disciple of Rotwang. On Rotwang's behalf he used coercion, entrapment and murder against his master's rivals. After Rotwang's defeat he became the Serpent and was sealed in the mire. The three pillars each carry an inscription naming one of his sins: using relatives as hostages in political schemes, spreading slander to exploit the nobility's arrogance, and pushing others to a point of no return.

Atmosphere: Piramida: a tiered mountain city under a vast sky, the beacon of the lighthouse, long tables and the statue overhead; a feeling of old duty and fellowship. Dreadshade Mire: grey fog, dead water, glowing sealing pillars and the sense of being watched.

Dangers: Dreadshade Mire is marked by Lightkeeper notice signs as extremely dangerous; entry is discouraged because of low visibility and roaming Wild Hunt creatures. Elite enemies include Fishers of Hidden Depths, Wilderness Exiles and Radiant Glacial Wolves; pale-furred wolves and Treasure Hoarders are the ordinary threats.

The Serpent of All Evils summons Abyssal enemies, including Evil Eyes of Blightseep, Wasteland Wild Hunt enemies and Fishers of Hidden Depths, during its boss fight.

Travel: South: Paha Isle across the water. North: Wavechaser Plain and then Ashveil Peak. Piramida has a Meeting Point and bulletin boards; teleport waypoints connect the area to the rest of Nod-Krai.

Quests: To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner (world quest, 6.3): in Dreadshade Mire the Traveler investigates three sealing pillars and defeats the Serpent of All Evils. Nightingale's Song, the Nod-Krai quest series, also uses Piramida.

Before the quest the pillars are cleared of Wild Hunt enemies and Abyssal riftlines; absorbing spirebloom in the final fight grants a light-blade charge that can strike Abyssal enemies hard. At the end of the later quest The Last Night, the First Light, the Serpent of All Evils joins the Ultimate Calamity in the final fight against the Traveler and Illuga.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is open; the Serpent of All Evils has been defeated in the world quest, and Piramida remains the Lightkeepers' stronghold.

After Nightingale's Song, Piramida appears in a different state from before. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the area.

220.content:
Piramida is the city of the Lightkeepers, built on a mountain around a giant golden-age lighthouse. Its namecard line reads that in the blackest of nights, a lamp shall rise. A statue of Solovei the Torchforger stands in it; a mead hall at its top holds the Lightkeepers' feasts.

By the testimony of Nikita it stands on the ruins of Prokhor Trubetskoy's castle. Its appearance differs before and after the quest Nightingale's Song.

221.content:
Dreadshade Mire is a fog-shrouded swamp where Solovei, the Torchforger, and Aila, first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, sealed the Serpent of All Evils with three ancient stone seals. Lightkeeper signboards warn that entry is not advised.

Each pillar carries ancient incantations that list one of the Serpent's three great sins and bind it to stone and spell. Wild Hunt creatures patrol the mire.

222.content:
Wavechaser Plain: Wavechaser Plain is the central, coastal plain of Pohjola, the large island of northern Nod-Krai (added in 6.3). It holds the Pillar of Embla, a tower that the scholar Rotwang built to break the sky, the Knights of Favonius outpost Favonius Keep, the lake Amsvartnir and the barrier islands of the Wing of Keres.

Past and present sit side by side here: an Abyssal tower from the Cataclysm, Frostmoon Scion relics, and the tents of Mondstadt's knights, whose Grand Master's expedition made camp in Nod-Krai.

Geography: A wide plain beside the sea in the middle of Pohjola, bordered by Voidsea Outlook to the south and Ashveil Peak to the north. The Pillar of Embla rises from it, Lake Amsvartnir lies north of Piramida, and the Wing of Keres is a chain of barrier islands off the western side.

Local specialties: Winter Icelea and Pine Amber. The plain has a Radiant Moongecko as a boss. Exploration features include Moonlane paths, Lunar Conflux Barriers and Abyssal riftline puzzles, and the Pillar of Embla has Abyssal Fog Barriers, Abyssal Riftlines, Evil Eyes of Blightseep and Solaris Core puzzles.

Places: Pillar of Embla: a divine pillar rooted in the earth and reaching skyward, built by Rauthvangi. Favonius Keep: the Knights' camp. Lake Amsvartnir: a lake with a sacred forest and a legend of a hidden court. Wing of Keres: barrier islands with Verdant Crests and other Frostmoon Scion artifacts.

The pillar's loading-screen text says its presence has caused irreversible changes to the surroundings over the last five hundred years. Amsvartnir's name echoes the Old Norse lake where a wolf was bound. A viewpoint at the lake is called Palaces of Times Bygone. Ancient Handwriting appears at the lake during the quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song. The Wing of Keres hides a letter in a time capsule tied to the quest A Distant Dream of Elysium.

People: Favonius Keep is staffed by the Knights of Favonius Expedition Team: Garrison Commander Anselm and Knights including Ekbert, Erminie, Laurent, Leifhelm, Nannina and Winfried; Godwin joins after Varka's story quest.

In Tower of Inversion the Traveler works with Illuga, the Lightkeeper Vlaicu; at the top of the tower the quest steps have the Traveler talk to the historical Alia.

Governance: No local government. The Knights of Favonius run the Keep as an expeditionary garrison, and Lightkeepers watch the surroundings.

History: Five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm, Rauthvangi (known at the Belyi Tsar's court as Rotwang) came to Nod-Krai and raised the Pillar of Embla to reach the false sky and open the way to the Abyss, which he called his 'Elysium'. The Scourge of Endless Decay aided him. According to Frostmoon Scion records, Aila went to the pillar at Solovei's request and ended the Abyssal catastrophe.

The Lost Notes give a later layer: a group from Mondstadt following Master Roland, a knight devoted to chivalry, marched west expecting to end their campaign in Natlan but did not. In Nod-Krai they met monster hunters calling themselves the Lightkeepers, who invited them to join; Roland refused, saying the land must be cleansed with blood, and that people who seize chances to rob, and desperate outlaws, were targets of the purge. The Lightkeepers lent the group a lighthouse as shelter. Abyssal monsters pressed in and locals avoided them. The author, the last of the group, held the lighthouse alone after refusing local help, while Roland went to track monsters.

Atmosphere: Salt wind off the sea, a tall pillar dominating the skyline, ruined stone, the smell of dandelion wine at the Keep and the sense of old failures. The Lost Notes' tone is exhausted and conflicted: the writer doubts whether the campaign saves people or merely kills.

Dangers: Wild Hunt and Abyssal enemies, Abyssal Riftlines and Fog Barriers around the pillar, and, among the Wing of Keres islands, Evil Eye of Blightseep puzzles. Pale-furred wolves roam Amsvartnir.

Travel: Favonius Keep has a Meeting Point at the large tent. The road runs from Voidsea Outlook north through the plain toward Ashveil Peak.

Quests: Tower of Inversion (world quest, Nightingale's Song Act I, part 2; 6.3): the Traveler and Illuga enter the Pillar of Embla, purify its core and restore its barrier cores. It leads into When War Songs Rise in Ashveil Peak. Echoes of a Forsaken Song, the quest that unlocks the Ancient Handwriting, also touches the lake.

Inside the tower, the Traveler cleanses corruption from three cores (south, east, north) and then touches the top core, after which they talk to Alia, a historical figure. Completing the quest earns the Silver Lampwick.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the plain is open to explore; the Pillar of Embla has been cleansed and the Knights' camp remains.

Varka returned to Mondstadt in 6.4 but still travels to the outpost. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the plain.

223.content:
A tower built by Rauthvangi (Rotwang) to reach the false sky and ascend to his 'Pitch-black Elysium'. Aila ended the catastrophe at Solovei's request, 500 years ago, and the pillar still shapes its surroundings. It appears in a corrupted and a cleansed form.

Rauthvangi was a Khaenri'ahn scholar exiled for his obsession with the Abyss who later entered the Belyi Tsar's court; he was killed by the Traveler and Illuga in the later quest The Last Night, the First Light.

224.content:
The Knights of Favonius' outpost and expedition camp in Nod-Krai, with a large tent as its Meeting Point. Its map text describes warm dandelion-wine-scented breezes and a quote about stories gathering wherever people live.

See the Mondstadt entry for the Varka expedition. Garrison Commander Anselm leads the Expedition Team stationed there.

225.content: A lake north of Piramida, above which the Royal Court of the Seelie is said to lie. Legend says whoever breaks the golden branch in the lake's sacred forest finds the court, which is hidden from mortal eyes by day.

226.content: The barrier islands on the western side of Wavechaser Plain, decorated with Verdant Crests and other Frostmoon Scion artifacts. The name probably alludes to the winged death spirits of Greek myth (an editor's note, not stated in the game).

227.content:
Wing of Keres: Wing of Keres is the name for the barrier islands on the western side of Wavechaser Plain in Nod-Krai. They are decorated with Verdant Crests and other artifacts of the Frostmoon Scions. A buried time capsule written by Hyperborean engineers is the main thing to find there.

The islands are a place for exploration: free kuuhenki, ride Moonlanes and solve Abyss and kuuvahki puzzles. The wiki suggests the name alludes to the keres of Greek myth.

Their one piece of story is the Hyperborean time capsule letter, a first-hand glimpse of Hyperborea's outlook during the Elysium Project.

Geography: A string of barrier islands off the western shore of Wavechaser Plain, within Pohjola. Winter Icelea grows here, and the islands are connected by Moonlanes, with kuuhenki in the north, west and south.

Puzzles include the Evil Eye of Blightseep (west) and The Solaris Core and Nycalyx (south). Hilichurls and a Blazing Axe Mitachurl hold the northern kuuhenki.

History: No local history of the islands themselves is given in the pages read. The Verdant Crests and Frostmoon Scion artifacts imply the Scions' presence, and a letter buried in a time capsule shows that Hyperborean people also left something here.

In the letter, written to a distant successor, the author says it is the tenth year since Hyperborea began the 'Elysium Project'; that all the clans have united to shape the world into an Elysium for humankind alone; that they follow Dawn's Navigator (Koitar) and the Exalted Saint (Anacharsis); and that they have mastered the Tekhneikos of tailoring Seeds of Life, so adjusted new humans wield elemental forces at will. The author hopes the successors command the elements freely, no longer need the Firmament's gifts, and have broken through the limits of the firmament.

Quests: A Distant Dream of Elysium (unofficial name, hidden exploration objective, 6.3): free three kuuhenki in any order, then ride the Moonlane, which completes the objective (chests and the achievement The Mound in the Moonlight). Afterwards the mound of dirt near the chests can be examined to read the Letter Buried in the Time Capsule.

Dangers: Evil Eyes of Blightseep and a small group of hilichurls, including a Blazing Axe Mitachurl, in the north.

Atmosphere: Offshore islets by the sea, dotted with Frostmoon Scion crests and white kuuhenki gliding along the Moonlanes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the islands are an unpopulated exploration site; the time capsule has been unearthed.

Nothing in the pages read changes their state through 7.1.

key: Letter Buried in the Time Capsule
228.comment: Wing of Keres: Hyperborean Time Capsule
228.content: A letter buried at Wing of Keres by a Hyperborean author, addressed to a successor in a far brighter era. Written in the tenth year of the Elysium Project, it describes a united civilisation led by Dawn's Navigator and the Exalted Saint, advanced Tekhneikos and Mekhaneikos, and hopes of reaching the true cosmos.

229.content:
The Witch's Garden (also: Witch's Garden, Wonderland in the Rabbit Hole): The Witch's Garden is a garden point of interest in Voidsea Outlook, Nod-Krai, introduced in version 6.3. It holds the Witch's Lodge, one of the secret homes of the Hexenzirkel mage Nicole, and has a Meeting Point of the same name beside a statue before the bridge. Its map description stresses that the garden's sculptures are ordinary and hold no time-stopping magic.

Visitors reach it through Nicole's Witch's Lodge world quest, which she presents as a tale about a grand mage called Nicola Coco. Over the following versions the lodge became a small treasure-hunt house with rooms that open one at a time. Nicole treats the place as both a hobby and a trap for the curious: help is offered to those who do their own work.

Within Nod-Krai it works as a quiet, whimsical corner more than a threat. It is tied to Nicole personally, and its theme is a mage's show of power that she keeps deliberately gentle.

Geography: The garden lies in the Voidsea Outlook area of Nod-Krai, which the wiki locates at the southern end of the island Pohjola, north of Paha Isle. A bridge leads toward the lodge; the Meeting Point statue stands before it.

A statue of a squirrel and several carved animals, including finches and a squirrel carving, appear in the quest storyline. Nicole says the statues are her way of capturing a moment in time. The viewpoint description calls the decorations ordinary sculpture with no power to stop time, and describes the secret garden as a place without secrets, which comments ironically on Fate.

Places: The Witch's Lodge is the only listed point of interest inside the garden. The Meeting Point (level 5 unlocks a final Nicole conversation, Witch's Chatter) sits by the bridge-side statue.

After The Joyous Floating Island the lodge interior opens: a tea room with oversized teapots and a Mandragora statue, a study with a painting, a studio with an angel statue, a tall study with bookshelves, and a hidden room that overlooks the world. Each new quest unlocks another room, and the hidden room bears a resemblance to structures at the Temple of Space.

People: Nicole is the only resident, and she is often absent. Post-quest lines have her say she is away (in one set, in Sumeru), leaving tea on the table; during The Lost Palace she says she is running a sculpture stall in Fontaine. Paimon and the Traveler are her usual guests.

Nicole mentions friends from the Hexenzirkel, among them Alice, Anya and Barbeloth, and says Mr. Nine could help finish her writing. Her mention of the nearby Curatorium of Secrets and its member Nefer is a plain pointer for uninvited greedy visitors.

Culture: In the Witch's Homework conversation Nicole serves a tea party where the teapot stays half full and a fresh cake or cookie is always on each plate, which she explains as keeping a mage's elegance. She also says guidance can breed complacency and entitlement if given carelessly.

History: The Witch's Garden opened with Luna IV (6.3, released 2026-01-14), together with its Witch's Lodge quest and Meeting Point. The hidden Beyond Silver and Fine Gold quest series, with new rooms, arrived with Luna VII (6.6, 2026-05-20), the same version as Nicole's release.

In the Witch's Lodge quest the Traveler and Paimon photograph local subjects for statue ideas, drive off an enraged Mandragora, and carve a squirrel statue together with Nicole two days later. Nicole then tells her improvised tale of Nicola Coco, a mage who turns out to be a princess from Planet Meow, and says every creation eventually escapes its creator's control.

Quests: Witch's Lodge (6.3) opens the area; Witch's Chatter follows at Meeting Point level 5. Beyond Silver and Fine Gold (6.6) has four weekly parts, The Joyous Floating Island, The Silent Theater, The Lost Palace and The Forgotten Lighthouse. A Window Into the World and Witch's Homework: The Role of a Guide...? add the hidden room and an extra conversation.

The quest series is spaced out: after finishing a room, the next unlocks at 04:00 the following Monday, and the whole set takes about four weeks. Each quest ends with a treasure chest whose Mora and other rewards Nicole says have been fully handed over, joking that more will take a few hundred years.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the garden is open. Nicole is a playable character and Hexenzirkel member as of 6.6, and the lodge remains available.

No canon through 7.1 shows the garden damaged, abandoned or changed in function.

Atmosphere: Warm, whimsical and theatrical: tea on the table, carved animals standing in the open, a mage who narrates herself as grand while clearly enjoying the audience. The sense is of a theatre set the owner built for visitors, not a fortress.

Music tied to the area includes the tracks After Tea Party and Seelieland Nocturne from the album Where Roads Are Pledged to Cross.

Dangers: The only hostile encounters in the lodge storyline are a Mandragora (including a giant Mandragora statue that Nicole animates) and the puzzle statues. Nicole says she does not turn people into statues, though she jokes she might.

Travel: It is reached on foot in Voidsea Outlook, and the Meeting Point acts as a waypoint. Quest rooms are entered through the lodge doors; in the hidden-room storyline the lodge is described as containing more space than its outside shows.

230.comment: The Witch's Garden: Nicole's Witch's Lodge quest
230.content:
The Witch's Lodge world quest begins when the Traveler enters the garden and hears a narrated story about a runaway who falls into a secret home. The voice belongs to Nicole, who calls herself Nicola Coco, the Great Mage Everlasting. She asks for photographs of lively subjects to inspire statues, and later shows the Traveler how to carve blocks using number clues. The finished lodge appears beside the bridge. Her story is improvised, ends with Planet Meow and a cat-turned protagonist, and she says this is a creation that outgrew its author.

Nicole uses a Mandragora, finches and a squirrel statue as models. Post-quest she gives randomised dialogue about building several homes, hiding in Sumeru, and missing the angels as a people. Treat the Planet Meow tale as in-world fiction told by Nicole, not as lore.

231.comment: The Witch's Garden: Beyond Silver and Fine Gold
231.content:
This four-part world series unlocks the lodge's rooms, each with a treasure hunt for three golden feathers. In the tea room Nicole shrinks the party for the Great Mage's Tea Party. The studio frames show her joining the Hexenzirkel after an invitation from Alice and, according to the quest, the first angel Koitar's betrayal beneath an Irminsul. The Lost Palace room is a shrine she says was her home as an angel. The Forgotten Lighthouse uses words that become golden platforms.

In The Silent Theater Nicole says Alice knew her identity and told her to stay quiet at that first tea; she admits speaking to Alice's mind and says Alice complained of a headache afterward. In The Lost Palace she explains that angels gathered for her stories about humans. In The Forgotten Lighthouse she begins to explain things by going back to the first time the mages challenged the Anemo Archon, and hopes Alice never hears of her embarrassment.

232.comment: The Witch's Garden: Witch's Lodge hidden room
232.content:
After A Window Into the World, a bookcase in the lodge opens to a room that Nicole calls one of her fixed observation points for changes in the world, chosen for excellent visibility. She says the scene it shows exists only in her memories. She says she has no regrets about the price she paid for becoming human, yet remains an angel at heart.

Nicole mentions that if she kept her former form and power she would be bound by many more restrictions from the Heavenly Principles, including limits on what she may speak of. She says Teyvat's fate has been shaken more often recently. Her voice line when the platform is used with her as the active character begins with the words that observation is commencing.

233.comment: The Witch's Garden: Nicole and the Curatorium of Secrets
233.content: In Witch's Chatter Nicole says she would help a visitor who is willing to rely on their own effort. A person who expects magic to do all the work would be guided away to the nearby Curatorium of Secrets, where she says Nefer would know how to deal with them better than she would. She is clear that she would not turn them into a statue.

234.content:
Witch's Lodge (also: Mage's lodge, Nicole's lodge): The Witch's Lodge is a secret home of Nicole, an angel and member of the Hexenzirkel, tucked away in The Witch's Garden in Nod-Krai's Voidsea Outlook. Legend says it holds vast riches that only a mind as sharp as the witch's can find. The Traveler enters it room by room through Nicole's world quests.

Nicole says she builds several homes so that someone will eventually wander in by mistake. The first quest, Witch's Lodge (Version 6.3), has her tell a story in which she poses as "Nicola Coco, the Great Mage Everlasting", who keeps her secret home and needs a helper to build her territory. She then asks the Traveler for photos of finches, a squirrel and a mandragora as models for statues.

Geography: The lodge stands in The Witch's Garden, a point of interest in the Voidsea Outlook area at the southern end of Pohjola, north of Paha Isle. The exterior unlocks with the quest Witch's Lodge, and the interior after the quest The Joyous Floating Island. The garden's Meeting Point stands at the statue before the bridge.

The grounds are dotted with exquisite statues. In Nicole's story they are opponents turned to stone, but she then admits she was joking and says they are her way of capturing a moment in time.

Places: Rooms unlock one at a time: a tea room with a mandragora statue standing in for the Dodo-King, a study with a painting, a studio with an angel statue, a tall study with bookshelves and a typewriter, an upstairs room on the left of the entrance, and a hidden room on the right.

The tea room's statue is Nicole's stand-in for the Dodo-King in her tea-party game. The painting in the study shows a gathering Nicole misses, with candlesticks and a pot of tea left for the Dodocos. The studio angel statue prompts Nicole to say that the humans of today live comfortably, addressed to "sisters". In the tall study, Nicole misplaces a favorite book and a wind tunnel appears to help the player reach it; a chest of 200,000 Mora appears when it is found.

People: Nicole is its owner and appears in person during the quests, usually at the top of the stairs. She tells stories, jokes about being a "great mage" and takes the Traveler's help in building and carving. Paimon accompanies the Traveler throughout.

Alice of the Hexenzirkel borrowed the lodge key to set up a tea room, which Nicole mentions when the Traveler finds a large Seelie Court chair in the tea room during Witch's Homework: The Role of a Guide...?, a quest in which Barbeloth also appears.

Quests: The Witch's Lodge quest opens the series: after the photo task and a fight with an enraged mandragora, the Traveler carves a statue by following number clues that show how many blocks must stay in each row. The series Beyond Silver and Fine Gold then unlocks one room each week, after the previous one is fully explored, over about four weeks: The Joyous Floating Island, The Silent Theater, The Lost Palace and The Forgotten Lighthouse. A fifth quest, A Window Into the World, opens the hidden room.

Once a quest in the series is done and before the next unlocks, Nicole says she has no more chests to give and offers to scrape some together if the Traveler gives her a few hundred years. After A Window Into the World, she says the scenery in the hidden room exists only in her memories.

Atmosphere: Cozy, theatrical and full of storybook touches: statues, tea sets, cluttered shelves and Nicole's habit of narrating her life as a tale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lodge is a furnished retreat that Nicole shares with the Traveler; she may be away at other homes.

235.content: Nicola Coco, the Great Mage Everlasting, is the character in Nicole's story-in-progress who lives in a secret home, turns people into statues as a "joke" and needs a hero to build her territory. Nicole later reveals that the voice and the story were hers. She says a figure called Mr. Nine can refine the text later.

236.content: In the lodge, the Traveler and Paimon help Nicole carve statues from blocks. Numbers on the blocks show how many blocks in that row or column must stay; players use Trim Excess and Preserve Shape skills, and a squirrel statue rotates the model. This is a gameplay puzzle presented in-story as Nicole's craft lesson.
